paras.en: And find them I would.
paras.zh: 而我一定会找到他们。

paras.en: My ankle had recently healed.
paras.zh: 我的脚踝前不久好了。

paras.en: It just needed a little more time before it could bear the brunt of the long walk to the mist, and then I would go from this place.
paras.zh: 只差一点时间，就能扛住走去找迷雾的长路，到时我就离开这儿。

paras.en: I would travel back to the forest.
paras.zh: 我要回森林去。

paras.en: Find my family again.
paras.zh: 再找到我的家人。

paras.en: I stared out the tiny bedroom window, onto the cold afternoon streets.
paras.zh: 我望着小卧室窗外，冷清的午后街道。

paras.en: Light flakes of snow were falling from the sky, dusting the cobblestones below.
paras.zh: 细雪从天上飘落，给下面的鹅卵石铺上一层薄粉。

paras.en: Was winter here already?
paras.zh: 冬天已经来了吗？

paras.en: It was easier to lose track of the days shut up inside a wooden box.
paras.zh: 关在木头盒子里，日子更容易数不清。

paras.en: But I knew soon it would come, blanketing the world in white, the chill creeping into our bones.
paras.zh: 可我知道它快来了，会把世界盖成白茫茫，寒气钻进骨头。

paras.en: Back home, we’d all huddle by the fire on cold winter days, cozy under mountains of reindeer hides, cuddling close to keep each other warm.
paras.zh: 在家里，寒冬里我们都挤在火边，裹在成堆的驯鹿皮下，依偎着互相取暖。

paras.en: There would be stories.
paras.zh: 会有故事。

paras.en: Songs.
paras.zh: 会有歌。

paras.en: I missed the songs most of all.
paras.zh: 我最想念的，是那些歌。

paras.en: I opened my mouth to sing.
paras.zh: 我张口想唱。

paras.en: My mother’s song.
paras.zh: 母亲的歌。

paras.en: A song of Ahtohallan, a magical river of memories.
paras.zh: 一支关于阿图哈兰的歌，那条记忆的魔法之河。

paras.en: Only Ahtohallan knows, A fierce longing rose inside me.
paras.zh: 只有阿图哈兰知道，一股强烈的渴望在我心底升起。

paras.en: Did Ahtohallan know what had happened the day of the dam celebration?
paras.zh: 阿图哈兰可知道大坝庆典那天发生了什么？

paras.en: I wished I knew how to find her, to ask her.
paras.zh: 我真希望知道怎么找到她、去问问她。

paras.en: But she was very far away.
paras.zh: 可她太远了。

paras.en: Too far for a young girl like you to go, A sob rose to my throat.
paras.zh: 远得不是你这样的小姑娘能去的，一声呜咽涌上我的喉咙。

paras.en: I missed them all so much.
paras.zh: 我好想他们每一个人。

paras.en: Would I ever see them again? “Are you all right?” I whirled at the sound of the voice and, to my shock, stood face to face with none other than the boy I had saved in the woods.
paras.zh: 我还能再见到他们吗？“你还好吗？”听见这声音我猛地转身，震惊地发现，站在我面前的竟是我在林中救下的那个男孩。

paras.en: Agnarr.
paras.zh: 安格瑞。

paras.en: I stared at him, disbelieving.
paras.zh: 我难以置信地盯着他。

paras.en: He was dressed in a sharp red suit with a matching tie, and his blond hair was cropped close to his head.
paras.zh: 他穿着笔挺的红西装，配同色领带，金发也剪得紧贴头皮。

paras.en: They must have shaved it to work on his wound.
paras.zh: 准是为了处理伤口才剃的。

paras.en: It made him look older and his leaf-green eyes even bigger.
paras.zh: 这让他显得成熟了些，叶绿色的眼睛显得更大。

paras.en: I felt my face turn as red as his suit.
paras.zh: 我觉得自己的脸涨得和他西装一样红。

paras.en: What was he doing here?
paras.zh: 他来这儿干什么？

paras.en: He couldn’t be one of the orphans, not in that outfit.
paras.zh: 他穿成这样，不可能是孤儿。

paras.en: Had he come here from the village to thank me for my rescue?
paras.zh: 他是从村里来，为救他之事道谢的？

paras.en: Did he even remember?
paras.zh: 他还会记得吗？

paras.en: I scanned his face for recognition but saw none.
paras.zh: 我在他脸上寻找认出我的神色，却什么也没看到。

paras.en: I thought back to that moment in the wagon, when he’d slipped his hand in mine.
paras.zh: 我想起马车里那一刻，他把我的手握进他手心。

paras.en: But he’d been so out of it.
paras.zh: 可那时他那么不清醒。

paras.en: He probably didn’t remember.
paras.zh: 他大概不记得了。

paras.en: I could never forget.
paras.zh: 我却永远忘不了。

paras.en: He backed away, catching the look on my face. “S-sorry,” he stammered. “I didn’t mean to intrude.
paras.zh: 他退后半步，捕捉到我脸上的神情。“对、对不起，”他结巴了。“我不是有意打扰。

paras.en: I just heard you singing, and…What was that song?” I wasn’t sure what to say. “Just something my mother used to sing to me,” I confessed at last, though I wasn’t certain this was wise to admit.
paras.zh: 我刚听见你在唱歌，然后……那是什么歌？”我不知该说什么。“就是我母亲以前唱给我听的，”我终于坦白，尽管不确定承认这个是否明智。

paras.en: It was a Northuldra song, after all.
paras.zh: 毕竟，那是北地人的歌。

paras.en: Still, something in his face told me I could trust him.
paras.zh: 可他脸上的某种神情告诉我，我可以信他。

paras.en: At least a little. “That’s nice,” Agnarr said, sounding suddenly wistful. “I barely knew my mother.
paras.zh: 至少信一点点。“那真好，”安格瑞忽然有些怅然。“我几乎不了解我母亲。

paras.en: She left when I was a small child.
paras.zh: 我很小的时候她就走了。

paras.en: And let’s just say Father wasn’t exactly the lullaby type.” He gave a bitter laugh. “You know how kings are.” My pulse jumped.
paras.zh: 而且嘛，父亲可不是会唱摇篮曲的那种。”他苦笑一声。“你懂国王是怎么回事。”我的脉搏一跳。

paras.en: His father, a king?
paras.zh: 他父亲是国王？

paras.en: But that would make him… “There you are, Prince Agnarr.
paras.zh: 那他岂不是……“你在这儿啊，安格瑞王子。

paras.en: I was wondering where you’d wandered off to.” A deep baritone rang out as Lord Peterssen stepped into the room.
paras.zh: 我还在想你溜哪儿去了呢。”一个低沉的男中音响起，彼得森大人走进房间。

paras.en: His eyes settled on me and he gave me a friendly smile. “Oh, good.
paras.zh: 他的目光落在我身上，友好地一笑。“哦，好。

paras.en: You’ve already become acquainted.
paras.zh: 你们已经认识了。

paras.en: I hope Agnarr has been minding his manners,” he added, poking Agnarr in the ribs.
paras.zh: 希望安格瑞还懂点规矩，”他补充道，戳了戳安格瑞的肋骨。

paras.en: Agnarr playfully shoved him back. “I am nothing if not the picture of decorum and grace!” he declared haughtily, but with a tease in his tone.
paras.zh: 安格瑞顽皮地把他推回去。“我要是少了体面与优雅，那还算什么！”他傲慢地宣布，语气里却带着戏谑。

paras.en: Lord Peterssen snorted in disbelief.
paras.zh: 彼得森大人嗤之以鼻，不信。

paras.en: Meanwhile, I was staring at the two of them, my mind racing so fast I could barely put a thought together.
paras.zh: meanwhile，我盯着他们俩，脑子转得太快，几乎连不成一个念头。

paras.en: Agnarr, the boy I rescued.
paras.zh: 安格瑞，我救下的男孩。

paras.en: He was a prince?
paras.zh: 他是个王子？

paras.en: The heir to the throne of Arendelle?
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔王位的继承人？

paras.en: I’d rescued the prince of Arendelle. “Your—Your Majesty,” I stammered, dropping to my knees as I desperately tried to recall from the Arendellian fairy tales I’d read how the common people greeted royals, hoping I was doing it right.
paras.zh: 我救的竟是阿伦黛尔的王子。“陛、陛下，”我结巴着跪下，拼命回想读过的阿伦黛尔童话里平民如何向王室行礼，希望自己没做错。

paras.en: Only, it seemed I had gotten it wrong.
paras.zh: 只可惜，我好像搞错了。

paras.en: Agnarr shook his head, his cheeks coloring. “Oh, stop,” he mumbled. “You don’t need to do that.” “Sorry.” I scrambled to my feet, my face burning with shame. “I don’t…I mean…I didn’t…” The prince stepped forward, holding out his hand.
paras.zh: 安格瑞摇头，两颊泛红。“噢，快别，”他嘟囔。“你不必这样。”“抱歉。”我慌忙起身，羞得脸发烫。“我……我是说……我没……”王子上前一步，伸出手。

paras.en: I reached for it hesitantly, trying to pretend it was the first time we’d touched. “Name’s Agnarr,” he said. “It’s very nice to meet you.” “I’m…Iduna,” I said.
paras.zh: 我迟疑地握住，假装这是我们第一次触碰。“我叫安格瑞，”他说。“很高兴认识你。”“我……伊杜娜，”我说。

paras.en: Then I squared my shoulders and lifted my chin, acting as if I met princes all the time and it was really no big deal. “It’s…nice to meet you, too.” He gave a perfunctory nod, all business now.
paras.zh: 然后我挺起肩膀、抬起下巴，装作常常见王子、这没什么大不了。“也……很高兴认识你。”他敷衍地点点头，此刻公事公办起来。

paras.en: He was no longer an injured boy but the heir apparent. “I hope they are treating you well here at the orphanage,” he continued. “I know it’s a little crowded right now.
paras.zh: 他不再是那个受伤的男孩，而是王储了。“我希望孤儿院这里待你不薄，”他接着说。“我知道现在是有点挤。

paras.en: Many lost parents during the battle of the Enchanted Forest—myself included.
paras.zh: 魔法森林一战中，许多人失去了父母——我也包括在内。

paras.en: But we’re doing our best to care for everyone.
paras.zh: 但我们正尽全力照顾每一个人。

paras.en: Peterssen and I have asked the council to allocate additional funds for an expansion to the building.
paras.zh: 彼得森和我已请议会拨出额外款项，扩建这栋楼。

paras.en: Along with extra food.
paras.zh: 还有额外的食物。

paras.en: And chocolate,” he added with a grin. “That was my idea.” I thought back to the tiny square of chocolate he’d slipped me in the wagon. “A very good idea,” I agreed. “Chocolate makes everything better.” He looked surprised as I parroted his words back to him.
paras.zh: 还有巧克力，”他咧嘴补了一句。“这主意是我出的。”我想起他在马车上塞给我的那小块巧克力。“很好的主意，”我赞同。“巧克力能让一切变好。”我把他的话学舌回去，他显得有些惊讶。

paras.en: His brows creased as if he was trying to remember.
paras.zh: 他皱起眉，像在努力回想。

paras.en: Then he grinned. “I think you and I are going to get along very well.” Peterssen clapped his hands. “Great.
paras.zh: 接着他咧嘴一笑。“我觉得你我会相处得很好。”彼得森拍手。“太好了。

paras.en: Now that introductions have been made, it’s time to head back to the castle.
paras.zh: 既然介绍过了，也该回城堡了。

paras.en: If you’re ready, Iduna?” I stared at Lord Peterssen in shock, unable to fully comprehend what he was saying. “You want me to come to the castle?” “Yes, of course,” he said in a voice that left no room for argument. “I said I’d take care of you, didn’t I?
paras.zh: 你要是准备好了，伊杜娜？”我震惊地盯着彼得森大人，一时没法完全明白他的话。“你要我进城堡？”“当然，没错，”他用不容置疑的口气说。“我说过会照顾你，不是吗？

paras.en: Well, I apologize it’s taken some time to get organized.
paras.zh: 唉，抱歉拖了这么久才安排好。

paras.en: Things have been—tumultuous the past few weeks, as you can imagine.
paras.zh: 这几周——就如你能想见的，乱成一团。

paras.en: Transitions of power, all that sort of thing.” He waved a hand. “But now that the dust is settled, I have returned to keep my promise.
paras.zh: 权力交接，诸如此类。”他摆摆手。“不过如今尘埃落定，我回来兑现承诺了。

paras.en: You’ll still live here, of course.
paras.zh: 你当然还住这儿。

paras.en: But you will also start daily educational lessons at the castle.
paras.zh: 但你也将在城堡开始每日的课业。

paras.en: Agnarr’s own tutor, Miss Larsen, will teach you.
paras.zh: 安格瑞自己的家庭教师拉森小姐会教你。

paras.en: It’s the very least that we could do for the sacrifices your parents made.” I stared at him, fear rising inside me.
paras.zh: 为你父母的牺牲，这是我们至少能做的。”我盯着他，心里升起恐惧。

paras.en: The castle?
paras.zh: 城堡？

paras.en: They wanted me to go to the castle?
paras.zh: 他们要我进城堡？

paras.en: On a daily basis?
paras.zh: 天天去？

paras.en: Were they joking?
paras.zh: 他们在开玩笑吗？

paras.en: If anyone learned who I was… “I—I don’t think I can…” I stammered. “You can I started to open my mouth, probably to argue again.
paras.zh: 要是有人知道我是谁……“我、我觉得我不行……”我结巴。“你能……”我张开嘴，大概又要争辩。

paras.en: But at that moment, the orphan children from earlier stormed back into the bedroom.
paras.zh: 可就在这时，先前那两个孤儿冲回了寝室。

paras.en: Now it was the boy playing the part of the “evil Northuldra,” coming after the squealing girl with a mad look in his eyes. “I’m going to kill you!” he cried. “Like I killed the king!” Agnarr’s face turned stark white.
paras.zh: 这回是男孩扮“邪恶北地人”，眼里冒着火追着尖叫的女孩。“我要杀了你！”他喊。“就像我杀了国王那样！”安格瑞的脸一下子惨白。

paras.en: My heart panged as I caught the anguish swimming in his green eyes.
paras.zh: 我心头一痛，捕捉到他绿眼里翻涌的痛苦。

paras.en: He might have been the prince, but he was also a boy who had lost his father.
paras.zh: 他也许是王子，可他也是个失去父亲的男孩。

paras.en: Perhaps Peterssen would have stepped in and said something, but I beat him to it.
paras.zh: 彼得森本要上前说点什么，却被我抢了先。

paras.en: The children dove back on my bed, wrestling one another, still shouting about magic and treachery.
paras.zh: 孩子们又扑回我的床，互相扭打，还在喊着魔法和背叛。

paras.en: I marched over to “Magic?” I broke in with an exaggeratedly jovial tone. “Please.
paras.zh: 我走过去，“魔法？”我用夸张的欢快语气插嘴。“得了吧。

paras.en: Who needs magic when you have super tickle powers?” Without warning, I pounced, grabbing them and tickling them under their arms.
paras.zh: 有超级挠痒功在，谁还需要魔法？”我毫无预兆地扑上去，抓住他们，挠他们的胳肢窝。

paras.en: They squealed in protest, trying to wiggle away as they begged for mercy, not unlike the Northuldra children back home.
paras.zh: 他们尖叫着抗议，扭着身子想挣脱、讨饶，和我们家乡的北地孩子没什么两样。

paras.en: Tickle torture, it seemed, was universal. “Let us go!” cried the boy. “Please!” “We have chores to do!” the girl giggled, swatting my hands away. “Chores?” I repeated in as innocent a voice as I could muster.
paras.zh: 挠痒酷刑，看来是全人类通用的。“放我们走！”男孩喊。“求你了！”“我们还有活儿要干！”女孩咯咯笑着拍开我的手。“活儿？”我用尽量天真的声音重复。

paras.en: I released them, rising back to my feet. “Why didn’t you say so?
paras.zh: 我放开他们，站起身。“你怎么不早说？

paras.en: I’d certainly never want to keep you from chores “Yes, chores!” the girl agreed, a look of relief on her face. “Come on, Peter.
paras.zh: 我当然不愿耽误你们干活——”“对，干活！”女孩如释重负地应和。“走吧，彼得。

paras.en: Let’s go do our chores!” They leapt from the bed, nearly knocking Agnarr over as they fled for the stairs.
paras.zh: 我们去干活！”他们从床上蹦下，逃向楼梯时差点撞翻安格瑞。

paras.en: He watched them go, his face still pale.
paras.zh: 他望着他们跑掉，脸色仍然苍白。

paras.en: But then he turned to me.
paras.zh: 可接着他转向我。

paras.en: And he smiled.
paras.zh: 他笑了。

paras.en: It was a smile so bright it seemed to light up the entire room.
paras.zh: 那笑容亮得仿佛照亮了整个房间。

paras.en: Peterssen stood behind Agnarr, nodding his approval at how I’d handled the situation.
paras.zh: 彼得森站在安格瑞身后，对我处理这局面的方式颔首赞许。

paras.en: I smiled back shyly at the prince. “Let me get my coat.”
paras.zh: 我羞涩地朝王子回笑。“我去拿外套。”

paras.en: “AND THIS IS MY GREAT-GREAT-GREAT-grandfather Eric.
paras.zh: “这位是我高高大祖父埃里克。

paras.en: Will you look at that mustache?
paras.zh: 你瞧瞧那胡子？

paras.en: Talk about hair goals!
paras.zh: 那才叫胡子界的标杆！

paras.en: And over here—that’s Great-Grandmother Else.
paras.zh: 这边这位——是高祖母埃尔瑟。

paras.en: I always thought she looked like a nice lady.
paras.zh: 我一直觉得她是个和善的女士。

paras.en: The kind who sneaks her grandchildren cookies when their parents aren’t looking.” I glanced over at Iduna, who was staring up at the paintings in my family’s portrait room, a polite but otherwise unreadable expression on her face.
paras.zh: 就是那种趁父母不注意、偷偷给孙辈塞饼干的那种。”我瞥了眼伊杜娜，她正仰头望着我家肖像室里的画像，脸上挂着礼貌却读不出情绪的表情。

paras.en: Was I boring her?
paras.zh: 我是不是把她讲烦了？

paras.en: Was I talking too much?
paras.zh: 我是不是话太多了？

paras.en: I was probably talking too much.
paras.zh: 我大概是话太多了。

paras.en: But who could blame me?
paras.zh: 可这能怪谁呢？

paras.en: After the dam tragedy, they’d all but shut the castle gates, with only essential staff remaining inside.
paras.zh: 大坝惨剧之后，城堡大门几乎全关了，只留必要的仆人在内。

paras.en: And Lord Peterssen hadn’t been so keen on letting me run around the village unescorted, declaring it was way too dangerous under our current political climate.
paras.zh: 彼得森大人也不大乐意让我没人陪就满村跑，说以眼下这政治气候太危险。

paras.en: When a king died, a kingdom could go through a period of unrest.
paras.zh: 国王一死，王国可能要经历一段动荡。

paras.en: Neighboring countries could start sniffing around, looking for weakness.
paras.zh: 邻国可能开始嗅探，寻找弱点。

paras.en: Even within the kingdom, some ambitious great-nephew or -niece of the former king might start getting delusions of grandeur and decide they had some kind of claim to the throne.
paras.zh: 即便在王国之内，前国王某个野心勃勃的侄孙或侄孙女，也可能做起黄粱美梦，觉得自己对王位有某种主张。

paras.en: If only that pesky son of the king weren’t in the And that didn’t even count the Northuldra, who had become public enemy number one in Arendelle.
paras.zh: 要是国王那个讨人嫌的儿子不在……这还没算上北地人——他们已成了阿伦黛尔的头号公敌。

paras.en: What if they were, even now, people whispered, gathering their forces and preparing to lead an attack on our kingdom—to finish what was started back on their land?
paras.zh: 万一他们，就在此刻，有人窃窃私语，正集结兵力、准备进攻我们的王国——来完成他们在本土开启的未竟之事呢？

paras.en: It all sounded completely far-fetched to me, but as Peterssen always said, better to be safe than dead.
paras.zh: 这些在我听来全是无稽之谈，但正如彼得森常说的，宁可安全，不要送命。

paras.en: Until all potential threats had been uncovered, I was to remain inside the castle gates and only be allowed to leave when escorted by a full company of guards.
paras.zh: 在一切潜在威胁查明之前，我得待在城堡门内，只有在一整队卫兵护送时才准离开。

paras.en: Which meant I had been climbing the walls the past few weeks.
paras.zh: 也就是说，这几周我快把墙皮都爬破了。

paras.en: Utterly bored and alone.
paras.zh: 无聊透顶，孤零零的。

paras.en: Now, for the first time in forever, I had someone to talk to.
paras.zh: 而现在，破天荒第一次，我有了能说话的人。

paras.en: Of course, it didn’t hurt that this someone had the shiniest pile of hair I had ever seen and eyes like the sky on a cloudless winter’s day.
paras.zh: 当然，这人拥有一头我见过最亮泽的头发、一双像无云冬日的天空般的眼睛，这也不算坏事。

paras.en: Not that that mattered or anything.
paras.zh: 又不是那有什么要紧。

paras.en: It was just a fact.
paras.zh: 只是个事实罢了。

paras.en: I shook off that last thought and grinned at Iduna, hoping it came off as a nice grin and not slightly deranged.
paras.zh: 我把那个念头甩开，冲伊杜娜咧嘴一笑，希望看起来是友善的笑，而不是有点疯。

paras.en: She hadn’t said much since she got here, her face unreadable but definitely tensed, with eyes darting around each room we entered as if assessing it for potential danger.
paras.zh: 她来了之后话不多，脸上看不出情绪却明显绷着，每进一间房眼睛都四下扫视，像在评估潜在危险。

paras.en: It made sense: after all, it had only been a month since she’d lost her parents in an unexpected battle.
paras.zh: 这说得通：毕竟，她在一个突如其来的战斗里失去父母，才过了一个月。

paras.en: It was hard to feel safe after going through something like that.
paras.zh: 这很难感到安全。

paras.en: I knew from experience.
paras.zh: 这点我深有体会。

paras.en: Ooh!
paras.zh: 噢！

paras.en: I should show her the library.
paras.zh: 我该带她看看藏书室。

paras.en: But no one could stop me from reading about them.
paras.zh: 不过谁也拦不住我读关于它们的书。

paras.en: People always assumed being prince was such a glamorous thing.
paras.zh: 人们总以为当王子是件光鲜的事。

paras.en: But in a way, it was like being a prisoner.
paras.zh: 可某种程度上，它像坐牢。

paras.en: My responsibility to my kingdom always had to come first over my Like now, after my father’s death.
paras.zh: 我对王国的责任，总得排在个人前头……就像现在，父亲死后。

paras.en: It would be years before Arendelle fully recovered.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔要好些年才能完全恢复。

paras.en: At least that’s what the council said, during our latest meeting.
paras.zh: 至少议会是这么说的，在最近一次会议上。

paras.en: Peterssen was a competent leader, but he wasn’t a king.
paras.zh: 彼得森是个能干的领袖，但他不是国王。

paras.en: And our armies had been depleted from the battle in the Enchanted Forest, leaving us vulnerable.
paras.zh: 而我们的大军在魔法森林一战中损耗殆尽，让我们变得脆弱。

paras.en: The council believed we should reach out to other kingdoms for assistance; the kingdom of Vassar, for example, had a great army.
paras.zh: 议会认为我们该向其他王国求援；比如瓦萨尔王国，就有一支强大的军队。

paras.en: Perhaps they could be convinced to lend us aid if we ever needed it.
paras.zh: 也许能说动他们在我们需要时施以援手。

paras.en: At least that’s what members of the council argued for over an hour and a half at the meeting.
paras.zh: 至少那是议会成员在会上争了一个半小时的观点。

paras.en: Which had been so mind-numbingly dull I had almost fallen asleep three times.
paras.zh: 那过程无聊到让我差点睡着三回。

paras.en: Who would have thought being a great leader would be so boring?
paras.zh: 谁想得到，当个伟大的领袖会这么无聊？

paras.en: But now—now I had Iduna.
paras.zh: 可现在——现在我有了伊杜娜。

paras.en: I grabbed her hand. “Come on!” I said. “I’ve got something amazing to show you.” Her eyes widened at the grip of my hand on hers, but after a moment she let me lead her. “Ta-da!” I cried as I threw open the library doors.
paras.zh: 我抓住她的手。“来！”我说。“有样绝妙的东西给你看。”她被我握着手，眼睛睁大了，但片刻后任由我领着。“噔噔！”我推开藏书室的门，喊道。

paras.en: For a moment, Iduna said nothing, her mouth just sort of dropping open. “Do you like it?” I asked.
paras.zh: 有那么一会儿，伊杜娜一言不发，嘴巴就那么张着。“你喜欢吗？”我问。

paras.en: She walked into the room, sinking down onto a nearby padded stool. “These are all…your books?” she asked, her blue eyes wide as they took in the towering shelves. “All of them?” When I nodded in response, her eyes inexplicably filled with tears.
paras.zh: 她走进房间，在一张就近的软凳上坐下。“这些……全都是你的书？”她问，蓝眼睛睁得大大的，打量着高耸的书架。“全部？”我一点头，她的眼里无缘无故盈满泪水。

paras.en: It wasn’t quite the reaction I had been hoping for. “Iduna, what is it?” I asked.
paras.zh: 这反应可不是我期待的。“伊杜娜，怎么了？”我问。

paras.en: Her eyes darted in all directions, looking everywhere but at me. “My…mother, she would have loved this room,” she whispered at last. “She had a book.
paras.zh: 她的眼睛四处乱瞟，看哪都行就是不看我。“我……母亲，她一定会喜欢这房间，”她终于低语。“她有一本书。

paras.en: She used it to teach me to read.” Her voice sounded soft and far away and sad.
paras.zh: 她用它教我认字。”她的声音轻柔、飘远，又带着哀伤。

paras.en: Of course.
paras.zh: 当然。

paras.en: What a dunce I could be!
paras.zh: 我真是个蠢材！

paras.en: I dropped to my knees in front of her. “I’m sorry,” I said, trying to make her meet my I groaned inwardly at my attempt at an apology.
paras.zh: 我在她面前单膝跪下。“对不起，”我说，想让她看我……我这道歉的尝试，让我在心里直叹气。

paras.en: Seriously, Agnarr?
paras.zh: 说真的，安格瑞？

paras.en: You are the worst.
paras.zh: 你真是最差劲的。

paras.en: You’re supposed to be trying to cheer her up.
paras.zh: 你本该想办法让她高兴的。

paras.en: Instead you’ve made her cry. “We don’t have to look at these,” I added quickly, jumping back to my feet. “They’re kind of musty anyway.
paras.zh: 结果你倒把她弄哭了。“我们不必看这些，”我连忙补充，跳回脚。“再说它们也有点发霉。

paras.en: Want to see the kitchen?
paras.zh: 想看看厨房吗？

paras.en: I bet Olina has finished up the desserts for tonight’s banquet.
paras.zh: 我打赌奥丽娜已经做好了今晚宴会的甜点。

paras.en: And I’m really good at distracting her for an advanced taste test.” She gave me a wan smile. “Maybe later,” she said. “I’m not that hungry right now.” Argh.
paras.zh: 而且我特别擅长引开她，好提前尝一口。”她给了我一个淡淡的笑。“也许晚点吧，”她说。“我现在不太饿。”哎。

paras.en: She rose to her feet, walking over to the large, circular wooden table in the center of the room, stopping in front of it and looking down.
paras.zh: 她站起身，走到房间中央那张圆形大木桌前，停在桌边低头看。

paras.en: Too late I realized there were full-on blueprints of the dam my father had built, spread across its surface.
paras.zh: 我太迟才意识到，桌上摊着我父亲修的大坝的完整蓝图。

paras.en: The plans that had started this whole thing, drawn up long before I was born, when my father and his people had first arrived in Arendelle.
paras.zh: 就是这份引发这一切的图，早在我出生前、父亲和他的人初到阿伦黛尔时就画好了。

paras.en: She traced a hand over the paper. “What do you think happened that day?” she asked, in a voice so soft I could barely hear her.
paras.zh: 她的手抚过图纸。“你觉得那天发生了什么？”她问，声音轻得我几乎听不见。

paras.en: I stepped closer, staring down at the plans. “I don’t know,” I said after a minute. “It started out as such a perfect day.
paras.zh: 我走近，低头盯着图纸。“我不知道，”过了一会儿我说。“开头本是那么完美的一天。

paras.en: The Enchanted Forest was so beautiful.
paras.zh: 魔法森林那么美。

paras.en: Everyone was having fun.
paras.zh: 人人都玩得开心。

paras.en: Laughing, joking.
paras.zh: 笑着，闹着。

paras.en: And then…they weren’t.” I swallowed hard as memories of the day came raging back at me.
paras.zh: 然后……就不是了。”我用力咽下，那天的记忆猛地涌回。

paras.en: The stench of smoke.
paras.zh: 烟的臭味。

paras.en: Swords clashing.
paras.zh: 刀剑相击。

paras.en: People screaming.
paras.zh: 人的尖叫。

paras.en: Wind blowing.
paras.zh: 风在吹。

paras.en: My father tumbling to his death. “Do you think the Northuldra betrayed us?” she asked It was, of course, the same question everyone had been asking since that fateful day.
paras.zh: 我父亲坠亡。“你觉得北地人背叛了我们吗？”她问……这当然是从那命中之日以来，人人都在问的问题。

paras.en: But somehow it sounded different coming from her mouth.
paras.zh: 可不知怎的，从她嘴里问出来，听起来不一样。

paras.en: Mostly because she was the first one who sounded like she really wanted an answer, instead of using the question as a preamble to rant on about the Northuldra and their vile magic. “I don’t know,” I said at last, keeping my voice low so no one could accidentally hear us if they walked past.
paras.zh: 多半因为她是第一个听起来真想要答案的人，而不是拿这问题当开场白、好去痛骂北地人和他们邪恶的魔法。“我不知道，”我终于说，压低声音，免得有人路过无意听见。

paras.en: I was the crown prince of Arendelle, after all.
paras.zh: 毕竟，我是阿伦黛尔的王储。

paras.en: Which meant I needed to side with my people, no matter what.
paras.zh: 这意味着我无论如何都得站在我的人民一边。

paras.en: And I did believe in them.
paras.zh: 而我也确实信他们。

paras.en: Arendelle was a good kingdom.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔是个好王国。

paras.en: People were kind to their neighbors.
paras.zh: 百姓对邻人友善。

paras.en: They helped others in need.
paras.zh: 他们帮助有难的人。

paras.en: But still, it didn’t make sense to me.
paras.zh: 可这仍让我想不通。

paras.en: Why would the Northuldra attack us after we gave them such a gift?
paras.zh: 我们给了他们那么大的礼物，北地人为什么要攻击我们？

paras.en: But then, why would we attack them?
paras.zh: 可话说回来，我们又为什么要攻击他们？

paras.en: Iduna looked up at me and I realized her eyes were brimming with tears again. “Has anyone gone back?” she asked, her voice wobbly. “To see what’s left?
paras.zh: 伊杜娜抬头看我，我发觉她眼里又盈满泪水。“有人回去过吗？”她声音发颤。“去看看还剩什么？

paras.en: Who survived?
paras.zh: 谁还活着？

paras.en: Are the Northuldra destroyed?” Oh!
paras.zh: 北地人全灭了吗？”噢！

paras.en: My eyes widened.
paras.zh: 我睁大了眼。

paras.en: She didn’t know!
paras.zh: 她不知道！

paras.en: Of course she didn’t.
paras.zh: 她当然不知道。

paras.en: No one outside the castle had any idea.
paras.zh: 城堡外没人知道。

paras.en: They were already too riled up, even without knowing about the magical mist; Lord Peterssen hadn’t wanted to cause a panic.
paras.zh: 即便不知那魔法迷雾，他们已经够激愤了；彼得森大人本就不想引起恐慌。

paras.en: I gestured for her to follow me.
paras.zh: 我示意她跟我来。

paras.en: We couldn’t talk about something this important here, in the center of the castle.
paras.zh: 这么重要的事，不能在城堡中心谈。

paras.en: There were too many eyes and ears, lurking around every corner.
paras.zh: 每个角落都藏着太多眼睛和耳朵。

paras.en: It would be safer to talk in the courtyard garden, despite the cold.
paras.zh: 去院子花园谈更安全，尽管冷。

paras.en: Hardly anyone ever went out there these days, especially since Peterssen had put the gardeners on leave when closing up the castle.
paras.zh: 近来几乎没人去那儿，尤其彼得森关闭城堡后让园丁放了假。

paras.en: We stepped outside, into the courtyard.
paras.zh: 我们走到外面，进了庭院。

paras.en: Everything was gnarled and barren in the throes of winter.
paras.zh: 深冬里，一切都扭曲而荒芜。

paras.en: But I ignored it all, leading Iduna straight to my favorite tree.
paras.zh: 可我不管这些，径直把伊杜娜领到我那棵最爱的树前。

paras.en: My reading tree, I’d dubbed it, since I’d spent so much time from a young age sitting “Do you want to sit—?” I started to ask.
paras.zh: 我管它叫“我的读书树”，因为从小我就常坐在……“你想坐下——？”我开口问。

paras.en: But to my surprise, she had already swung herself into the tree itself, easily pulling herself up by her hands to reach the higher branches.
paras.zh: 可出乎我意料，她已经荡身进了树里，双手一撑就轻松攀上了更高的枝丫。

paras.en: I watched, mesmerized for a moment by her graceful, catlike movements, then decided to join her, hoisting myself up—albeit far more clumsily—onto one of the lower branches.
paras.zh: 我看着，一时被她优雅如猫的动作迷住，然后决定也上去，把自己——虽说笨拙得多——撑到一根较低的树枝上。

paras.en: A moment later, she crawled back down to my level, settling herself gracefully on a nearby branch.
paras.zh: 片刻后，她爬回我这一层，优雅地在一根近旁树枝上坐定。

paras.en: It was as if she were a bird that had lived in trees all her life.
paras.zh: 她就像一只在树上活了一辈子的鸟。

paras.en: She leaned toward me expectantly. “So, what is it?” she prompted.
paras.zh: 她带着期待倾身向我。“那么，是什么？”她催促道。

paras.en: I bit my lower lip. “Look, you have to keep this quiet, okay?
paras.zh: 我咬住下唇。“听着，这件事你得保密，好吗？

paras.en: They aren’t telling everyone the truth.
paras.zh: 他们没对所有人说真话。

paras.en: They’re too afraid it’ll cause a panic.” “What will?” “The Enchanted Forest.
paras.zh: 他们太怕会引起恐慌了。”“什么会？”“魔法森林。

paras.en: It’s…covered in mist.” Her eyes widened.
paras.zh: 它……被迷雾罩住了。”她的眼睛睁大了。

paras.en: But strangely she didn’t look surprised. “They say it’s magical,” I added. “Like, it totally looks as if you could walk through it, but you can’t.
paras.zh: 可奇怪的是，她并不显得惊讶。“据说那是魔法，”我补充。“就是说，它看着完全像能走过去，可你走不过去。

paras.en: And if you try, it bounces you back.
paras.zh: 你要试，它会把你弹回来。

paras.en: No one can get in.
paras.zh: 没人进得去。

paras.en: And…well, I’m guessing no one can get out, either.” She plucked a twig from a branch, folding it in her hand.
paras.zh: 而且……嗯，我猜也没人出得来。”她从枝上折下一小段嫩枝，在手里折着。

paras.en: Her face had gone pale. “So you think people are still in there?
paras.zh: 她的脸白了。“所以你觉得里面还有人？

paras.en: Alive?” she asked.
paras.zh: 还活着？”她问。

paras.en: Suddenly I realized why she was so interested.
paras.zh: 忽然我明白了她为何这么关心。

paras.en: Lord Peterssen said her parents had been killed in the battle.
paras.zh: 彼得森大人说她父母死在了战斗中。

paras.en: But what if they hadn’t been?
paras.zh: 可万一他们没死呢？

paras.en: What if they were trapped in the mist?
paras.zh: 万一他们被困在迷雾里呢？

paras.en: Like I hoped Lieutenant Mattias was. “I don’t know,” I admitted. “But I think there’s a chance.
paras.zh: 就像我希望马蒂亚斯中尉那样。“我不知道，”我承认。“但我想有这个可能。

paras.en: Not that it matters.
paras.zh: 虽说这也无关紧要。

paras.en: Unless the mist lifts someday, we’ll never know what’s within it.
paras.zh: 除非哪天迷雾散去，我们永远无从知晓里面是什么。

paras.en: All we can do is hope that—” “I want to see.” I blinked at her, not understanding what she meant. “The mist,” she clarified at my bemused expression. “Do you know where it is?
paras.zh: 我们能做的只有希望——”“我想去看看。”我冲她眨眨眼，不明白她的意思。“那迷雾，”见我困惑，她澄清。“你知道它在哪儿吗？

paras.en: Can you take me there?” Her blue eyes flashed with inner fire.
paras.zh: 能带我去吗？”她的蓝眼里闪着内心的火。

paras.en: I shook my head. “It’s not that easy.
paras.zh: 我摇头。“没那么容易。

paras.en: For one thing, it’s really far away.
paras.zh: 一来，它实在很远。

paras.en: Like over a day’s journey.
paras.zh: 要走一天多。

paras.en: And Lord Peterssen and the soldiers would never let us go.
paras.zh: 二来彼得森大人和士兵绝不会放我们走。

paras.en: We’re only kids.
paras.zh: 我们只是孩子。

paras.en: It’s far too dangerous.” The expression on her face was so fierce that a shiver ran through me that had nothing to do with the biting cold. “I must see it,” she declared. “We can leave tonight.” I stared at her, incredulous.
paras.zh: 太危险了。”她脸上的神情那么决绝，一阵战栗穿过我身——与刺骨的寒冷无关。“我必须去看，”她宣告。“我们今晚就走。”我难以置信地盯着她。

paras.en: Who was And, unfortunately, I couldn’t join her. “I’m sorry.
paras.zh: 她是谁……而不巧的是，我没法跟她去。“对不起。

paras.en: I can’t.
paras.zh: 我不行。

paras.en: Not that I don’t want to,” I added quickly, after catching a flash of frustration on her face. “It’s just that they watch me all the time; they even guard my bedroom while I sleep.
paras.zh: 不是我不想去，”见她脸上掠过一丝挫败，我连忙补充。“只是他们时刻盯着我；连我睡觉都有人守着卧室。

paras.en: I can barely go to Blodget’s Bakery for cookies without a full-on army in tow.” She nodded slowly, then dropped fluidly out of the tree.
paras.zh: 我去趟布洛杰特面包店买饼干，都得一整支军队跟着。”她缓缓点头，然后灵活地跃下树。

paras.en: I stared down at her through the branches, feeling my heart ache unexpectedly as I caught her slumped shoulders and bowed head.
paras.zh: 我隔着枝丫低头看她，捕捉到她耷拉的肩膀和低垂的头，心忽然莫名地疼。

paras.en: I’d disappointed her, this girl who had already lost everything.
paras.zh: 我让她失望了，这个已经失去一切的女孩。

paras.en: But something about being the one to cause her any further pain made me feel a weight that was almost too much to bear. “I’m sorry,” I said again, slipping down from the tree myself. “Maybe once things lighten up a little, I can make something happen.
paras.zh: 可意识到是自己给她带来了更多痛苦，那分量几乎让我承受不住。“对不起，”我又说，自己也溜下树。“也许等局势松动一点，我能想点办法。

paras.en: We could form a convoy.
paras.zh: 我们可以组个车队。

paras.en: Journey out there together.” “Sure,” she said absently as we turned to walk back inside the castle.
paras.zh: 一起出发去那儿。”“行吧，”我们转身走回城堡时，她心不在焉地说。

paras.en: But I could tell she had already dismissed me in her mind.
paras.zh: 可我看得出，她心里已经把我否了。

paras.en: Which hurt more than I wanted to admit.
paras.zh: 这比我想承认的更伤人。

paras.en: And suddenly all I wanted to do was find some way to help her with her quest.
paras.zh: 而忽然间，我只想找点法子帮她完成她的追寻。

paras.en: But at the moment, that seemed even more impossible than getting the mist itself to part.
paras.zh: 可眼下，这看起来比让迷雾自己裂开还不可能。

paras.en: I SNUCK OUT OF ARENDELLE LATE THAT night, over the bridge and into the hills, armed only with a satchel filled with bread and cheese, the horse I’d “borrowed” from the stables just outside the orphanage while everyone was sleeping, and an old map I’d found in the Arendelle library, which I’d used to plot out my trek.
paras.zh: 那天深夜，我溜出阿伦黛尔，过了桥进了山，随身只带一只装满面包和奶酪的挎包、一匹趁孤儿院众人睡着时从马厩“借”来的马，还有一张在阿伦黛尔图书馆找到的旧地图——我靠它规划了路线。

paras.en: I was nervous, a little excited, but mostly freezing cold as we climbed the hills and the temperature continued to drop.
paras.zh: 我很紧张，有点兴奋，但主要是冷得要命——我们爬山时气温还在降。

paras.en: I didn’t love the idea of journeying alone.
paras.zh: 我可不喜欢独自上路这主意。

paras.en: I knew it was dangerous.
paras.zh: 我知道这危险。

paras.en: The elders had always lectured us about going off by ourselves.
paras.zh: 长老们总教训我们别单独行动。

paras.en: They were great believers in strength in numbers.
paras.zh: 他们深信人多力量大。

paras.en: If only Agnarr had agreed to go with me.
paras.zh: 要是安格瑞肯跟我走就好了。

paras.en: I could tell he wanted to, even though he couldn’t.
paras.zh: 我看得出他想，尽管他去不了。

paras.en: Which was ridiculous, right?
paras.zh: 这荒唐，对吧？

paras.en: A prince should be able to do whatever he wanted.
paras.zh: 王子该能为所欲为才对。

paras.en: And yet he seemed as trapped in the castle as my family was in the mist.
paras.zh: 可他倒像被困在城堡里，正如我的家人困在迷雾中。

paras.en: The mist…Would I have been trapped in it, too, had I not run back to the Arendellian camp for my mother’s shawl?
paras.zh: 那迷雾……要不是我跑回阿伦黛尔营地去取母亲的披肩，我是不是也会被它困住？

paras.en: Had I not stopped to save Agnarr…?
paras.zh: 要不是我停下来救安格瑞……？

paras.en: I didn’t know whether to consider myself lucky or not.
paras.zh: 我不知该觉得自己幸运还是不。

paras.en: Which side of the mist did I want to be on?
paras.zh: 我究竟想站在迷雾的哪一侧？

paras.en: Trapped in the Enchanted I shook my head.
paras.zh: 困在魔法……我摇摇头。

paras.en: What I wanted didn’t change a thing.
paras.zh: 我想要什么，改变不了任何事。

paras.en: The fact was I was on the outside, and I needed to see the mist for myself.
paras.zh: 事实是我在这边，我得亲眼去看看那迷雾。

paras.en: Maybe if I went to it, I could call for Gale and the other spirits.
paras.zh: 也许我到了那儿，能呼唤盖尔和其他精灵。

paras.en: Maybe they could give me some answers about what had happened.
paras.zh: 也许他们能给我些关于发生了什么的答案。

paras.en: And how long this apparent curse would last.
paras.zh: 以及这明显的诅咒会持续多久。

paras.en: As my horse crossed a long barren plain, snow began to fall from the sky.
paras.zh: 我的马穿过一片长长的荒原，雪开始从天上落下。

paras.en: Big, fat flakes that landed in clumps on my hair and clothes.
paras.zh: 大朵大朵的雪片，成团地落在我头发和衣服上。

paras.en: The Arendellian clothes I had on were a poor defense against extreme cold weather, and I longed for the old reindeer hides I’d used back home to keep warm.
paras.zh: 我身上阿伦黛尔的衣服御寒很差，我怀念家乡用来保暖的旧驯鹿皮。

paras.en: But still I pressed on.
paras.zh: 可我仍继续前行。

paras.en: I was Northuldra, after all.
paras.zh: 毕竟，我是北地人。

paras.en: I knew how to live among the elements.
paras.zh: 我知道怎么在风雨元素间生存。

paras.en: This was nothing I hadn’t faced before.
paras.zh: 这不过是我从前也面对过的。

paras.en: Though…never alone A wolf howled in the distance and I inhaled sharply.
paras.zh: 虽说……从没独自过。远处一声狼嚎，我猛吸一口气。

paras.en: It was almost dawn when I finally reached the map’s end—a large empty clearing just outside the forest, devoid of trees.
paras.zh: 我终于到达地图的尽头——森林外一大片空旷的空地，没有树。

paras.en: I knew the spot well—my mother used to take me here when I was little to see the four stone monoliths rising high into the sky.
paras.zh: 这地方我很熟——小时候母亲常带我来，看那四块直插天空的石头巨碑。

paras.en: I remembered her explaining the symbols carved into the stones.
paras.zh: 我记得她讲解石头上刻的符号。

paras.en: The four spirits: earth, fire, water, and wind—each with the powers to help the Northuldra with their daily lives, so long as we respected them and their mother, the mighty river Ahtohallan.
paras.zh: 四位精灵：土、火、水、风——各有神力帮北地人过日常日子，只要我们敬重它们和它们的母亲、那强大的河流阿图哈兰。

paras.en: But that day the stones were gone.
paras.zh: 可那天，石头不见了。

paras.en: They’d completely disappeared behind smoky grayish-blue clouds that were as thick as soup and completely opaque, swirling around in a perfect storm and rising high into the sky.
paras.zh: 它们完全消失在烟蓝色的云团后——那云浓得像汤、完全不透明，打着旋聚成一场完美的风暴，直冲高空。

paras.en: This was it.
paras.zh: 就是它了。

paras.en: The mist.
paras.zh: 那迷雾。

paras.en: I slid off my horse, my heart pounding as I approached it.
paras.zh: 我滑下马，心跳如鼓地靠近它。

paras.en: By the time I reached it, my whole body was shaking with trepidation.
paras.zh: 等我走到跟前，整个人怕得发抖。

paras.en: I reached out, brushing the clouds with my fingertips.
paras.zh: 我伸出手，用指尖轻触那云。

paras.en: The mist pushed me away, as if it couldn’t bear my touch.
paras.zh: 迷雾把我推开，像受不了我的触碰。

paras.en: And when I attempted to step through, I bounced right back.
paras.zh: 我试着穿过去，却被直接弹回。

paras.en: I stared at the mist, my mind racing with horror.
paras.zh: 我盯着迷雾，脑中惊恐地飞转。

paras.en: So it was Or was it to punish them?
paras.zh: 所以它……还是说，是为了惩罚他们？

paras.en: Us.
paras.zh: 我们。

paras.en: Everyone.
paras.zh: 所有人。

paras.en: More importantly, how long would it last?
paras.zh: 更重要的是，它会持续多久？

paras.en: Was this a temporary thing?
paras.zh: 这是暂时的吗？

paras.en: Or would it go on forever?
paras.zh: 还是会永远下去？

paras.en: I scrambled to my feet, determination rising inside me.
paras.zh: 我慌忙起身，一股决心在心里升起。

paras.en: Maybe all it would take was a little more force.
paras.zh: 也许只差再使点劲。

paras.en: I backed up, then ran forward, hard as I could toward the mist.
paras.zh: 我退后，然后拼全力朝迷雾冲去。

paras.en: BAM!
paras.zh: 砰！

paras.en: I hit the cold ground hard as the mist shook me off and threw me backward like a rag doll.
paras.zh: 我重重摔在冷地上——迷雾把我抖落，像甩破布娃娃一样把我甩了回去。

paras.en: Determined, I leapt back to my feet, charging at it again, this time holding out my arms, ready to shove it away with both hands.
paras.zh: 我不屈，跳起身又朝它冲，这次张开双臂，准备用双手把它推开。

paras.en: But the mist repelled my advance once again.
paras.zh: 可迷雾再次挡住了我的进击。

paras.en: I flew through the air, then dropped unceremoniously, landing hard on my recently healed ankle.
paras.zh: 我飞了出去，然后狼狈地坠下，重重落在刚愈合的脚踝上。

paras.en: It crumpled beneath me and I cried out as daggers of pain shot up my leg.
paras.zh: 它在身下塌了下去，我痛叫一声，刀扎般的痛顺腿窜上。

paras.en: I collapsed, clutching my leg in agony.
paras.zh: 我瘫倒，痛苦地抱住腿。

paras.en: Tears welled in my eyes and I angrily wiped them away.
paras.zh: 眼里涌出泪，我气恼地把它们抹掉。

paras.en: I tried to stand, but my ankle barked in pain and I realized I couldn’t put any weight on it again.
paras.zh: 我试着站起，可脚踝痛得叫唤，我意识到自己再也不能把重量压上去了。

paras.en: It was swelling, too, already double its normal size with skin that had taken on a purplish hue.
paras.zh: 它还在肿，已经肿到平时两倍大，皮肤泛起了紫色。

paras.en: I curled my hand into a fist and slammed it against the ground in frustration. “Why?” I demanded, looking up at the mist. “You tell me why, right now!” But there was no answer.
paras.zh: 我攥拳狠狠砸在地上，沮丧地。“为什么？”我冲迷雾质问。“你告诉我为什么，就现在！”可没有回答。

paras.en: The mist just swirled its endless gray clouds.
paras.zh: 迷雾只管打着旋，翻它的无尽灰云。

paras.en: Blocking me from my only home.
paras.zh: 把我挡在我唯一的家门外。

paras.en: My family, my friends, completely walled off from reach.
paras.zh: 我的家人、朋友，全被墙隔得遥不可及。

paras.en: Despair settled like a heavy weight in my stomach.
paras.zh: 绝望像块重石沉在肚里。

paras.en: What came next?
paras.zh: 接下来呢？

paras.en: Should I head back to Arendelle, keep living the lie?
paras.zh: 该回阿伦黛尔，继续演那场谎？

paras.en: Leave everything I ever knew and loved behind?
paras.zh: 把一切我熟知和所爱的抛在身后？

paras.en: Become someone else entirely?
paras.zh: 彻底变成另一个人？

paras.en: Daughter of Greta and Torra.
paras.zh: 葛蕾塔和托拉的女儿。

paras.en: Whoever they were.
paras.zh: 管他们是谁。

paras.en: I sat up, rubbing my sore ankle.
paras.zh: 我坐起，揉着酸痛的脚踝。

paras.en: I stared bitterly at the mist. “You couldn’t have given me one more person?” I growled. “Even one?” Why did I have to be the only Northuldra to Because you chose another path, You chose to save your enemy.
paras.zh: 我苦涩地盯着迷雾。“你就不能多留我一个人吗？”我低吼。“哪怕一个？”为什么偏偏我是唯一的北地人……因为你选了另一条路，你选了救你的敌人。

paras.en: I scowled at the fog. “What was I supposed to do?” I demanded. “Just leave him there to die?” If the mist had an answer, it chose not to share it with me.
paras.zh: 我朝雾皱眉。“我还能怎样？”我质问。“就让他死在那儿？”迷雾若有答案，也选择不告诉我。

paras.en: I wrapped my arms around my chest, shivering.
paras.zh: 我双臂抱胸，瑟瑟发抖。

paras.en: The sun had risen, but its early morning rays were barely visible behind thick storm clouds.
paras.zh: 太阳升起了，可清晨的光线在浓密的风暴云后几乎看不见。

paras.en: It would snow again soon; I could smell it in the air.
paras.zh: 很快又要下雪；我从空气里闻得出来。

paras.en: The temperature had dropped further and the wind had picked up, icy blasts stinging my cheeks and nose.
paras.zh: 气温又降了，风也起了，冰冷的疾风刺着我的脸颊和鼻子。

paras.en: I needed to get back to the orphanage before my absence was noticed.
paras.zh: 我得在没人发现我不在之前赶回孤儿院。

paras.en: Gritting my teeth against the sure pain, I tried again to rise to my feet.
paras.zh: 我咬牙忍着那必然的痛，再试着站起来。

paras.en: But my ankle wasn’t having it, forcing me to collapse back onto the cold, hard ground.
paras.zh: 可脚踝不答应，逼我重新瘫回冰冷坚硬的地上。

paras.en: In the distance, a wolf howled, followed by another.
paras.zh: 远处一声狼嚎，接着又一声。

paras.en: Desperate, I lifted my voice to the sky, attempting to call for Gale. “Ah ah ah ah!” The Wind Spirit had always been there for me in the past.
paras.zh: 绝望中，我向天空扬声，试图呼唤盖尔。“啊——啊——啊——啊！”风灵过去总在我身边。

paras.en: Swooping in to save me anytime I found myself in a mess.
paras.zh: 每当我在麻烦里，它就俯冲来救我。

paras.en: But that day my repeated calls went unanswered.
paras.zh: 可那天，我一再去唤，毫无回应。

paras.en: And only an angry, unfriendly wind howled through the trees, chilling me to the bone.
paras.zh: 只有一阵愤怒、不友善的风穿过树林呼啸，把我冻到骨头里。

paras.en: Was Gale also trapped behind the mist?
paras.zh: 盖尔也被困在迷雾后了吗？

paras.en: Or was the Wind Spirit simply angry at me?
paras.zh: 还是风灵单纯在生我的气？

paras.en: The thought made me sad.
paras.zh: 这念头让我难过。

paras.en: In so many ways, the Wind Spirit had been my best friend.
paras.zh: 在许多方面，风灵曾是我最好的朋友。

paras.en: My only Would I be alive when it did?
paras.zh: 我唯一的……等它回来时，我还在吗？

paras.en: Only Ahtohallan knows….
paras.zh: 只有阿图哈兰知道……

paras.en: My mother’s voice rose once again in my heart as I stared out at the impenetrable mist.
paras.zh: 我望着那穿不透的迷雾，母亲的声音再一次在我心底响起。

paras.en: A crushing despair began to weigh on my chest.
paras.zh: 一种压垮人的绝望开始压上胸口。

paras.en: Everyone I ever loved was there behind that wall.
paras.zh: 每个我爱的人都在那道墙后。

paras.en: And I was stuck on the outside, utterly alone.
paras.zh: 而我卡在外头，孤零零一个。

paras.en: But I was not dead yet.
paras.zh: 但我还没死。

paras.en: Grimacing, I forced myself to my hands and knees, ignoring the pain shooting up my leg.
paras.zh: 我龇牙咧嘴，强撑着自己手膝着地，不顾顺腿窜上的痛。

paras.en: I began a halting crawl around the unforgiving surroundings, scooping up piles of leaves and tiny Huddling by the tiny pile, I struck the flint together as I had been taught to do.
paras.zh: 我磕磕绊绊地在冷酷的四周爬，拢起一堆堆落叶和细……我蜷在那一小堆旁，按学来的法子敲打火石。

paras.en: At first nothing happened.
paras.zh: 起初什么也没发生。

paras.en: Then there was a spark of light that died quickly on leaves damp with the first breath of snow.
paras.zh: 接着迸出一点火星，却在沾了初雪湿气的叶子上很快灭了。

paras.en: Finally, I managed to create a small flame with a single dry leaf.
paras.zh: 终于，我用一片干叶点起了小小的火苗。

paras.en: The flame spread to the next leaf and then a twig.
paras.zh: 火苗蔓延到下一叶，再到一小枝。

paras.en: The crackling sound was a merry contrast to the desolate setting.
paras.zh: 那噼啪声，与荒凉的环境形成欢快的对照。

paras.en: I had a fire.
paras.zh: 我有火了。

paras.en: A tiny one—Bruni would have smiled at its feeble flame—but it was better than nothing.
paras.zh: 很小的一团——布鲁尼准会对它微弱的火苗微笑——但总比没有强。

paras.en: I held my freezing hands over it, warming them as best I could.
paras.zh: 我把冻僵的手伸到火上，尽量取暖。

paras.en: As the heat from it spread through my fingertips, a small shred of hope rose in my heart.
paras.zh: 热从指尖漫开，一丝微小的希望在心里升起。

paras.en: The wolves in the distance howled again, but I ignored them this time, instead drowning out their voices with a song of my own.
paras.zh: 远处的狼又嚎，可这回我不管它们，反而用自己的歌盖过它们的声音。

paras.en: Until I heard a noise behind me.
paras.zh: 直到我听见身后一声响动。

paras.en: I CLAMPED MY MOUTH SHUT, WHIRLING around, my heart in my throat at the sudden sound.
paras.zh: 我猛地闭嘴，转过身，那突如其来的声响让心提到了嗓子眼。

paras.en: A heavily cloaked figure rode into view astride a tall white horse.
paras.zh: 一个裹得严严实实的人影，骑着一匹高大的白马出现在视野里。

paras.en: At first I thought it must be an illusion—the kind of hallucination one might see before freezing to death.
paras.zh: 起初我以为那准是幻觉——冻死前会看到的那种幻象。

paras.en: But when I blinked, the figure was still there.
paras.zh: 可我眨眨眼，那身影还在。

paras.en: It was Agnarr. “Sorry I’m late,” he said with a bashful grin.
paras.zh: 是安格瑞。“抱歉我来晚了，”他带着腼腆的笑说。

paras.en: Emotion flooded me before I could stop it.
paras.zh: 情绪在我来得及阻止前就涌了上来。

paras.en: He’d come!
paras.zh: 他来了！

paras.en: He’d actually come.
paras.zh: 他真的来了。

paras.en: Not that I’d needed him, of course, I scolded myself.
paras.zh: 当然，我并不需要他，我责备自己。

paras.en: Obviously.
paras.zh: 显然。

paras.en: I wasn’t some damsel in distress from one of those Arendellian books, in need of rescue from a handsome prince.
paras.zh: 我又不是那些阿伦黛尔书里的落难少女，需要帅气王子来救。

paras.en: Still, I couldn’t stop the fountain of joy from bubbling up inside me as I watched him approach on his horse.
paras.zh: 可看着他骑马走近，我止不住心里那股喜悦的泉涌。

paras.en: I wasn’t alone anymore.
paras.zh: 我不再是一个人了。

paras.en: I gasped as he climbed down from the horse and strode toward me. “Are you all right?” he asked, his smile fading as he got closer to me and observed my swollen ankle.
paras.zh: 他下马大步朝我走来，我倒抽一口气。“你还好吗？”他问，走近查清我肿起的脚踝，笑容淡了。

paras.en: My pathetic little fire. “I’m fine,” I shot back quickly, though it was obvious I “Eh.” He shrugged. “I figured in this case it might be better to ask forgiveness than permission.” His mouth quirked. “Besides, everyone probably thinks I’m holed up in my room with a good book, as usual.
paras.zh: 我那可怜的小火堆。“我没事，”我飞快回嘴，尽管显然我……“呃。”他耸耸肩。“我想这回还是先斩后奏比较好。”他嘴角一挑。“再说了，大家大概都以为我像往常一样窝在房里看好书呢。

paras.en: They won’t start looking for me for ages.” I watched as he walked over to the mist, dragging a hand across its surface, his eyes as wide as saucers. “So, this is it,” he marveled. “The magical mist everyone’s been talking about.” “Don’t try to walk through it,” I warned him ruefully. “It may look like mist, but it’s solid as rock.” “Did you walk around it?
paras.zh: 他们一时半会儿不会来找我。”我看着他走到迷雾前，用手拂过它的表面，眼睛瞪得像碟子。“所以，这就是它了，”他惊叹。“大家一直说的魔法迷雾。”“别试着穿过去，”我无奈地警告。“它看着像雾，其实硬如岩石。”“你绕着它走过吗？

paras.en: See if there were any openings?” I shook my head. “But if there were, people would have come out by now, right?
paras.zh: 看有没有什么缺口？”我摇头。“可要是有，人早就出来了，对吧？

paras.en: They would have made their way back to Arendelle.” “Yeah.” His smile faded. “I guess you’re right.” Another gust of wind blew through the clearing and I shivered violently, the cold seeping into my bones despite the warmth of the fire.
paras.zh: 他们早该回到阿伦黛尔了。”“是啊。”他的笑淡了。“我想你是对的。”又一阵风刮过空地，我剧烈地打了个寒颤，尽管有火，冷还是渗进了骨头。

paras.en: Agnarr noticed immediately and abandoned the mist, walking over to me and pulling off his thick woolen cloak, then draping it over my shoulders. “You’ll be cold,” I protested.
paras.zh: 安格瑞立刻注意到，离开迷雾走到我身边，脱下厚羊毛斗篷披在我肩上。“你会冷的，”我抗议。

paras.en: He waved a hand. “The cold never bothers me.” “Liar,” I accused as his body betrayed him with a fierce, all-consuming shiver.
paras.zh: 他摆摆手。“寒冷从不烦我。”“骗子，”我戳穿，因为他的身体出卖了他——一阵猛烈、止不住的寒颤。

paras.en: He grinned sheepishly. “Okay fine.
paras.zh: 他不好意思地咧嘴。“好吧。

paras.en: I hate the cold.
paras.zh: 我恨冷。

paras.en: But I’m not taking back my cloak.” “Then come share it with me,” I said, beckoning him over. “This thing is huge.
paras.zh: 但我的斗篷不收回。”“那就过来跟我一起披，”我招手叫他。“这斗篷大得很。

paras.en: Surely it can warm us both.” Something flashed across Agnarr’s face that I didn’t quite recognize, but after a moment’s pause, he relented and dropped down to join me by the fire, crawling under the thick fabric I held open and wrapping it around his body.
paras.zh: 肯定够暖咱俩。”安格瑞脸上掠过一丝我不太认得的神色，但顿了顿，他还是让步，在火边挨着我坐下，钻进我撑开的厚布里，把自己裹上。

paras.en: I could feel his shoulder press up against mine, and a strange sensation wormed through my stomach.
paras.zh: 我能感到他的肩膀抵着我的，一种奇怪的感觉在我胃里蠕行。

paras.en: Back home, my family had always huddled together on cold nights, using our shared body heat to keep warm.
paras.zh: 在家里，寒夜里我们一家总挤在一起，用彼此的体温取暖。

paras.en: This was no different, right?
paras.zh: 这没两样，对吧？

paras.en: Except somehow it was.
paras.zh: 可不知怎的，它就是不一样。

paras.en: It felt a lot different. “Scooch in,” I said jokingly, trying to ease the sudden tension.
paras.zh: 感觉大不一样。“往里挤挤，”我玩笑道，想缓解这突来的紧张。

paras.en: It was what we used to say back home. “There’s plenty of room for two.” “I’m not surprised,” he replied, inching us closer to the fire. “It was my father’s cloak.
paras.zh: 这是我们在家常说的话。“两个人挤挤够宽。”“我不意外，”他答，把我们往火边挪近。“这是我父亲的斗篷。

paras.en: He was a large man.” He trailed off, his gaze going back to the mist.
paras.zh: 他是个大块头。”他说着没了下文，目光又回到迷雾上。

paras.en: A look of longing came over his face.
paras.zh: 他脸上浮起渴望的神情。

paras.en: And suddenly I was struck by the fact that I was not the only one who had lost people that day.
paras.zh: 忽然我猛然意识到，那天失去亲人的，不止我一个。

paras.en: Agnarr had lost his father.
paras.zh: 安格瑞失去了父亲。

paras.en: And likely others, too. “Do you miss him?” I asked. “Your father.” He didn’t answer at first, still staring into the swirling gray fog.
paras.zh: 大概也失去了别人。“你想他吗？”我问。“你父亲。”他起初没答，仍盯着翻卷的灰雾。

paras.en: Then he gave a long sigh. “My father and I had a…complicated…relationship.
paras.zh: 然后他长叹一声。“我父亲和我……关系……挺复杂。

paras.en: We fought that day at the dam.
paras.zh: 那天在大坝边我们吵了。

paras.en: He was angry at me for wandering off to explore.
paras.zh: 他气我乱跑去看新鲜。

paras.en: He said I was acting like a child, not a prince.” He scowled. “He scolded me in front of everyone—all the soldiers and shield-maidens.
paras.zh: 他说我像孩子，不像王子。”他皱眉。“他当着所有人——所有士兵和持盾女战士——骂我。

paras.en: I was embarrassed.
paras.zh: 我丢脸。

paras.en: Angry, too.
paras.zh: 也生气。

paras.en: I’ve been angry with him for a long time.
paras.zh: 我生他气很久了。

paras.en: It was like nothing I ever did was good enough for him.
paras.zh: 好像我做的事，没有一件让他满意。

paras.en: That he wished he had a better son.” He gulped a breath, like he was about to say something he wasn’t certain should be said out loud. “The truth is, as much as I miss him, I think I’m still pretty angry with him now.” He dropped his gaze to his hands.
paras.zh: 好像他巴不得有个更好的儿子。”他咽了口气，像要说出什么不确定该不该说出口的话。“其实，哪怕我想他，我想我现在还是挺生他气的。”他垂眼看着自己的手。

paras.en: My heart panged at the conflicting emotions I saw on his face.
paras.zh: 看到他脸上矛盾的表情，我的心一痛。

paras.en: When he looked up at me again, his eyes were rimmed with unshed tears. “But I feel guilty, too.
paras.zh: 他再抬头看我时，眼眶里含着没掉的泪。“可我也觉得愧疚。

paras.en: If we hadn’t fought that day, I would have been by his side when it all happened.
paras.zh: 要是那天我们没吵，一切发生时我本该在他身边。

paras.en: Maybe I could have helped.
paras.zh: 也许我能帮上忙。

paras.en: Maybe I could have saved him.” His voice broke. “Maybe he wouldn’t be dead.” I nodded slowly, not trusting my voice to speak.
paras.zh: 也许我能救他。”他的声音破了。“也许他就不会死。”我缓缓点头，不敢开口出声。

paras.en: I thought about my own last day in the forest.
paras.zh: 我想起自己在森林里最后那天。

paras.en: Yelana calling me to my lessons.
paras.zh: 耶拉娜喊我去上课。

paras.en: Had I listened to her, I would never have discovered Agnarr.
paras.zh: 要是我听了她的，就永远不会遇见安格瑞。

paras.en: I would not be here, now, wrapped in his father’s cloak, his warm shoulder pressed against mine.
paras.zh: 就不会在这儿，此刻裹着他父亲的斗篷，他温暖的肩膀抵着我的肩。

paras.en: I sighed resignedly.
paras.zh: 我认命地叹了口气。

paras.en: As much as I wanted to, I couldn’t regret what I had done.
paras.zh: 尽管我想后悔，却没法为做过的事后悔。

paras.en: And I knew, in my heart, I would have done it anyway, even knowing the cost.
paras.zh: 而我心里知道，就算知道代价，我还是会那么做。

paras.en: I did not deserve to be locked “Let’s make a pact,” he declared. “We’ll come back here twice a year.
paras.zh: 我不该被锁……“我们定个约定吧，”他宣布。“我们每年回来两次。

paras.en: Every spring and autumn,” he added. “We’ll travel out here and we’ll check the mist.
paras.zh: 每春秋两季，”他补充。“我们远道来这儿，查看这迷雾。

paras.en: Maybe it’ll start to fade gradually.
paras.zh: 也许它会慢慢淡去。

paras.en: Maybe we’ll start finding weak spots.
paras.zh: 也许我们会开始找到薄弱处。

paras.en: Maybe we’ll eventually find a place we can push through.” His eyes shone as he spoke, and I found myself getting swept up in his hope, however naive.
paras.zh: 也许终有一天能找到可以穿过去的地方。”他说话时眼睛发亮，我不由自主被他的希望卷了进去，哪怕天真。

paras.en: The mist parting.
paras.zh: 迷雾裂开。

paras.en: Us stepping through.
paras.zh: 我们穿过去。

paras.en: Our families, our friends, greeting us on the other side.
paras.zh: 我们的家人、朋友，在另一侧迎接我们。

paras.en: Instinctively, I reached out, clasping his hand in my own and squeezing it tight.
paras.zh: 出于本能，我伸出手，把他的手握进掌心，紧紧一握。

paras.en: He turned to look at me, his eyes sparkling. “So, is that a yes?” he asked. “We’ll return in six months?” I nodded solemnly. “Six months,” I agreed, before shivering again.
paras.zh: 他转头看我，眼里闪着光。“那么，答应了？”他问。“我们六个月后回来？”我郑重点头。“六个月，”我应下，然后又打了个寒颤。

paras.en: I laughed. “Though next time I’m bringing a much warmer coat.” “And I’m bringing chocolate,” Agnarr added with a mischievous grin. “A lot of chocolate.” And just like that, I found my very first friend on the other side of the mist.
paras.zh: 我笑了。“不过下次我要带件暖和得多的外套。”“而我要带巧克力，”安格瑞淘气地咧嘴补充。“好多巧克力。”就这样，我找到了自己在迷雾另一侧的第一位朋友。

chapters.title: Chapter Nine: Iduna: Four Years Later

paras.en: “AND SO, IT BEGINS!
paras.zh: “那么，开始吧！

paras.en: OUR EIGHTH BIANNUAL trek to the glorious, yet still stubbornly mist-bound Enchanted Forest!” I said as I jumped into the wagon beside Agnarr.
paras.zh: 我们第八次半年一度的远行，奔赴那壮丽却仍固执地被迷雾锁住的魔法森林！”我边说边跳上安格瑞身旁的马车。

paras.en: He flicked the reins from the driver’s seat and the two horses dutifully sprang into action, the wagon lurching in their wake before I was properly seated.
paras.zh: 他在车夫座上甩了甩缰绳，两匹马听话地动起来，车在它们身后一颠，我还没坐稳。

paras.en: I squealed in protest, grabbing the prince’s arm to prevent myself from tumbling off altogether. “Someone’s in a hurry,” I teased after regaining my balance.
paras.zh: 我尖叫着抗议，抓住王子的胳膊不让自己翻下去。“有人急得很嘛，”找回平衡后我打趣道。

paras.en: I shoved him playfully in the other direction, to give him a taste of his own medicine. “I’m just relieved to finally be on our way!” he declared. “We’re three weeks late this spring, you know!” “Oh, I’m so About a year ago, I’d started apprenticing under an inventor named Johan, who was working to find a way to harness wind power in order to create a natural fuel source for grain mills and water pumps.
paras.zh: 我顽皮地把他往另一边推，让他也尝尝这滋味。“终于上路了，我可松了口气！”他宣布。“今年春天我们晚了三周呢，你知道的！”“噢，我太……大约一年前，我开始给一位叫约翰的发明家当学徒，他正设法利用风力，为磨坊和水泵造一种天然燃料。

paras.en: It was fascinating work, and it turned out I was good at it, too.
paras.zh: 这工作很迷人，而且结果证明我也挺在行。

paras.en: After all, I did know something about the power The past few weeks we’d had terrific weather conditions brought about by an unexpected late spring storm that blew gales of glorious wind into our fjord, so when I wasn’t continuing my studies under the close and demanding eye of Miss Larsen at the castle, I’d been working every spare moment.
paras.zh: 毕竟，我确实懂点那力量……过去几周，一场意外的暮春风暴把壮观的大风刮进我们的峡湾，带来了极好的天气条件，于是除了在城堡里在拉森小姐严格的要求下继续学业，我一有空就在干。

paras.en: It hadn’t been easy to find time to get away.
paras.zh: 要抽出时间离开并不容易。

paras.en: Agnarr gave me a mock offended look. “I work hard, too, you know,” he reminded me. “Arendelle does not just rule itself.” “I know, I know,” I assured him, giving him a comforting pat. “Heavy is the head that wears the crown.” Even though Lord Peterssen was still acting as regent for the next three years—until Agnarr would assume the throne—the young prince had a ton of responsibilities to his kingdom.
paras.zh: 安格瑞做出一副被冒犯的样子。”我也辛苦着呢，你知道的，“他提醒我。”阿伦黛尔可不是自己管自己的。“”知道知道，“我安慰地拍拍他。”为王者，负重也。“”虽说到安格瑞继位前，彼得森大人还要再摄政三年，可这位年轻王子对王国已有一堆责任。

paras.en: And they seemingly grew more and more each day.
paras.zh: 而且似乎与日俱增。

paras.en: Agnarr sat in on all the council meetings where they discussed state affairs, and listened to petitions from the people of Arendelle every week.
paras.zh: 安格瑞列席所有讨论国事的议会，每周听阿伦黛尔百姓的请愿。

paras.en: He was always patient, listening carefully, trying to come up with reasonable solutions.
paras.zh: 他总很有耐心，仔细听，想办法给出合理的解决。

paras.en: And the people loved him for that.
paras.zh: 百姓因此爱戴他。

paras.en: I’d constantly hear them singing the praises of the fair-minded, rational, and intelligent soon-to-be king as I walked through town.
paras.zh: 我在镇上走，常听见他们赞美这位公正、理性又聪慧的准国王。

paras.en: It warmed my heart to know he was such a beloved ruler even before officially taking the throne.
paras.zh: 知道他还没正式登基就已是这么受爱戴的君主，我心里暖暖的。

paras.en: From what I’d gathered, his father had been respected—feared, even—but the people had never truly warmed to him the way they seemed to have already warmed to Agnarr.
paras.zh: 据我所知，他父亲受人尊敬——甚至让人畏惧——但百姓从没像对安格瑞这样真正亲近过。

paras.en: Agnarr reached into his satchel, pulling out a chunk of chocolate and snapping it in two.
paras.zh: 安格瑞伸手进挎包，掏出一块巧克力，掰成两半。

paras.en: He kept one, handing the larger half to me.
paras.zh: 自己留一块，把大的那半递给我。

paras.en: I smiled as I bit into the sweetness, savoring the rich taste on my tongue.
paras.zh: 我笑着咬下那甜味，回味舌尖浓郁的滋味。

paras.en: One of my favorite things about Arendelle—the chocolate.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔让我最喜欢的东西之一——就是巧克力。

paras.en: That, and all the books at my disposal, thanks to the castle library.
paras.zh: 还有，多得是任我翻阅的书，多亏了城堡藏书室。

paras.en: Even four years into our shared lessons, I never tired of exploring the dusty shelves and seeing what new adventures I could find.
paras.zh: 哪怕我们一起上课都四年了，我仍不厌其烦地探索那些落灰的书架，看能找到什么新冒险。

paras.en: As the wagon rolled across the bridge and out of the village, then started up into the hills, I reached into my own satchel, “I’m boring you already, huh?
paras.zh: 马车过桥出村，然后开始上山，我伸手探进自己的挎包，“我这么快就让你无聊了，嗯？

paras.en: And here we’ve barely left town.” My eyes sparkled as I cracked open the book. “Nothing personal.
paras.zh: 我们才刚出镇呢。”我翻开书，眼睛亮了。“别往心里去。

paras.en: I’m just at a really good part.” “Oh, fine,” he said, turning back to the horses. “Guess I’ll have to entertain myself.” He cleared his throat and broke out into a loud, bellowing, and really terrible rendition of a popular Arendellian song: “I smell that reindeer pee, blowing through the fjord.
paras.zh: 我只是看到特精彩的一段。”“噢，行吧，”他转回去看马。“看来我得自己找乐子了。”他清清嗓子，放声吼出一首流行阿伦黛尔歌的、实在难听至极的版本：“我闻到那驯鹿尿，飘过峡湾。

paras.en: Iduna’s ignoring me, so I’m really bored….” Urgh. “What?” he asked, shooting me an all-too-innocent look. “You don’t like my singing?” “No one likes your singing, Agnarr.
paras.zh: 伊杜娜不理我，所以我真无聊……”呃。“怎么？”他投来一个过于无辜的眼神。“你不喜欢我唱？”“没人喜欢你唱，安格瑞。

paras.en: Not even the horses.” “Is that true?” he asked the horses in question, flicking the reins again.
paras.zh: 连马都不喜欢。”真的吗？“他问那两匹马，又甩了甩缰绳。

paras.en: The two mares snorted loudly—a definitive answer, if I ever heard one.
paras.zh: 两匹母马大声喷着鼻——要我说，这答案再明确不过。

paras.en: I started giggling.
paras.zh: 我咯咯笑起来。

paras.en: Agnarr sighed. “Everyone’s a critic.” He flashed me a silly grin, telling me he didn’t really mind.
paras.zh: 安格瑞叹气。”个个都是乐评家。“他冲我傻笑，告诉我他其实不在意。

paras.en: I smiled back at him, setting the book on my lap. “You’re in a good mood,” I noted. “And why wouldn’t I be?” he shot back, stretching his arm out to the landscape in front of us. “The sun is shining.
paras.zh: 我回他一笑，把书放腿上。”你心情不错嘛，“我说。”我凭什么不好？“他回嘴，手臂朝眼前风景一展。”阳光灿烂。

paras.en: The sky is blue.
paras.zh: 天空湛蓝。

paras.en: I’ve got my best friend by my side and we’re leaving the dreary castle for a few days of freedom.” “With all twenty-two of our very best friends,” I added, glancing back at the Arendelle mounted guard at our backs.
paras.zh: 我最好的朋友在身边，我们离开沉闷的城堡，享受几天自由。“”还有我们二十二个最要好的朋友，“我补充，回头瞥了眼身后阿伦黛尔的骑兵卫队。

paras.en: Agnarr had insisted they stay at least twenty yards behind us, but it was difficult to ignore their presence altogether. “Ugh.
paras.zh: 安格瑞坚持让他们至少落后二十码，可要完全无视他们的存在很难。”呃。

paras.en: Don’t look at them,” he groaned. “Pretend it’s just me and you, like the old days.” I smiled at this.
paras.zh: 别看他们，“他呻吟。”就当只有我和你，像从前那样。“我为此笑了。

paras.en: Back in the “old days” as he called them, we’d made this journey on the sly, sneaking out of Arendelle every At this point, it had become such a time-honored tradition that it was hard to remember that first year, when I’d headed out alone, scared and sad and reckless, desperate to learn the fate of my family.
paras.zh: 在他口中的”旧日“，我们曾偷偷走这趟路，每次溜出阿伦黛尔……到如今它已成了悠久的传统，让人难记起头一年——那时我独自上路，又怕又悲又莽撞，拼命想打听家人的下落。

paras.en: When Agnarr had come after me—to make sure I was safe—even at the risk of getting in serious trouble once he returned home.
paras.zh: 那时安格瑞追了出来——只为确保我安全——哪怕回去会惹上大麻烦。

paras.en: Back then he had been a stranger.
paras.zh: 那时他还是个陌生人。

paras.en: My enemy.
paras.zh: 我的敌人。

paras.en: And yet somehow it hadn’t felt like that as I watched him step up to the mist.
paras.zh: 可看着他走到迷雾前，那感觉却不知怎的不像了。

paras.en: As I saw the grief washing over his boyish face.
paras.zh: 当我看见悲伤漫上他孩子气的脸。

paras.en: As he spoke of his dead father and all the things he’d never gotten a chance to say to him.
paras.zh: 当他谈起死去的父亲，和所有没机会对他说出口的话。

paras.en: It was the first time I realized we were more alike than different.
paras.zh: 那是我第一次意识到，我们相似多于不同。

paras.en: That we should be friends, not enemies.
paras.zh: 我们本该是朋友，不是敌人。

paras.en: The next few trips had been a lot more fun.
paras.zh: 后来几次出行快活多了。

paras.en: We’d sneak out of Arendelle in the dead of night with only the provisions we could carry on our backs.
paras.zh: 我们在深夜溜出阿伦黛尔，只带背得动的东西。

paras.en: Which had led to some difficulties that second trip when we’d run out of snacks halfway there.
paras.zh: 这导致第二次半路零食吃光，出了点麻烦。

paras.en: Luckily for my indoorsy prince, I knew how to live off the land and showed him which berries were safe to eat and which streams were safe to drink from.
paras.zh: 幸亏我这位爱待屋里的王子，我知道怎么靠野地谋生，告诉他哪些莓子能吃、哪些溪水能喝。

paras.en: Unfortunately, he’d still gotten quite the stomachache after drinking some supposedly clean river water, which I felt bad about.
paras.zh: 可惜，他喝了号称干净的河水后还是闹了挺厉害的肚子，我有点过意不去。

paras.en: Though not bad enough to stop me from teasing him about his “delicate princely stomach”…which made him want to push me into the river. “What are you reading, anyways?” Agnarr asked now, throwing me a glance.
paras.zh: 不过还没到让我停下去取笑他”娇贵王子的胃“的地步……那倒让他想把我推进河里。”你到底在读什么？“安格瑞这会儿瞥我一眼问。

paras.en: I held the cover up to him. “‘ Creatures of Mists and Legends “Oh, it is.” I nodded, warming to the topic of my latest literary conquest. “Right now, I’m reading about the Huldréfolk.” “Hold-a-fork-of-what?” “ Huldréfolk, “That’s creepy.” “It’s fascinating “What do they do with them once they find them?” “They keep them.” “Okay.
paras.zh: 我把封面举给他看。”'《迷雾与传说中的生灵》'“哦，是呢。”我点头，对我最新征服的文学话题来了劲。“这会儿我在读胡尔德精灵。”“hold-a-fork-of-啥？”“胡尔德精灵。”“那挺瘆人。”“可迷人……”“他们找到后怎么处置？”“他们养着。”“好吧。

paras.en: Not I snorted. “Sure.
paras.zh: 才不……”我嗤鼻。“当然。

paras.en: I’ll let you tell them that.
paras.zh: 我让你去跟他们讲这个。

paras.en: Or maybe you can make it a law, once you’re king.” “Absolutely.
paras.zh: 或者等你当了国王，立条法也行。”“绝对。

paras.en: In fact, it’ll be my very first act as rightful ruler of Arendelle!” he declared. “Who knows, maybe I’ll get all those lost socks back.” “Ah, yes.
paras.zh: 事实上，这将是我作为阿伦黛尔合法 ruler 的第一道政令！”他宣布。“谁知道呢，也许我能把那些失踪的袜子都找回来。”“啊，对。

paras.en: King Agnarr, first of his name.
paras.zh: 安格瑞王，同名第一任。

paras.en: Returner of Stinky Socks.
paras.zh: 臭袜回收者。

paras.en: You’re sure to be a legend,” I teased as I turned back to my book.
paras.zh: 你准会成传奇，”我打趣着转回书。

paras.en: A comfortable silence fell over us as the wagon continued to roll down the path.
paras.zh: 马车沿路继续滚，一阵舒服的沉默落在我俩之间。

paras.en: It was a beautiful day, the world springing back to life after sleeping all winter.
paras.zh: 那是个美丽的日子，世界在冬眠后正苏醒过来。

paras.en: Tiny green buds poked their heads out from the earth.
paras.zh: 小小的绿芽从土里探出头。

paras.en: Emerald leaves unfurled from tree branches.
paras.zh: 翡翠般的叶子在枝上舒展。

paras.en: It was as if there was a promise in the air.
paras.zh: 空气里仿佛有个承诺。

paras.en: A rebirth.
paras.zh: 一次重生。

paras.en: It made my heart swell with joy.
paras.zh: 它让我的心涨满欢喜。

paras.en: It also reminded me of home.
paras.zh: 它也让我想起家。

paras.en: Although by now, my concept of “home” had become somewhat complicated.
paras.zh: 虽说如今，我“家”的概念已变得有点复杂。

paras.en: Arendelle no longer seemed a scary place, with shadows lurking in every corner.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔不再像个处处藏着阴影的可怕地方。

paras.en: Instead, it was familiar, expected, comforting.
paras.zh: 相反，它熟悉、可料、让人安心。

paras.en: It was Though I did wonder, deep down, if they would still be so welcoming if they knew the truth of who I was.
paras.zh: 它是……不过心底里，我确实怀疑，要是他们知道我是谁，还会这么欢迎我吗。

paras.en: Where my real home lay.
paras.zh: 我真正的家在何处。

paras.en: Because that was the dark cloud that still hung over an otherwise upbeat kingdom.
paras.zh: 因为那片乌云，仍悬在这个本该明朗的王国上空。

paras.en: The resentment and suspicion of the Northuldra and their supposed sorcery were still on the tips of But instead of souring their wine, this Northuldra was helping their farmers become self-sufficient.
paras.zh: 对北地人和他们所谓妖术的怨恨与猜疑，仍挂在……可这北地人没去酸他们的酒，反在帮他们的农民自给自足。

paras.en: Instead of tearing shingles from roofs, I was poring over books, studying the science of wind.
paras.zh: 没去掀房顶的瓦，我正埋头书本，研究风的科学。

paras.en: Instead of lurking under children’s beds, I had started teaching orphans to read.
paras.zh: 没去躲在孩子们床下，我已开始教孤儿认字。

paras.en: Living a normal life, with no magic flowing through my perfectly average, human veins.
paras.zh: 过着平常日子，魔法没在我再普通不过的人类血管里流半点。

paras.en: In fact, I hadn’t even been able to ask the spirits for help since the mist had fallen.
paras.zh: 事实上，自迷雾落下，我连向精灵求助都做不到了。

paras.en: I still tried to call for Gale every once in a while, but the Wind Spirit never answered.
paras.zh: 我仍时不时试着呼唤盖尔，可风灵从不回应。

paras.en: It was as if they’d all fallen fast—and firmly—asleep.
paras.zh: 仿佛它们都沉沉——且牢牢——地睡去了。

paras.en: But that didn’t make for a good story, did it?
paras.zh: 可那可不算个好故事，对吧？

paras.en: WE SETTLED DOWN TO CAMP FOR THE NIGHT, still a few miles away from the mist.
paras.zh: 我们安顿下来扎营过夜，此时距离迷雾还有几英里。

paras.en: We did this each time, though we probably could have made it in a single day if we really pushed ourselves.
paras.zh: 每次我们都是这么做的，虽说如果真狠下心赶路，我们大概一天就能到。

paras.en: But Agnarr loved the excuse to be away from the castle, his studies, and the endless meetings, even if it meant having an entourage in tow. “How do I start this fire again?” Agnarr asked, frustrated, struggling with the flint.
paras.zh: 可安格瑞很享受能离开城堡、离开功课和无休止的会议的机会，哪怕这意味着要带着一队随从同行。“我该怎么重新生起这堆火来着？”安格瑞有些懊恼地摆弄着火石问道。

paras.en: I rolled my eyes good-naturedly.
paras.zh: 我没好气地翻了个白眼，却掩不住笑意。

paras.en: No matter how many times we went through this ritual, the prince could not seem to grasp the simple tasks of outdoor living.
paras.zh: 无论我们重复过多少次这套仪式，这位王子似乎始终学不会户外生存的那些简单活儿。

paras.en: The product of growing up in a bespoke castle, I supposed.
paras.zh: 我想，这大概就是从小长在专为他打造的城堡里的结果吧。

paras.en: I came over to help him, flicking the stones together in one swift motion to create a spark.
paras.zh: 我走过去帮他，手腕一抖，石片相击，瞬间迸出火星。

paras.en: Then I leaned over the pile of twigs he’d gathered and blew gently, coaxing them to light.
paras.zh: 接着我俯身凑向他捡来的那堆细枝，轻轻吹气，引它们燃起来。

paras.en: Once they were aflame, I added more leaves, then a few sticks of wood.
paras.zh: 等火苗蹿起，我又添上些枯叶，再架上几根木柴。

paras.en: Soon we had a cheery little fire. “I don’t know how you do it,” he said, shaking his head. “First time, every time!
paras.zh: 很快，我们就有了团欢快的小火。 “我真不知道你怎么做到的，”他摇着头说，“每次都一次成功！

paras.en: It’s like magic.” I frowned. “Not magic,” I said firmly. “Only practice.
paras.zh: 简直像魔法一样。”我皱起眉。“不是魔法，”我斩钉截铁地说，“只是练习。

paras.en: And patience.” He grinned at me, leaning back against a nearby boulder and placing his hands behind his head.
paras.zh: 还有耐心。”他冲我咧嘴一笑，往后靠向身旁一块大石头，双手枕在脑后。

paras.en: He glanced at the company of guards, setting up camp a short distance away.
paras.zh: 他瞥了眼不远处正扎营的卫兵们。

paras.en: We would join them later in the evening, when it was time to go to sleep.
paras.zh: 等晚上该睡了，我们才会过去跟他们会合。

paras.en: Agnarr and I each had our own tent, circled by guards.
paras.zh: 安格瑞和我有各自的帐篷，外头围着卫兵。

paras.en: But for now, they allowed us a tiny bit of time alone with one another. “Practice,” he scoffed. “As if I have time for that.
paras.zh: 不过眼下，他们容许我们单独相处一小会儿。“练习？”他嗤笑道，“说得好像我有那闲工夫似的。

paras.en: I swear Lord Peterssen has been setting up more meetings on purpose these days, just to keep me busy.” He shook his head. “First thing I do when I become king?
paras.zh: 我发誓，彼得森大人最近是故意安排更多会议的，就为了把我忙得团团转。”他摇摇头。“等我当了国王第一件事？

paras.en: Outlaw meetings throughout the land.” He winked at me. “I can do that, right?” “Oh, yes,” I agreed. “I’m sure everyone “Annihilator of Meetings.
paras.zh: 就是取缔全境的会议。”他朝我眨眨眼。“这我总可以吧？”“哦，当然，”我附和道，“我相信所有人都会称你为‘会议终结者’。

paras.en: Returner of Stinky Socks.
paras.zh: ‘臭袜子归还者’。

paras.en: I’ve got quite a legacy going, don’t I?” he said jokingly.
paras.zh: 我这也算留下了不小的‘威名’了吧？”他打趣道。

paras.en: Then he sighed. “You don’t know how lucky you are to not have to think about this ruling-the-kingdom stuff.
paras.zh: 接着他叹了口气。“你不知道自己有多幸运，完全不用操心治理王国这种事。

paras.en: I wouldn’t wish it on my worst enemy.” I gave him a sympathetic look.
paras.zh: 就算是我最恨的仇敌，我也不愿把这种担子扣给他头上。”我同情地看了他一眼。

paras.en: While we liked to tease each other, I knew how hard Agnarr worked each day, trying to make Arendelle a better place.
paras.zh: 虽然我们总爱互相打趣，但我知道安格瑞每天有多努力，一心想把阿伦黛尔变得更好。

paras.en: It wasn’t easy. “But enough about me,” he declared, sitting up straighter, changing the subject. “ You’re I smiled, happy that he remembered my latest project, though not surprised.
paras.zh: “这可不容易。” “不过不说我了，”他坐直身子，转了话题，“你……”我笑了，很高兴他还记得我最近的项目，尽管并不意外。

paras.en: Agnarr was always asking about my work and genuinely wanting to know about my progress and failures, celebrating alongside me when I had a breakthrough and consoling me when a new idea flopped.
paras.zh: 安格瑞总是过问我的工作，真心想知道我的进展和挫折，在我有了突破时一同庆祝，在新点子失败时安慰我。

paras.en: He treated my apprenticeship as if it were just as important as ruling a kingdom.
paras.zh: 他对待我的学徒生涯，仿佛和国王理政一样重要。

paras.en: But that was Agnarr.
paras.zh: 可安格瑞就是这样的人。

paras.en: He always took an interest in the little things happening around the kingdom: how the crops were growing, how the people were getting along, the new babies who were born, the elders who died.
paras.zh: 他总惦记着王国里发生的小事：庄稼长得怎样，百姓相处得可好，谁家添了新生儿，哪位长者离世了。

paras.en: All that on top of the big-picture “We’re getting there,” I said. “We’re still working out some kinks.
paras.zh: 这些之外，还有那些大局…… “我们快成了，”我说，“还有些小毛病要打磨。

paras.en: But I had a new brainstorm the other day and Johan’s going to try it out while we’re gone.
paras.zh: 不过前几天我有了个新点子，约翰趁我们不在会去试一试。

paras.en: Hopefully he’ll finally get it to work.” It was funny; when I’d first seen the “apprentice wanted” posting a year ago, I’d immediately applied, thinking maybe it might help me find Gale.
paras.zh: 希望他终于能把它做成功。”说来好笑；一年前我头回看到那张“招学徒”的告示时，立刻就报了名，心想或许能借此找到风灵。

paras.en: But while the Wind Spirit remained in hiding, I began to fall in love with the work itself.
paras.zh: 可风灵始终躲着不见，我却渐渐爱上了这份工作本身。

paras.en: It gave me something to do and it made me feel like I was an important part of the town.
paras.zh: 它让我有事可做，也让我觉得自己是镇上重要的一分子。

paras.en: Something more than just being the prince’s best friend. “That’s great!” Agnarr exclaimed. “And then maybe Johan will invite you to join him permanently!” He knew this was my greatest dream.
paras.zh: 而不只是王子的好朋友而已。“太棒了！”安格瑞嚷道，“那说不定约翰会正式请你一直留下来跟着他！”他知道那是我最大的梦想。

paras.en: My apprenticeship would end in a few months, along with my formal lessons with Miss Larsen.
paras.zh: 再过几个月，我的学徒期就结束了，和拉森小姐的正式课业也一样。

paras.en: That meant I would be able to take on a full-time role with Johan, if he agreed.
paras.zh: 这意味着只要约翰同意，我就能全职跟着他干了。

paras.en: No longer simply working for “I hope so,” I said. “If not now, then maybe someday.” “You know, I could always put out a royal decree,” Agnarr teased. “I could even make it a law.” I laughed. “Nah.
paras.zh: 不再是只给人当…… “但愿吧，”我说，“就算不是现在，也许总有一天。” “你知道，我随时可以下道王室敕令，”安格瑞逗我，“甚至立成法律都行。”我笑了。“才不。

paras.en: I’d rather earn it on my own,” I told him. “It will mean more that way.” “And you will,” he said fervently. “I know it.
paras.zh: 我宁愿凭自己本事挣来，”我告诉他，“那样才有意义。” “你一定行的，”他热切地说，“我相信。

paras.en: If anyone can do it, you can.” His warm words sent a shiver rippling through me, and I put my hands out to warm them by the fire.
paras.zh: 这世上要是有人能做到，那一定就是你。”他温暖的话让我周身泛起一阵颤栗，我伸出手到火边取暖。

paras.en: Night had begun to fall and with it a chill had crept into the air.
paras.zh: 夜色已开始降临，空气中悄悄渗入一丝寒意。

paras.en: Agnarr hopped to his feet and walked over to the wagon, pulling out his father’s old cloak.
paras.zh: 安格瑞一跃起身，走向马车，拽出他父亲那件旧斗篷。

paras.en: The same one he’d draped over my shoulders the very first time we’d encountered the mist together.
paras.zh: 就是当初我们头一回一起遇见迷雾时，他披在我肩上的那件。

paras.en: He didn’t wear it much anymore, but he liked to bring it along on these journeys for sentimental reasons.
paras.zh: 他如今不太穿它了，却喜欢在旅途上带着，只为念旧。

paras.en: He walked over to me now, draping it over my shoulders. “That better?” he asked. “Much,” I agreed, smiling up at him.
paras.zh: 他走到我面前，把斗篷披在我肩上。“暖和点了？”他问。“好多了，”我笑着仰头看他。

paras.en: Way up.
paras.zh: 仰得老高。”

paras.en: While Agnarr used to be not that much taller than me, he’d shot up in the past couple of years, sprouting broad shoulders and long, lean muscles, seemingly overnight.
paras.zh: 安格瑞过去没比我高多少，这两年却猛地蹿了起来，肩膀变宽，长出修长结实的肌肉，简直像是一夜之间。

paras.en: His hair had darkened, too, though it was still blondish red, and it was longer than the cropped-close-to-his-head style he’d had for a while after the dam tragedy.
paras.zh: 他的发色也深了，虽仍带着点红棕，却比水坝惨剧后有一阵子那种贴着头皮的短发要长。

paras.en: And he had a bit of stubble on his upper lip, as if he wanted to grow a mustache but wasn’t quite ready to commit.
paras.zh: 上唇还冒出点胡茬，像是想留胡子又下不定决心。

paras.en: But for all these changes, his eyes remained the same: as emerald green as the forest itself in the richest months of summer, flecked with blues and yellows that seemed to dance when he smiled.
paras.zh: 可纵有千般变化，他的眼睛没变：仍是盛夏森林最浓郁时那般翡翠般的绿，缀着蓝与黄的点点光斑，一笑便仿佛在起舞。

paras.en: When he smiled at me.
paras.zh: 尤其是他冲我笑的时候。

paras.en: Now this big, strong man-boy shivered noticeably, evidently cold himself.
paras.zh: 如今这个高大强壮的“大男孩”明显打了个寒颤，显然自己也冷了。

paras.en: I opened up the cloak to invite him under it, like I’d done that first time by the mist and every trip since.
paras.zh: 我掀开斗篷，邀他进来，就像第一次在迷雾边以及之后每次出行那样。

paras.en: He grinned. “Scooch in?” he asked, quoting me. “If you can manage it,” I teased as he attempted to fit inside. “Seriously, if you keep growing we’re going to have to bring two cloaks next time.” “Nah,” he said, pulling one end of the cloak over his shoulder, his warm body pressing against mine.
paras.zh: 他咧嘴一笑。“挤一挤？”他学着我的口气问。“看你能不能塞得下，”我一边逗他一边看他往里挪，“说真的，你再长下去，下次我们可得带两件斗篷了。” “才不，”他说着把斗篷一角拉过自己肩头，温热的身体贴着我。

paras.en: His thigh to my thigh.
paras.zh: 他的大腿贴着我的。

paras.en: His arm tucking around my waist.
paras.zh: 他的手臂环住我的腰。

paras.en: My head sinking down onto his shoulder. “See?” he said, his voice dropping lower. “Plenty of room.” “Oh, yes,” I agreed, my tone light even as I ignored my racing pulse. “Plenty.
paras.zh: 我的头靠上他的肩。“瞧见没？”他声音低了下来，“地方宽敞着呢。” “哦，是呀，”我应道，语气轻松，却刻意不去理自己狂跳的脉搏，“宽敞。

paras.en: Perhaps we should invite the horses in, too.
paras.zh: 也许该把马也请进来。

paras.en: And the guards…” He snorted, sighing contentedly as he looked up at the sky. “I love these trips,” he declared. “I wish we could do them every night of the year.
paras.zh: 还有卫兵……”他哼了一声，心满意足地叹着，仰望天空。“我好爱这些旅途，”他说，“真希望一年三百六十五天夜夜都能这样。

paras.en: Sit by a warm fire.
paras.zh: 守着温暖的火。

paras.en: Sleep under the stars.” He nudged me with one arm. “Why did people invent roofs anyway?” “Um, to keep out the rain perhaps?” “Oh.
paras.zh: 睡在星空下。”他拿胳膊肘轻轻碰我。“说起来，人干嘛要发明屋顶啊？”“呃，大概是挡雨吧？”“哦。

paras.en: Right.” He grinned. “You’re such a know-it-all.” He closed his eyes.
paras.zh: 对哦。”他咧嘴一笑。“你真是个万事通。”他闭上眼。

paras.en: I tried not to notice how warm and solid he felt pressed up against me.
paras.zh: 我努力不去在意贴着我时，他身上有多温暖、多结实。

paras.en: Something I was trying and failing at quite a bit these past few months.
paras.zh: 这几个月来，我试了又试，却总也做不到。

paras.en: Which was ridiculous.
paras.zh: 真是荒唐。

paras.en: This is just Agnarr, The goofy boy who can barely manage not to fall out of a tree.
paras.zh: 这不过是安格瑞，那个笨手笨脚、差点在树上摔下来的傻小子。

paras.en: Yet still, when this goofy boy dragged his thumb across my palm, I couldn’t resist a small tremble, my whole body seeming to alight with fire at his simple touch.
paras.zh: 可即便如此，当这个傻小子用拇指掠过我的掌心，我还是忍不住轻轻一抖，整个人像被他轻轻一碰就燃起火来。

paras.en: He noticed, looking down at me with sleepy eyes. “Are you all right?” he asked. “Yep, perfectly fine,” I responded quickly, hoping he couldn’t see my blushing face in the dim light cast by the fire.
paras.zh: 他察觉了，睡眼惺忪地低头看我。“你没事吧？”他问。“嗯，好得很，”我飞快答道，但愿火光昏暗，他看不见我发红的脸。

paras.en: We’d been holding each other’s hands since that very first day in the castle when he dragged me along from room to room while giving me a tour.
paras.zh: 从城堡里头一天起，他就拉着我从这屋走到那屋带我参观，从那时起我们就一直牵着彼此的手。

paras.en: Since that first night out by the mist, when I’d been so lost in my despair.
paras.zh: 从迷雾边那第一夜起，那时我正深陷绝望。

paras.en: His touch had always been comforting, friendly.
paras.zh: 他的触碰向来令人安心、亲切。

paras.en: A promise that everything would be okay.
paras.zh: 像在承诺一切都会好起来。

paras.en: But now?
paras.zh: 可现在呢？

paras.en: It felt different.
paras.zh: 感觉不一样了。

paras.en: A promise, still.
paras.zh: 承诺还在。

paras.en: But maybe of another sort.
paras.zh: 却也许是另一种。

paras.en: I let out a small sigh.
paras.zh: 我轻轻叹了口气。

paras.en: Agnarr suddenly scrambled to his feet, breaking the warm connection between us. “Are you hungry?” he asked. “Thirsty?
paras.zh: 安格瑞忽然跳起身，打破了我俩之间那温热的联结。“饿不饿？”他问，“渴不渴？

paras.en: Cold?
paras.zh: 冷不冷？

paras.en: Hot?” “I’m fine,” I assured him. “Just…a little nervous for tomorrow.
paras.zh: 热不热？” “我挺好，”我向他保证，“只是……对明天有点紧张。

paras.en: As always.” He gave me a sympathetic look, sitting back down, this time across from me, not under the cloak.
paras.zh: 老样子。”他同情地看看我，重新坐下，这次坐在我对面，没钻进斗篷里。

paras.en: He was still close though.
paras.zh: 不过他仍离得很近。

paras.en: Close enough that I could reach out and touch him if I wanted to.
paras.zh: 近得只要我想，伸手就能碰到他。

paras.en: Instead, I buried my hands under the cloak, clasping them together to give them something to do. “I get it,” Agnarr said. “As fun as these trips are, the conclusion is always hard.” I nodded slowly.
paras.zh: 我反倒把双手埋进斗篷下，交握在一起，好让它们有点事做。“我懂，”安格瑞说，“这些旅行再好玩，结尾总叫人难受。”我缓缓点头。

paras.en: Every trip was always the same.
paras.zh: 每次出行都是如此。

paras.en: The buildup, the anticipation.
paras.zh: 铺垫，期待。

paras.en: Only to end in familiar disappointment.
paras.zh: 到头来总是熟悉的失望。

paras.en: The mist was still there, thick and impenetrable as always.
paras.zh: 迷雾还在那儿，一如既往地浓重、不可穿透。

paras.en: I was beginning to think it would remain that way “What would you do if the mist was gone?” I asked him. “The very first thing?” It was an old game—one we indulged in every trip to the mist—and I knew his answer before he spoke it.
paras.zh: 我渐渐觉得它会一直这样…… “要是迷雾散了，你会做什么？”我问他，“第一件事是什么？”这是个老游戏——每次去迷雾我们都玩——答案我没等他说就知道了。

paras.en: But something about the familiarity of it was soothing, quelling the rising uneasiness inside.
paras.zh: 可这种熟稔本身有种安抚的力量，压下了心底升起的惶惶不安。

paras.en: He hugged his knees to his chest, staring into the fire. “First, I’d look for Mattias,” he said. “I know he’s still alive in there.
paras.zh: 他抱着膝盖贴近胸口，盯着火。“首先，我会去找马蒂亚斯，”他说，“我知道他还活着，在那里面。

paras.en: Somewhere.
paras.zh: 在某个地方。

paras.en: After all, he was the best soldier in the land.
paras.zh: 毕竟，他可是全国最棒的士兵。

paras.en: No way was he taken down in battle.” “And when you found him?” I prompted, as I always did. “First I’d give him the biggest hug.
paras.zh: 绝不可能在战斗中被撂倒。”“找到他之后呢？”我像往常那样追问。“首先我要给他个最用力的拥抱。

paras.en: Which he’d hate, of course.
paras.zh: 他肯定讨厌就是了。

paras.en: He’s always saying real soldiers don’t hug.” He grinned. “But he’d like it, deep down.
paras.zh: 他老说真正的士兵不拥抱。”他咧嘴一笑。“可骨子里他会喜欢的。

paras.en: Also, I’d promote him to general of the Arendelle guard.” “Anything else?” Agnarr’s eyes sparkled. “I’d give him all the gossip about Halima down at the village.
paras.zh: 而且，我会提拔他当阿伦黛尔卫队的将军。”“还有别的吗？”安格瑞眼睛发亮。“我要把村里哈利玛的事全讲给他听。

paras.en: He’s crazy about her.
paras.zh: 他可迷她了。

paras.en: He’d want to know everything.” “She’s pretty crazy about him, too, from what I’ve gathered,” I said with a giggle, thinking back to the woman who worked at Hudson’s Hearth, a local eatery where everyone gathered to chat or for one of their famous buttered biscuits.
paras.zh: 什么事他都想知道。”“据我所知，她对他也挺上心的，”我咯咯笑着，想起那个在哈德森炉边小馆干活的女人——那是家本地小馆，大家聚在那儿闲聊，或来份他们有名的黄油饼干。

paras.en: Men were always trying to flirt with her, but she turned them down every time.
paras.zh: 男人们总想跟她调情，可她每次都拒绝。

paras.en: There was only one man for her, she’d declare, even if he was gone forever.
paras.zh: 她总说，这世上只有一个男人配得上她，即便他永远不在了。

paras.en: It was impossibly romantic. “Oh, and one other thing,” Agnarr suddenly added, his eyes shining.
paras.zh: 真是浪漫得不像话。“哦，还有一件事，”安格瑞忽然眼睛一亮，补了一句。

paras.en: I looked up.
paras.zh: 我抬起头。

paras.en: This wasn’t part of our script. “What’s that?” “I’d like to find my rescuer.” Something thudded in my heart. “Your…rescuer?” “You know, the person who saved me.
paras.zh: 这不在我们的剧本里。“什么？”“我想找到我的救命恩人。”我的心猛地一沉。“你……救命恩人？”“你知道的，就是救了我的人。

paras.en: The one who got me to the wagon.
paras.zh: 是把我弄上马车那个人。

paras.en: I bet he or she is still stuck in the mist, too.” “Why do you think that?” “Well, they’d have to be.
paras.zh: 我打赌他或她现在还困在迷雾里。”“你怎么这么想？”“嗯，肯定得是这样。

paras.en: Or they would have come forward “Maybe they believe saving your life was reward enough?” I suggested casually, my heart fluttering at this unfamiliar territory.
paras.zh: 不然他早该站出来了……” “也许他觉得救你一命就是足够的报偿？”我故作随意地试探，踏入这片陌生领地，心里直打鼓。
