paras.en: Had I given off signals that had led Johan to the wrong conclusions?
paras.zh: 难道我流露过什么，让约翰得出错误结论？

paras.en: But no.
paras.zh: 可没有。

paras.en: I had given him an honest day’s work. “Iduna.
paras.zh: 我给过他诚诚实实一天的工。“伊杜娜。

paras.en: Talk to me.” Agnarr’s face was inches from mine. “Are you all right?
paras.zh: 跟我说。”安格瑞的脸离我几寸。“你没事吧？

paras.en: Are you…” His face turned pale. “Are you upset about what happened in the library?
paras.zh: 你……是不是……”他脸色发白。“在为图书馆里的事难过？

paras.en: ’Cause we can talk about it.
paras.zh: 因为我们可以谈谈。

paras.en: If you thought it was a mistake—” I choked out a laugh.
paras.zh: 如果你觉得那是个错误——”我呛出一声笑。

paras.en: And here I had been worrying he was thinking the same thing about me. “No,” I assured him, giving him a sad smile as I laid my hand on his shoulder.
paras.zh: 而我方才还担心他也在这么想我。“不，”我向他保证，把手搭上他肩，苦涩地一笑。

paras.en: It was all I could do not to crawl into his arms, let him hold me.
paras.zh: 我拼命忍住不钻进他怀里，让他抱着我。

paras.en: Tell me everything would be all right.
paras.zh: 告诉我会好起来的。

paras.en: But I had to get this out first. “In fact, the library thing was the good part about this week.” His brows furrowed. “What happened?” “Well, for starters, Johan proposed.” Agnarr’s face turned as white as a ghost’s. “He d-did?” he stammered. “Um, that’s…wow.” He swallowed hard. “What did you say?” “I told him no.
paras.zh: 可我得先把这事说出来。“其实，图书馆那桩，是这周里好的一桩。”他皱起眉。“怎么了？”“嗯，首先，约翰求婚了。”安格瑞脸白得像鬼。“他……他求了？”他结巴，“呃，这……哇。”他狠狠咽唾沫。“你怎么回的？”“我拒绝了他。

paras.en: Obviously,” I snapped, feeling annoyed I even had to answer that question.
paras.zh: 这还用问，”我没好气地说，烦的是连这都要解释。

paras.en: That on some level Agnarr wouldn’t already know.
paras.zh: 仿佛安格瑞本该心里有数。

paras.en: But how could he?
paras.zh: 可他怎么会知道？

paras.en: We’d never talked about these kinds of things.
paras.zh: 这类事我们从未谈过。

paras.en: We’d never even expressed feelings for one another until recently. “Phew.” Agnarr’s face shone with relief. “I mean, he’s totally wrong for you,” he added hastily when I gave him a look.
paras.zh: 直到最近，我们连心意都没表露过。“呼。”安格瑞一脸 relief。“我的意思是，他跟你完全不配，”见我瞪他，他连忙补道。

paras.en: I swallowed down a bitter laugh.
paras.zh: 我把一声苦笑咽了下去。

paras.en: Wrong for me.
paras.zh: 不配。

paras.en: It was Agnarr who was wrong for me.
paras.zh: 不配的是安格瑞。

paras.en: The one unattached man in Arendelle I could never have.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔那个我永远得不到的未婚男人。

paras.en: The only one I wanted.
paras.zh: 也是我唯一想要的。

paras.en: In the end they only marry their own kind.
paras.zh: 到头来，他们只娶自己人。

paras.en: I closed my eyes, trying to reset my sanity. “Anyway, when I said no to his proposal, he basically fired me.
paras.zh: 我闭上眼，想把自己拉回理智。“总之，我拒绝求婚后，他基本就把我炒了。

paras.en: Which means I’m not going to get to work on windmills anymore.” “What?” Agnarr looked horrified. “He can’t do that!” “He already has.” Suddenly I felt a million years old. “Well, he has to rehire you then.
paras.zh: 也就是说，我不能再造风车了。”“什么？”安格瑞一脸惊恐。“他不能这么干！”“他已经干了。”忽然间我觉得自己老了一百万岁。“那他得重新雇你。

paras.en: That’s illegal.
paras.zh: 这是非法的。

paras.en: Or it should be, if it’s not.
paras.zh: 就算现在不是，也能让它变成非法。

paras.en: I can make it illegal.
paras.zh: 我可以立这条法。

paras.en: I could send over some guards to talk to him.
paras.zh: 我可以派几个卫兵去跟他谈谈。

paras.en: I could…put him in jail even.
paras.zh: 我甚至……可以把他关起来。

paras.en: I mean, unjust firing of perfectly qualified apprentices who simply aren’t into marriage…or something?
paras.zh: 我是说，无端解雇完全合格、只是不想结婚的学徒……总该算某种罪吧？

paras.en: That has to be a crime of some sort.” I couldn’t help a small smile at this.
paras.zh: 这说法让我忍不住微微一笑。

paras.en: His outrage on my behalf made me feel better.
paras.zh: 他为我发的火，让我好受了些。

paras.en: Even if I didn’t want him to follow through with any of it. “Thank you,” I said. “I appreciate the support.
paras.zh: 即便我并不想他真去实行任何一条。“谢谢你，”我说，“谢谢你的支持。

paras.en: But I’d prefer to deal with this myself.
paras.zh: 可我宁愿自己处理。

paras.en: It’s my problem, not yours.” “I know, but…” His shoulders slumped in defeat. “I want to help you.” “And I love that you do.
paras.zh: 这是我的问题，不是你的。” “我知道，可是……”他肩膀一垮，泄了气。“我想帮你。” “我喜欢你这份心。

paras.en: But I’m not some damsel in distress from one of your books.
paras.zh: 可我不是你书里那种等着被救的落难少女。

paras.en: I have always taken care of myself.
paras.zh: 我一向自己顾自己。

paras.en: And I will take care of this, too.” “I understand,” he said.
paras.zh: 这桩我也自己顾。”“我明白，”他说。

paras.en: And my heart swelled at the acceptance on his face.
paras.zh: 他脸上那份接纳，让我心里一暖。

paras.en: He wanted to help.
paras.zh: 他想帮忙。

paras.en: But he was also willing to step back and let me do it my way.
paras.zh: 却也愿意退后，让我用自己的方式。

paras.en: He wouldn’t force me or guilt me into something I didn’t want.
paras.zh: 他不会逼我，也不会用愧疚拿捏我。

paras.en: All he wanted was for me to be happy.
paras.zh: 他只要我开心。

paras.en: And he would do anything, I knew, to make it so—even if that meant doing nothing at all. “Isn’t there anything I can do for you?” he asked softly.
paras.zh: 而我知道，为了让我开心，他什么都肯做——哪怕那意味着什么都不做。“难道我就不能为你做点什么？”他柔声问。

paras.en: He reached out, brushing a lock of hair from my face.
paras.zh: 他伸手，拂开我脸上的一缕发。

paras.en: His eyes were tender, kind. “What do you need, Iduna?” My emotions flooded my heart at his simple words.
paras.zh: 他的眼神温柔、和善。“你需要什么，伊杜娜？”这简单一句话，情绪涌满我心。

paras.en: And suddenly I realized there was only one thing I needed.
paras.zh: 我忽然明白，我需要的只有一件事。

paras.en: The one thing I should not ask for.
paras.zh: 那件我不该开口要的事。

paras.en: The one thing I wasn’t sure I could live without. “I need you,” I whispered. “Just you.” His breath caught in his throat.
paras.zh: 那件我不知能否离得开的事。“我需要你，”我低语，“只要是你。”他的呼吸堵在喉间。

paras.en: For a moment, he just looked at me.
paras.zh: 有那么一刻，他只是看着我。

paras.en: Just looked and looked and looked until time itself And then he kissed me.
paras.zh: 只是看啊看啊，直到时间本身……然后他吻了我。

paras.en: It didn’t begin gently this time, like the kiss we’d shared in the secret room.
paras.zh: 这一次不像密室里那个吻，起初轻柔。

paras.en: Instead, it felt desperate in its intensity.
paras.zh: 反而带着近乎绝望的热度。

paras.en: And as he dug his hands deep into my hair, heat rose inside me, until I felt as if I would literally burst into flames. “Agnarr,” I whispered, my mouth against his. “Iduna…” I don’t know how long we kissed in that tree.
paras.zh: 当他双手深深插进我的发，一股热流在我体内升腾，仿佛我真的要燃成火焰。“安格瑞，”我贴着他的唇低语，“伊杜娜……”不知我们在树上吻了多久。

paras.en: It could have been hours, years, minutes, or only a few blissful seconds.
paras.zh: 也许是几小时、几年、几分钟，或只是几秒销魂。

paras.en: But when we finally pulled apart, flushed and breathless, we looked each other in the eyes, no longer bashful.
paras.zh: 可当我们终于分开，满脸通红、喘着气，彼此对望，不再羞怯。

paras.en: As if nothing in the world mattered outside that tree.
paras.zh: 仿佛这世界除树外再无他物。

paras.en: No past, no potential future.
paras.zh: 没有过去，没有可能的未来。

paras.en: Nothing could steal this moment away from the two of us. “I love you,” he whispered.
paras.zh: 没有什么能夺走我俩这一刻。“我爱你，”他低语。

paras.en: So softly at first that I was half convinced I was making it up in my head.
paras.zh: 起初那么轻，我几乎以为自己脑中虚构。

paras.en: But then his voice rose.
paras.zh: 可随后他的声音扬起。

paras.en: More confident.
paras.zh: 更笃定。

paras.en: The voice of a boy who would soon be king. “I’ve always “I love you, too,” I replied, my voice so croaky that I wondered if he could even understand me.
paras.zh: 一个即将为王的男孩的声音。“我向来 “我也爱你，”我答，嗓子哑得不知他听不听得清。

paras.en: My admission wasn’t perfect, but there it was, all the same: vulnerable and true.
paras.zh: 我的表白不算完美，却一样在那里：脆弱而真实。

paras.en: My heart was his for the taking whether I liked it or not.
paras.zh: 我的心交给他任取，由不得我。

paras.en: I reached out and slipped my hand in his and squeezed it hard.
paras.zh: 我伸出手，滑进他的，用力一握。

paras.en: His hands were soft, not rough and calloused.
paras.zh: 他的手柔软，不粗糙、不长茧。

paras.en: But that didn’t mean they weren’t strong and fully capable. “Since…the day we first climbed this tree.” It wasn’t what I wanted to say, of course.
paras.zh: 可这不意味着它们不强健、不能担事。“从……我们头回爬这棵树那天起。”当然，这不是我想说的话。

paras.en: I wanted to tell him I’d loved him far longer.
paras.zh: 我想告诉他，我爱他久得多。

paras.en: Since that very first day he arrived in the Enchanted Forest.
paras.zh: 从他初到魔法森林那天起。

paras.en: When I’d seen the wonder in his eyes as he stroked the baby reindeer.
paras.zh: 从他抚摸小驯鹿时，我看见他眼里的惊奇。

paras.en: When his father yelled at him and I watched his narrow shoulders slump and his head bow in shame.
paras.zh: 从他父亲吼他，我看见他窄肩塌下、低头含羞。

paras.en: When he lay bleeding on the ground and I made the choice to save him—instead of myself.
paras.zh: 从他躺在地上流血，而我选择救他——而非自己。

paras.en: But I couldn’t say any of that.
paras.zh: 可这些我说不出口。

paras.en: Not now at least.
paras.zh: 至少现在不行。

paras.en: Not while everything was so fragile, so new.
paras.zh: 趁一切还这么脆、这么新。

paras.en: I knew in my heart this I smiled at the prince.
paras.zh: 我心里知道这一点的——我冲王子笑了。

paras.en: He smiled back at me, looking pretty pleased with himself.
paras.zh: 他回我一笑，一副自得样。

paras.en: Agnarr. “If only we could do this forever,” I said with a happy sigh. “We can!” he declared. “In fact, I’ll make a royal proclamation.
paras.zh: 安格瑞。“要是我们能永远这样多好，”我幸福地叹道。“我们能！”他宣告，“事实上，我要发布一道王室公告。

paras.en: Kissing no longer has to have any time limits whatsoever!” I giggled. “There are no time limits now!” His eyes met mine.
paras.zh: 亲吻从此再不限时！”我咯咯笑。“现在本就不限好吗！”他与我对视。

paras.en: They were soft and dreamy, a likely reflection of my own. “Then why can’t we do this forever?” he whispered.
paras.zh: 他的眼神温柔迷离，大概正映着我自己的。“那为何我们不能永远这样？”他低语。

paras.en: I could have offered up a million practical reasons.
paras.zh: 我本可以列出一百万条现实的理由。

paras.en: Instead, I kissed him again.
paras.zh: 可我转而，又吻了他。

paras.en: “‘AND SO THE ARENDELLIANS SETTLED DOWN on the grassy, green banks of what would henceforth be known as Arenfjord.’” A giggle escaped me, and Miss Larsen looked up from her history text, eyeing us with a suspicious expression.
paras.zh: “‘于是阿伦黛尔人便在青草茵茵的河岸定居下来，那地方从此被称为阿伦峡湾。’”我忍不住笑出声，拉森小姐从史书里抬起头，狐疑地瞅我们。

paras.en: Agnarr’s face grew wide and innocent as I bit my lower lip to stop from laughing, giving the prince a scolding look.
paras.zh: 我咬着下唇忍笑，朝王子递去一个责备的眼神，安格瑞却露出一脸无辜的夸张表情。

paras.en: How was I supposed to pay attention to our history lessons if he kept reaching under the table, grazing my knee with his hand and sending shivers straight up my spine?
paras.zh: 他老把手伸到桌下，擦过我的膝，惹得一阵战栗直窜我脊背，我怎么能专心听历史课？

paras.en: Good shivers, but still! “Is something amusing, Miss Iduna?” Miss Larsen asked pointedly. “No, ma’am,” I assured her. “I was just…thinking of something.” “Next class, let’s try to keep your concentration on learning, shall we?” Miss Larsen asked.
paras.zh: 是好意的战栗，可也够呛！“有什么好笑的，伊杜娜小姐？”拉森小姐咄咄地问。“没有，女士，”我向她保证，“我只是……想到点事。” “下节课，咱们试着把心思放在学习上，好吗？”拉森小姐说。

paras.en: I nodded as I gathered my things and headed for the secret library, knowing Agnarr was not far behind.
paras.zh: 我点点头，收拾东西朝密室图书馆去，知道安格瑞就在身后不远。

paras.en: In fact, over the past few months I had found it almost impossible to concentrate on anything but Agnarr and our secret romance.
paras.zh: 事实上，过去这几个月，我几乎没法把心思放在安格瑞和我们的秘密恋情之外任何事上。

paras.en: (Well, that and keeping it secret.) We still spent The secret room in the library had become our most frequented spot, both because it was so tucked away and because it was the place where we’d first given in to the rushes of feeling flooding through us.
paras.zh: （嗯，除了守住秘密。）我们仍常去——图书馆里的密室成了我们最常去的地方，既因它够隐蔽，也因那是我们头一回任凭汹涌情感将彼此淹没之处。

paras.en: We’d turned the room into our own special hideaway, with Agnarr reading aloud from various books or scrolls he’d uncovered while I painted stars on the ceiling with paint that seemed to glow in the dark.
paras.zh: 我们把那间屋变成了专属的小天地：安格瑞大声念他翻出的各种书卷，我则用仿佛会在暗处发光的颜料，在天花板上画星星。

paras.en: When I had finished, we lay on the floor, staring up at the vast sky, hands linked, as if we were on one of our mist trips.
paras.zh: 画完，我们躺在地板上，手牵着手仰望那片“星空”，像在迷雾之旅中一般。

paras.en: But as magical as these moments were, I still had to deal with real life.
paras.zh: 可尽管这些时刻如魔法，我仍得面对真实人生。

paras.en: Like what was I going to do to earn a living now that I was no longer an apprentice.
paras.zh: 比如，我不再是学徒了，靠什么谋生？

paras.en: Agnarr tapped his finger to his chin, considering the options. “What if you started your own windmill business?
paras.zh: 安格瑞指节抵着下巴，盘算起来。“要不你自个儿开家风车行？

paras.en: Give Johan a little competition.” “That would great,” I said with a chuckle. “But how would I start a business?
paras.zh: 给约翰点竞争。” “那敢情好，”我笑着说，“可我怎么开得起？

paras.en: No one’s going to invest in a sixteen-year-old girl.” “ I I groaned. “For the last time, I’m not taking your money, Agnarr.” “I don’t see why not.
paras.zh: 没人会投资一个十六岁姑娘。” “我”我直哼。“我再说最后一次，安格瑞，我不拿你的钱。”

paras.en: I have more than enough to spare.
paras.zh: 我闲钱多的是。

paras.en: Also, you’re a good investment.
paras.zh: 再说，你是笔好投资。

paras.en: I know you’d pay me back.” I kissed him in the space between his ear and collarbone, the place I knew always made him shiver. “Agnarr.
paras.zh: 我知道你会还我。”我吻在他耳与锁骨之间——那个我知道总让他发颤的地方。“安格瑞。

paras.en: I appreciate your faith in me.
paras.zh: 谢谢你对我的信心。

paras.en: But this is something I have to do on my own.” “Oh, fine.” He sat up and ran his hand through his hair. “So you don’t have money.
paras.zh: 可这事我得自己来。”“哦，行吧。”他坐起身，手梳过头发。“那你没钱。

paras.en: What do I scrunched up my nose. “Knowledge?
paras.zh: 那怎么办——”我皱起鼻子。“凭本事？

paras.en: I mean, I know how to build a windmill.
paras.zh: 我是说，我会造风车。

paras.en: I just don’t have the money to buy the supplies to do it.” “That’s it!” Agnarr cried, pointing at me. “I got it!” “What?” “You can be a teacher.” “A teacher?
paras.zh: 只是没钱买材料动手。” “这就对了！”安格瑞指着我叫，“我有了！” “什么？” “你可以当老师。” “老师？

paras.en: Like Miss Larsen?” He shook his head. “What I’m thinking is something a little more specialized.” “What do you mean?” “You told me Johan actually constructs these windmills on farmers’ lands, right?
paras.zh: 像拉森小姐那样？”他摇头。“我想的是更专门一点的。”“什么意思？”“你说过，约翰其实是去农夫的地里实地造风车，对吧？

paras.en: Well, what if they want to save money by just paying for the knowledge of how to build them and actually doing the construction themselves?” My eyes widened. “Oh!” “You could teach them, right?
paras.zh: 那万一他们想省钱，只花钱买‘怎么造’的本事，自己动手造呢？”我眼睛一亮。“哦！”“你能教他们，对吧？

paras.en: You’d provide the expertise and the building plans, for a reasonable fee.
paras.zh: 你出技术和图纸，收合理的费用。

paras.en: And they’d gather all the materials and labor.” “That’s…not a bad idea,” I said, trying to organize the thoughts whirling through my head. “This way people wouldn’t have to sacrifice half their life savings to get a windmill.” “And you’re such a good teacher,” Agnarr said. “You’re so patient with everyone.
paras.zh: 材料劳力全由他们自己凑。” “这……不坏，”我说，努力理顺脑中乱转的念头，“这样人们不必搭进半生积蓄就能得到风车。” “而且你是个好老师，”安格瑞说，“对谁都那么有耐心。

paras.en: Even me!” “ Especially “So, what do you think?” he asked. “I think you’re brilliant,” I declared. “But don’t let it go to your head.” He smiled. “There’s only one thing in my head right now, Iduna.” He lowered his mouth so his lips were right against mine. “And she’s going to make a terrific teacher.”
paras.zh: 连我都是！” “尤其——“那么，你觉得呢？”他问。“我觉得你聪明绝顶，”我宣称，“可别飘了。”他笑了。“此刻我脑子里只有一件事，伊杜娜。”他低下头，嘴唇贴着我的。“而她，会是一位出色的老师。”

chapters.title: Chapter Eighteen: Iduna: Six Weeks Later

paras.en: “ALL RIGHT, SO YOU HAVE SOME CHOICES here.
paras.zh: “好吧，你这儿有几种选择。

paras.en: You can just build your basic windmill—which will require fewer materials and is less labor intensive.
paras.zh: 可以只造基本款风车——用料少，也省力。

paras.en: Or you can add a roundhouse to the design.
paras.zh: 或者在设计上加个圆仓。

paras.en: This will cost more up front as it requires a lot more lumber.
paras.zh: 这样前期花费更高，因为要多用不少木料。

paras.en: However, you’ll gain a covered storage area for your grain or farm tools.” “Hm.
paras.zh: 不过，你会多出一个有顶的储物间，放谷物或农具。”“嗯。

paras.en: What do you suggest?” asked Mr.
paras.zh: 你建议哪种？”汉森先生

paras.en: Hansen, studying the plans that I’d sketched and laid out before him. “I don’t want to waste any money, but…” “A roundhouse will also protect your trestle—that’s basically the legs of the windmill—from bad weather,” I told him. “Which, we tend to have a lot of around here.
paras.zh: 盯着我摊在他面前、由我手绘的图纸问。“我不想浪费钱，可是……” “圆仓还能护住你的支架——就是风车的‘腿’——免遭坏天气，”我告诉他，“而这儿，坏天气可不少见。

paras.en: If you can afford it, I would definitely recommend it.” Mr.
paras.zh: 若力所能及，我一定推荐。”汉森先生

paras.en: Hansen looked up. “Well then, let’s go with that!” I smiled, rolling up the plans and putting out my hand.
paras.zh: 抬起头。“那好，就照这个！”我笑着卷起图纸，伸出手。

paras.en: He shook it with a firm grip. “Great,” I said. “I’ll revise these to include the roundhouse and get them back to you first thing tomorrow.
paras.zh: 他用力一握。“太好了，”我说，“我把圆仓加进去改好，明早头一件事就给你。

paras.en: Sound good?” “Fantastic.
paras.zh: 行吗？”“棒极了。

paras.en: This is going to save me a fortune from what I was going to pay Johan.
paras.zh: 这可比我原打算付给约翰的省下一大笔。

paras.en: And I don’t mind doing the work myself.
paras.zh: 而且活儿我自己干，不介意。

paras.en: I “Thank you “Oh, you better believe I will,” he declared. “I’ll sing your praises in the pub tonight.
paras.zh: 我“谢谢你“哦，这你放心，”他宣告，“今晚酒馆里我准替你美言。

paras.en: By morning, you’ll have more business than you can handle.” “Don’t worry.
paras.zh: 到明早，你接的活儿只怕忙不过来。”“别担心。

paras.en: I can handle quite a bit,” I assured him. “Thank you again.
paras.zh: 我挺能扛的，”我向他保证，“再次谢谢你。

paras.en: I’ll see you tomorrow.” And with that, I headed back down the hill, whistling cheerfully.
paras.zh: 明天见。”说罢，我吹着欢快的口哨下山。

paras.en: It was a beautiful day.
paras.zh: 天气真好。

paras.en: I was once again gainfully employed.
paras.zh: 我又有了正经活计。

paras.en: Self I still couldn’t believe how much fun I’d been having over the past few weeks.
paras.zh: 自——我仍不敢信，这几个星期我过得有多快活。

paras.en: It was hard work—yes.
paras.zh: 活儿是累——没错。

paras.en: And at the end of the day, I was exhausted.
paras.zh: 一天下来，筋疲力尽。

paras.en: But I was earning money every day, and I’d already raised almost enough to rent my own place.
paras.zh: 可我天天在挣钱，攒的已差不多够租个自己的屋。

paras.en: My own little home in the village—it sounded like a dream come true.
paras.zh: 村里属于自己的小窝——听起来像美梦成真。

paras.en: And Agnarr had been so encouraging.
paras.zh: 而安格瑞一直那么鼓舞我。

paras.en: Sure, he was busy, too—with all the council meetings and his royal duties.
paras.zh: 当然，他也忙——议会会议、王室职责不断。

paras.en: But he never missed a chance to meet me at the end of the day in our secret room in the library.
paras.zh: 可他从不放过一天结束时来图书馆密室见我的机会。

paras.en: We would curl up in one another’s arms, utterly spent from our very different days, and he’d make me tell him everything—even the boring stuff.
paras.zh: 我们相拥蜷着，各自熬过截然不同的白天、筋疲力尽，他非要我把一切都讲给他听——连无聊的琐事。

paras.en: And he’d act interested in all of it.
paras.zh: 而且每样他都装得津津有味。

paras.en: I reached the bridge that led into Arendelle, waving at a few people as I crossed.
paras.zh: 我走到通往阿伦黛尔的桥上，过桥时朝几个人挥手。

paras.en: My mind wandered to the first day I’d come to the town, still but a girl, frightened and alone.
paras.zh: 思绪飘回初来镇上的那天，我还是个惊恐孤独的女孩。

paras.en: The walls had seemed so tall and imposing then.
paras.zh: 那时城墙显得那么高、那么威严。

paras.en: The streets so narrow and tight.
paras.zh: 街道那么窄、那么挤。

paras.en: I couldn’t imagine, at the time, living in a place like this.
paras.zh: 那时我无法想象，会住在这样的地方。

paras.en: But now, it felt like home.
paras.zh: 可如今，这里像家。

paras.en: It would never replace the forest I grew up in.
paras.zh: 它永远替代不了我长大的森林。

paras.en: I still mourned my old life and family and all I had lost that day.
paras.zh: 我仍哀悼旧日的生活、家人，和那天失去的一切。

paras.en: But it had been so long now, that life had begun to feel almost like a dream.
paras.zh: 可时日已久，那段生活已开始像一场梦。

paras.en: A beautiful dream of an enchanted forest, with magical spirits and a family that loved me.
paras.zh: 一场魔法森林、魔法精灵与爱我的家人的美梦。

paras.en: There was a time when I truly believed I would die if I could I just hoped, somehow, Agnarr could be a part of that future, too.
paras.zh: 曾有一度，我真切相信自己若不能……我只盼着，无论如何，安格瑞也能成为那未来的一部分。

paras.en: “I WAS MINDING MY OWN BUSINESS!” declared Mrs.
paras.zh: “我不过是各忙各的！”奥尔森夫人

paras.en: Olsen, a local fishing boater sporting a ropy silver braid that trailed down her back. “Sitting in my boat, sewing up my nets for the next day’s haul.
paras.zh: 宣称——她是本地渔家，拖着一条长长的银色发辫垂到背后。“坐在船上，缝补明天要用的网。

paras.en: When all of a sudden, I felt like I couldn’t breathe!
paras.zh: 忽然之间，我觉得喘不上气！

paras.en: It was as if I had a noose tied around my neck.
paras.zh: 像脖子上套了根绞索。

paras.en: But when I reached up to try to remove it, there was nothing there!” She shook her head. “I’ve been too afraid to get on my boat ever since.” I nodded along, careful to keep my expression neutral from my seat on the dais in the Great Hall, as she continued with her tirade.
paras.zh: 可我伸手去解，却什么也没有！”她摇着头。“从那以后，我怕得再不敢上船。”我在大厅高台上坐着，努力保持神情中立，听她接着发牢骚，只管点头附和。

paras.en: The Tuesday petitioner session—where the people of Arendelle would come to air their grievances to the crown and ask for help or advice—often proved to be a difficult balancing act for me.
paras.zh: 周二的陈情会——阿伦黛尔的百姓来向王室诉说委屈、求援或求建议——于我常是难把握的平衡。

paras.en: As their would-be ruler, I needed to act concerned and sympathetic, but at the same time impartial.
paras.zh: 身为未来的君主，我既要显得关切、同情，又要保持公正。

paras.en: Sometimes it was hard to keep a straight face, while at other times it was hard not to rush over to them with a hug and comforting words.
paras.zh: 有时难绷住脸，有时又难忍住不冲过去拥抱、说些安慰的话。

paras.en: Some of their complaints were petty, like the neighbor’s goat had eaten their prize tulips.
paras.zh: 有些牢骚鸡毛蒜皮，比如邻居的山羊啃了心爱的郁金香。

paras.en: Others, though, were truly heartbreaking: like the one from a woman whose husband had A shepherd named Aksel stood to echo Mrs.
paras.zh: 可也有真正心碎的：比如那位丈夫……一个叫阿克塞尔的牧羊人站起来附和奥尔森夫人。

paras.en: Olsen. “I’ve always kept a herd of sheep grazing in the hills,” he began. “Never had a single problem keeping them there.
paras.zh: “我一向把羊群放在山上吃草，”他开口，“从没出过半点岔子。

paras.en: But yesterday I went up to check on them?
paras.zh: 可昨天我上山去看？

paras.en: And they had all turned purple!” “Purple?” I frowned. “What do you mean, purple?” “I mean, purple!
paras.zh: 它们全变紫了！”“紫了？”我皱眉。“什么意思，紫了？”“就是紫了！

paras.en: Day before their wool was as white as the driven snow.
paras.zh: 前一天毛还白得像雪。

paras.en: Now it’s bright purple!
paras.zh: 现在通体亮紫！

paras.en: They’re acting spooked, too.
paras.zh: 它们还吓得不轻。

paras.en: I’m sure they’re under some kind of evil spell.” “It’s the spirits,” declared Gunnar, our town’s new blacksmith, who had been standing near the back of the room.
paras.zh: 准是中了什么邪咒。” “是精灵，”镇上新建的铁匠古纳尔宣称——他一直站在屋后。“就是水坝那天的那伙。

paras.en: He’d only arrived a month ago and had been a troublemaker ever since, stirring up the crowds with his constant talk of evil spirits. “The same ones from the day at the dam.
paras.zh: 他一个月前才来，从此尽惹事，老拿恶灵说事煽动人群。“和那天水坝上的是一伙。

paras.en: They’re toying with us now.
paras.zh: 他们现在拿我们寻开心。

paras.en: But mark my words, soon they’ll come down from the hills.
paras.zh: 可记着我这话，很快他们就会从山上下来。

paras.en: They will attack Arendelle with their black magic.
paras.zh: 会用黑魔法攻打阿伦黛尔。

paras.en: We must be ready for them.” I groaned under my breath.
paras.zh: 我们必须有所防备。”我压着嗓子哼了一声。

paras.en: Not again. “Has anyone actually seen a spirit?” I cut in, my tone brusque. “In Arendelle, I mean, or anywhere nearby?” I turned to Aksel. “Did you see any by your sheep?
paras.zh: 又来了。“真有人见过精灵吗？”我插话，语气生硬，“我是说，在阿伦黛尔，或附近？”我转向阿克塞尔。“你羊旁边看见过？

paras.en: Or, Mrs.
paras.zh: 还是，奥尔森夫人

paras.en: Olsen, by your boat?
paras.zh: 你船边？

paras.en: Has anyone seen a single spirit in real life, ever?” Everyone shrugged noncommittally, looking down at their feet. “Could it be possible that something else is causing the problems then?
paras.zh: 有人真在现实里见过哪怕一个精灵吗？”众人含糊地耸肩，低头看脚。“那有没有可能，是别的东西惹的祸？

paras.en: Something non-magical in nature?” I asked. “Mrs.
paras.zh: 某种非魔法的原因？”我问。“奥尔森夫人

paras.en: Olsen, have you been checked by a doctor lately?
paras.zh: 你最近看过医生吗？

paras.en: The pollen is fierce this spring.
paras.zh: 今年春天花粉厉害。

paras.en: Maybe you had an allergy attack.
paras.zh: 说不定你是过敏发作。

paras.en: And, Aksel, could one of the shepherds from a neighboring town be jealous of your prizewinning wool—and hoped to gain advantage by dyeing your sheep when you weren’t looking?” “So, you’re saying you don’t believe us?” Gunnar asked. “That the crown won’t even investigate these extremely valid concerns, as odd as they may seem to you?” The room erupted in angry chatter.
paras.zh: 还有，阿克塞尔，会不会邻镇哪个牧羊人眼红你得奖的羊毛——趁你没看见，把羊染了色讨好自己？” “所以你是说，你不信我们？”古纳尔问，“说王室连调查这些虽怪却合理的担忧都不肯？”屋里顿时炸开愤怒的议论。

paras.en: Frustration flared through me. “No, what I’m saying is—” Lord Peterssen rose to his feet, placing a stilling hand on my shoulder. “Of course Prince Agnarr believes you,” he said. “And no matter who or what is behind these acts, they must stop immediately.
paras.zh: 一股烦躁窜过我。“不，我是说——”彼得森大人起身，按住我肩让我稍安。“安格瑞王子当然信你们，”他说，“无论背后是谁、是什么，都必须立刻停止。

paras.en: We will double our patrols, both in town and in the hills.
paras.zh: 我们会加倍巡逻，镇上和山上都不例外。

paras.en: If we find any suspicious individuals, or, uh, spirits skulking around, we will track them down and bring them in to face the law.” There were a few grunts from the crowd, but most did not seem appeased.
paras.zh: 若发现任何可疑人物，或，呃，精灵鬼鬼祟祟，我们就追查到底，送交法办。”人群里几声咕哝，多半却未平息。

paras.en: What did they want us to do?
paras.zh: 他们要我们怎样？

paras.en: This supposed enemy had never been seen.
paras.zh: 这假想之敌从没人见过。

paras.en: How were we to guard against magical spirits? “I think that’s enough for today,” Peterssen added, his voice rising above the din. “We will reconvene next week to hear any new grievances.
paras.zh: 我们怎么防备魔法精灵？“我想今天到此为止，”彼得森压过嘈杂，补了一句，“下周我们再聚，听新的诉苦。

paras.en: For now, please join us for refreshments in the Second Great Hall.” The mood of the crowd lightened immediately at this, all evil spirits forgotten, and they quickly evacuated the throne room to get themselves some treats.
paras.zh: 现在请各位移步第二大厅用茶点。”人群情绪立刻转好，恶灵全抛脑后，迅速撤出王座厅去寻吃的。

paras.en: Peterssen watched them file out, not saying a word.
paras.zh: 彼得森一言不发，看他们鱼贯而出。

paras.en: When at last they were all gone, I turned to him. “What is it with everyone and the spirits?” I asked, my tone unusually short with my closest advisor. “We haven’t seen any evidence of them since the mist rolled in.
paras.zh: 等终于走空，我才转向他。“大家怎么都跟精灵过不去？”我问，对最亲近的顾问语气也难得地冲。“迷雾涌来后，我们再没见过精灵的影子。

paras.en: Why does everything get blamed on them still?” Peterssen patted my shoulder. “People will always need something to blame for their troubles,” he explained. “And magical spirits are an easy target—since they can’t exactly defend themselves.
paras.zh: 为何凡事仍都怪到它们头上？”彼得森拍拍我肩。“人总得找个东西，为不顺心的事背锅，”他解释，“而魔法精灵是好靶子——反正它们没法替自己辩解。

paras.en: Also, to be frank, Agnarr, the people are just following the precedent set by your father.
paras.zh: 再者，坦白说，安格瑞，百姓不过是沿了你父亲立下的先例。

paras.en: Whenever something bad happened in Arendelle, he’d blame it on magic or evil spirits.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔一出坏事，他就怪魔法或恶灵。

paras.en: I don’t know if he truly believed it, or felt it was easier than taking responsibility.
paras.zh: 我不知道他真信，还是觉得比担责任省事。

paras.en: But I’m sure the people A distant memory floated into my consciousness. “He blamed them for my mother,” I said.
paras.zh: 但我敢说百姓……”一段遥远的记忆浮上心头。“他为了我母亲怪它们，”我说。

paras.en: I hadn’t thought of that moment in ages.
paras.zh: 那时刻我已多年没想起。

paras.en: But now it seemed clear as day.
paras.zh: 可此刻清晰如白昼。

paras.en: Me, age five, playing with a wooden horse in my bedroom.
paras.zh: 五岁的我，在卧室玩木马。

paras.en: My father’s hulking shape, standing silhouetted in the doorway.
paras.zh: 父亲魁梧的身影，立在门口，成了剪影。

paras.en: I looked up, startled.
paras.zh: 我抬头，吓了一跳。

paras.en: He’d cleared his throat before speaking.
paras.zh: 他开口前先清了清嗓。

paras.en: Agnarr, your mother is gone.
paras.zh: 安格瑞，你母亲不在了。

paras.en: She was taken by evil spirits.
paras.zh: 她被恶灵带走了。

paras.en: And she’s likely not coming back.
paras.zh: 多半不会回来了。

paras.en: I hadn’t been able to sleep for a week after that.
paras.zh: 那之后我整整一周睡不着。

paras.en: I kept looking for her during the day, praying the spirits would see fit to bring her back.
paras.zh: 白天我总寻她，祈祷精灵发发善心把她送回。

paras.en: At night, I lay awake, trembling with fear, imagining every shadow was an evil presence, lurking and waiting to take me away, too.
paras.zh: 夜里我睁眼躺着，怕得发抖，想象每个影子都是恶物，潜伏着等把我也要走。

paras.en: But no spirits came.
paras.zh: 可没有精灵来。

paras.en: And my mother never returned. “Yes.” Peterssen nodded thoughtfully. “That was likely an easier story for him to accept than the alternative.” “Which was…?” My heart pounded.
paras.zh: 我母亲也再没回来。“是的，”彼得森若有所思地点头，“对他而言，那大概比另一种说法更易接受。” “哪一种……？”我心怦怦跳。

paras.en: Was I finally going to be told some truth about my mother?
paras.zh: 我终于要听到关于母亲的真相了吗？

paras.en: If she hadn’t been taken by spirits, that meant she could still be out there, somewhere.
paras.zh: 若她不是被精灵带走，那意味着她可能还在某处。

paras.en: She could still be alive.
paras.zh: 可能还活着。

paras.en: But Peterssen only waved a hand. “I don’t know, Agnarr,” he said.
paras.zh: 可彼得森只摆摆手。“我不知道，安格瑞，”他说。

paras.en: But I could tell by his eyes that he did.
paras.zh: 可我从他眼里看得出，他知道。

paras.en: Or at least he knew something, if not the full extent of the story.
paras.zh: 至少他知道些，即便不是全貌。

paras.en: More secrets.
paras.zh: 又是秘密。

paras.en: Would I die buried in secrets?
paras.zh: 我会不会带着满身秘密入土？

paras.en: I shook my head, forcing myself back on task.
paras.zh: 我摇头，逼自己回到正事。

paras.en: My mother could wait for another day. “So, what do we do?” I asked. “We can’t very well fight against an imaginary force!” “No.
paras.zh: 母亲的事可以再等一天。“那么，我们怎么办？”我问，“总不能跟一团想象中的力量打仗！” “不能。

paras.en: But we can I sighed.
paras.zh: 但我们可以——”我叹气。

paras.en: Ruling a kingdom was turning out to be a lot more difficult than I had imagined.
paras.zh: 治理王国，比我想象的难得多。

paras.en: No wonder my father had always been in such a grumpy mood.
paras.zh: 难怪父亲总那么暴躁。

paras.en: I wanted to do the right thing for Arendelle.
paras.zh: 我想为阿伦黛尔做正确的事。

paras.en: But what that was, I wasn’t sure.
paras.zh: 可那是什么，我不确定。

paras.en: I rose from my seat and started toward the exit.
paras.zh: 我从座上起身，朝出口走。

paras.en: I was meant to meet Iduna in the village and I was already late.
paras.zh: 我本该在村里见伊杜娜，已经迟了。

paras.en: It was a big Before I could get very far, however, Peterssen called to me. “Agnarr?” He shifted from foot to foot, suddenly looking nervous “There is…one thing you could do to satisfy the people.” “Really?” Hope stirred in my chest. “What is it?” “Next week,” he began, “we will have some visitors at the castle.” “Visitors?” “The king of Vassar.” Peterssen cleared his throat. “And his daughter, Runa.” My heart plummeted.
paras.zh: 正要远走，彼得森却唤我。“安格瑞？”他双脚换着重心，忽然显得紧张。“有……一件事你可以做，好让百姓安心。” “真的？”我心里泛起希望。“是什么？” “下周，”他开口，“宫里要来客人。” “客人？” “瓦萨尔国王。”彼得森清清嗓。“还有他女儿，鲁娜。”我的心直坠。

paras.en: I had hoped that my telling them to do what they wanted had been enough of a non-reaction that it had dissuaded the council from the idea of marriage.
paras.zh: 我本以为，我让他们“随意处理”的冷淡态度，足以打消议会联姻的念头。

paras.en: But evidently, it’d been in the works all this time.
paras.zh: 可显然，这桩事早就在运作。

paras.en: I’d just been too busy with Iduna to notice. “Do you really think now is a good time?” I asked, trying to keep my voice neutral. “I mean, there’s so much unrest.
paras.zh: 只是我忙着和伊杜娜在一处，没留意。“你真觉得现在是好时机？”我问，努力让声音保持平淡，“我是说，眼下这么不安定。

paras.en: People choking, purple sheep…” My voice trailed off as I realized how ridiculous and desperate I sounded. “Oh, so you’re concerned about those sheep now, are you?” Peterssen’s mouth quirked.
paras.zh: 有人喘不上气，羊变紫了……”我意识到自己听来多荒唐多绝望，声音低了下去。“哦，所以你现在是关心那些羊了？”彼得森嘴角一弯。

paras.en: Then he gave me a fatherly smile. “It’s okay, Agnarr,” he assured me. “There’s nothing to be nervous about.” “Who said I was nervous?” I blurted out. “I just don’t need to meet anyone right now!
paras.zh: 接着他露出慈父般的笑。“没事，安格瑞，”他安慰，“没什么好紧张的。” “谁说我紧张了？”我脱口，“我只是现在谁都不想见！

paras.en: I’m only nineteen.” “And soon you will be twenty, then twenty-one.
paras.zh: 我才十九。”“很快你就二十，然后二十一。

paras.en: You’ll be taking the throne, and it’s always better if there is already an heir lined up when that happens.” So not only was I expected to marry this stranger, but I was meant to procreate with her without delay.
paras.zh: 你要继位，而那时若已定好继承人，总归更好。”所以我不只要娶这陌生人，还得立刻与她生儿育女。

paras.en: My stomach swam with nausea. “I don’t get any say in this at all?” I demanded.
paras.zh: 我胃里一阵翻江倒海。“我一点发言权都没有？”我逼问。

paras.en: I knew I was not acting like the heir apparent, but I couldn’t help it.
paras.zh: 我知道自己不似储君该有的样子，却身不由己。

paras.en: I didn’t want to meet anyone.
paras.zh: 我谁都不想见。

paras.en: Not when I already had Iduna.
paras.zh: 尤其当我已经有了伊杜娜。

paras.en: I knew from the start that Iduna and I could never marry.
paras.zh: 我从一开始就知道，我和伊杜娜永不可能成婚。

paras.en: Royalty married royalty—that was how it was always done.
paras.zh: 王室娶王室——向来如此。

paras.en: And with the kingdom of Arendelle still fragile in the wake of my father’s death and Peterssen as regent, this was not the time to buck the trends.
paras.zh: 而父亲过世后，阿伦黛尔仍脆弱，彼得森摄政，此刻绝非破例之时。

paras.en: We needed trade partners.
paras.zh: 我们需要贸易伙伴。

paras.en: We needed allies.
paras.zh: 我们需要盟友。

paras.en: We needed an army.
paras.zh: 我们需要军队。

paras.en: But I needed Iduna.
paras.zh: 可我需要伊杜娜。

paras.en: I hadn’t meant to fall in love with her.
paras.zh: 我本没打算爱上她。

paras.en: But who could blame me?
paras.zh: 可谁能怪我？

paras.en: She was smart, kind, funny, and good.
paras.zh: 她聪明、善良、有趣，又好。

paras.en: She was everything I ever wanted in a partner.
paras.zh: 她是我对伴侣一切期许的模样。

paras.en: A best friend, a true love.
paras.zh: 一位最好的朋友，一位真爱。

paras.en: She made me laugh.
paras.zh: 她逗我笑。

paras.en: She made my heart race.
paras.zh: 她让我心跳加速。

paras.en: Life without Iduna?
paras.zh: 没有伊杜娜的人生？

paras.en: I couldn’t bear the thought.
paras.zh: 我不敢想。

paras.en: Peterssen sighed. “Agnarr, you asked how you could help your people feel safe.
paras.zh: 彼得森叹气。“安格瑞，你问过怎么帮百姓安心。

paras.en: Well, Vassar is well known for its considerable army.
paras.zh: 瓦萨尔以拥兵雄厚闻名。

paras.en: An alliance with them would help us secure our harbors and farmlands.
paras.zh: 与之结盟，能助我们守住港口与农田。

paras.en: Make Arendelle safe.” “I’m fine with an alliance!” I protested. “But can’t we just make it into a trade deal or something?
paras.zh: 让阿伦黛尔安全。” “结盟我完全赞成！”我抗议，“可不能就做成贸易协定什么的？

paras.en: Why does it have to involve marriage?” “Because that’s how it’s done, Agnarr.
paras.zh: 为何非牵扯婚姻？”“因为向来如此，安格瑞。

paras.en: That’s how they can ensure the deal between the two nations sticks.
paras.zh: 这样他们才能确保两国之约牢不可破。

paras.en: No one betrays their own family.” Peterssen walked over and put a hand on my shoulder. “Look, I know this is all scary and new.
paras.zh: 没人会背叛自家人。”彼得森走过来，把手搭我肩上。“听好，我知道这一切又怕又新。

paras.en: But when King Nicholas and his daughter arrive next week, I cannot have you standing there looking like a scared rabbit.
paras.zh: 可下周尼古拉国王和女儿一到，我绝不容你站在那儿像只吓坏的兔子。

paras.en: It will suggest weakness.
paras.zh: 那会显得软弱。

paras.en: And we cannot afford to look weak right now.” “I know.” I groaned. “Conceal, don’t feel.
paras.zh: 而此刻我们输不起软弱。”“我知道。”我哼道。“掩饰，别去感受。

paras.en: Blah, blah, blah.” “Yes.” Peterssen’s gaze drilled into me. “If not for your own sake, then for the sake of your people.
paras.zh: blah, blah, blah。”“对。”彼得森目光紧盯着我。“若不为自己，也为你的百姓。

paras.en: You don’t have “Of course I will,” I broke in, mostly to get the conversation “I always worry about you, Agnarr,” Peterssen said, patting me on the arm. “That is my job.
paras.zh: 你不必——“我当然会，”我打断，多半是为终结这场谈话。“我一直担心你，安格瑞，”彼得森拍拍我胳膊，“那是我的职责。

paras.en: But I also trust you.
paras.zh: 可我也信你。

paras.en: I know you care about Arendelle.
paras.zh: 我知道你在乎阿伦黛尔。

paras.en: And I know you will do the right thing.”
paras.zh: 我知道你会做正确的事。”

paras.en: “AND THESE WILL BE YOUR KEYS, DEAR.” I smiled distractedly as Mrs.
paras.zh: 「亲爱的，这串就是你的钥匙了。」克莉丝滕森太太——一位把自家小屋出租给我的本地妇人——把一串挂在金属小环上的钥匙递过来时，我心不在焉地笑了笑。

paras.en: Christiansen, a local woman who had offered up a cottage for rent, handed me a set of keys strung on a small metal loop.
paras.zh: 克莉丝滕森太太是位本地人，她把一间小屋租给了我，此刻她把一串挂在金属小环上的钥匙递到我手里。

paras.en: As I closed my hand around them, my eyes rose in the direction of the castle on the far side of town, then dropped to the empty street in front of us.
paras.zh: 我握紧钥匙，目光却不由自主地飘向镇子另一头那座城堡，随后又垂落在我们面前空荡荡的街道上。

paras.en: A stirring of disappointment wound through my stomach.
paras.zh: 一股失望之感在胃里蜿蜒升起。

paras.en: Where was Agnarr?
paras.zh: 安格瑞在哪里？

paras.en: He was supposed to be here for this.
paras.zh: 他本该到场陪我一起的。

paras.en: I knew he had a meeting earlier, but he’d promised to be here on time.
paras.zh: 我知道他之前有个会议，可他答应过会准时过来的。

paras.en: He knew how important this was to me. “Iduna?” Mrs.
paras.zh: 他明白这对我有多重要。「伊杜娜？」克莉丝滕森太太——

paras.en: Christiansen frowned. “Aren’t you going to go in?” “Oh.
paras.zh: ——皱起了眉头。「你还不进去吗？」「哦。

paras.en: Sorry.
paras.zh: 抱歉。

paras.en: Yes.” I shook my head, turning to the door of my new place, a cottage just up the hill from Blodget’s Bakery.
paras.zh: 是的。」我摇了摇头，转身面向新家的门——那是间小屋，就在布洛杰特面包房上方的小山坡上。

paras.en: It was only two rooms, but it had a kitchen with a cooking top and an actual ice box for keeping food fresh.
paras.zh: 屋子只有两个房间，但有个带炉灶的厨房，还有一台真正的冰柜用来保鲜食物。

paras.en: Just off the kitchen was a seating area, with a door that led to a cozy bedroom.
paras.zh: 厨房旁边是休息区，一扇门通向舒适的卧室。

paras.en: There was even a patio in the back, big enough to put a chair out on—making it a perfect reading spot.
paras.zh: 后头甚至有个小露台，放把椅子绰绰有余——简直是完美的读书角落。

paras.en: It was simple.
paras.zh: 它很简单。

paras.en: Humble.
paras.zh: 朴素。

paras.en: But it was mine.
paras.zh: 但它是我的。

paras.en: All mine.
paras.zh: 完完全全属于我。

paras.en: After My hand trembled as I slid the key in the lock.
paras.zh: 我把钥匙插进锁孔的瞬间，手微微发抖。

paras.en: I knew I was moving slowly, but hoped Mrs.
paras.zh: 我知道自己动作很慢，只希望克莉丝滕森太太——

paras.en: Christiansen didn’t notice.
paras.zh: ——没有察觉。

paras.en: I just kept hoping Agnarr would appear.
paras.zh: 我只是不断盼着安格瑞能出现。

paras.en: We had planned to do this together.
paras.zh: 我们本说好要一起做这件事的。

paras.en: Step into my new home for the first time, side by side, entering this new life together.
paras.zh: 并肩第一次踏进我的新家，一起开启这段新生活。

paras.en: Where was he?
paras.zh: 他到底在哪儿？

paras.en: The door creaked open.
paras.zh: 门吱呀一声开了。

paras.en: I gave one last glance backward, but the street remained empty.
paras.zh: 我最后回头望了一眼，街上依然空无一人。

paras.en: Sighing, I stepped over the threshold, alone. “So, what do you think?” Mrs.
paras.zh: 我叹了口气，独自跨过门槛。「那么，你觉得怎么样？」克莉丝滕森太太——

paras.en: Christiansen asked, coming in behind me. “It’s a darling place, right?
paras.zh: ——跟在我身后进来说。「这地方挺可爱，对吧？

paras.en: Perfect for a single girl like you.” I flinched at the unintended jab. “It’s wonderful,” I assured her. “Just perfect.” And it was.
paras.zh: 特别适合你这样的单身姑娘。」这句无心的话刺得我缩了一下。「很棒，」我向她保证，「刚刚好。」确实如此。

paras.en: Perfect.
paras.zh: 完美。

paras.en: But also very empty. “Well, rent is due on the fifth of the month.
paras.zh: 但也空荡荡的。「嗯，房租每月五号交。

paras.en: You’re already paid up this month, so I’ll come around in thirty days.
paras.zh: 这个月你已经付过了，所以三十天后我再来。

paras.en: If you have any problems, please don’t hesitate to knock on my door.
paras.zh: 要是遇到什么麻烦，尽管来敲门找我。

paras.en: I’m only three houses down.” She grinned, putting out her hand. “Congratulations, Iduna.
paras.zh: 我就住在往下第三家。」她咧嘴一笑，伸出手。「恭喜你，伊杜娜。

paras.en: This is a big step for you.
paras.zh: 这对你来说是迈出了一大步。

paras.en: You should be very proud.” “I am.
paras.zh: 你应该感到骄傲。」「我确实骄傲。

paras.en: Thank you.” I shook her hand, trying to give her a smile.
paras.zh: 谢谢你。」我和她握了握手，努力挤出一个微笑。

paras.en: We said our goodbyes, and Mrs.
paras.zh: 我们道了别，克莉丝滕森太太——

paras.en: Christiansen headed out, pulling the door shut behind her.
paras.zh: ——走了出去，随手把门带上。

paras.en: Now alone, I looked around the place, poking my head into various cabinets and the closet in the back room.
paras.zh: 现在只剩我一个人，我打量着这间屋子，探头看了看各式橱柜和里屋的壁橱。

paras.en: I tested the bed, bouncing on it a little.
paras.zh: 我试了试床，在上头轻轻蹦了两下。

paras.en: Seemed comfy enough.
paras.zh: 似乎挺舒服的。

paras.en: But still, I felt restless.
paras.zh: 可我还是心神不宁。

paras.en: Unsettled.
paras.zh: 不安。

paras.en: Where was Agnarr?
paras.zh: 安格瑞到底在哪儿？

paras.en: Was he all right?
paras.zh: 他还好吗？

paras.en: What if something had happened to him?
paras.zh: 万一他出了什么事呢？

paras.en: I rose from the bed.
paras.zh: 我从床上起身。

paras.en: I needed to go find out.
paras.zh: 我得去弄清楚。

paras.en: I found him in the secret room.
paras.zh: 我在密室里找到了他。

paras.en: He was sitting in a chair, head in his hands.
paras.zh: 他坐在椅子上，双手抱着头。

paras.en: Hair mussed, eyes wild.
paras.zh: 头发乱蓬蓬的，眼神慌乱。

paras.en: I frowned, concern welling inside me.
paras.zh: 我皱起眉，心里涌起一阵担忧。

paras.en: I’d never seen him look so ill at ease. “Is everything all right?” I asked, worried. “I thought you were going to meet me at the house.” He looked up, his face turning even more pale. “Oh,” he said, rising to his feet. “I’m so sorry.
paras.zh: 我从没见他这样坐立不安。「一切都还好吗？」我担忧地问。「我以为你会在小屋那儿接我呢。」他抬起头，脸色变得更苍白了。「哦，」他站起身说，「真是太对不起了。

paras.en: I totally forgot.” He forgot?
paras.zh: 我完全忘了。」他忘了？

paras.en: This was like the biggest thing to happen to me all year!
paras.zh: 这可是我整年最要紧的一件事啊！

paras.en: Something was definitely wrong.
paras.zh: 肯定是出了什么问题。

paras.en: Agnarr wasn’t the type to just forget. “What’s wrong, Agnarr?” I asked gently. “Whatever it is, you can tell me.” He moaned and began to pace the room, back and forth like a caged wolf, his steps eating up the distance between the walls.
paras.zh: 安格瑞不是那种随随便便就会忘事的人。「怎么了，安格瑞？」我轻声问。「不管是什么，你都可以告诉我。」他呻吟一声，开始在屋里来回踱步，像一头困在笼里的狼，脚步丈量着两面墙之间的距离。

paras.en: His eyes darted to the stone shelves, the table, the floor—anywhere other than my face. “You’re going to hate me,” he said.
paras.zh: 他的目光在石架、桌子、地板间乱瞟——哪儿都看，就是不看我的脸。「你会恨我的，」他说。

paras.en: Wow.
paras.zh: 哇。

paras.en: He hung his head. “There will be visitors to the castle in two weeks.
paras.zh: 他垂下头。「两周后城堡要有客人来了。

paras.en: The king of Vassar.” I was puzzled. “So?” “And his…daughter.
paras.zh: 瓦萨国王。」我一头雾水。「所以呢？」「还有他的……女儿。

paras.en: Runa.” Oh.
paras.zh: 鲁娜。」哦。

paras.en: Agnarr turned to me, his gaze wild. “I tried to tell Peterssen I wasn’t ready.
paras.zh: 安格瑞转向我，目光狂乱。「我试着跟彼得森说，我还没准备好。

paras.en: That this wasn’t the right time!
paras.zh: 现在根本不是时候！

paras.en: But he insisted I at least meet her.” He dragged his fingertips through his hair. “I mean, I guess it’s not a big deal, right?
paras.zh: 可他坚持要我至少见见她。」他用指尖挠了挠头发。「我是说，这应该也不是什么大事，对吧？

paras.en: I meet people every day.” I felt dizzy, a pit forming in my stomach.
paras.zh: 我天天都在见人。」我觉得一阵眩晕，胃里仿佛塌陷出一个坑。

paras.en: But Agnarr was staring at me with such desperation that I found myself nodding along. “Yes,” I said. “You meet people every day.” But we both knew that this wasn’t just any person.
paras.zh: 但安格瑞那样绝望地盯着我，我不由自主地跟着点头。「是的，」我说，「你天天都见人。」可我们心里都清楚，这个人不一样。

paras.en: This was a royal suitor.
paras.zh: 这是一位王室求婚者。

paras.en: A woman the people of Arendelle might desire as a Unlike me.
paras.zh: 一位阿伦黛尔百姓或许会希望成为王后的女子——不像我。

paras.en: An orphan.
paras.zh: 一个孤儿。

paras.en: A nobody.
paras.zh: 一个无名小卒。

paras.en: They may flirt with you and sully your honor, In the end, they only marry their own kind.
paras.zh: 他们也许会和你调情、玷污你的名誉，但到头来，他们只会娶与自己同类的人。

paras.en: I squeezed my eyes shut.
paras.zh: 我紧紧闭上眼睛。

paras.en: This is your own fault, You knew from the start this was wrong.
paras.zh: 这是你自作自受，你从一开始就清楚这不对。

paras.en: That this could never be anything but a flight of fancy.
paras.zh: 这段感情终究不过是一场痴心妄想。

paras.en: There was never any future for you and Agnarr.
paras.zh: 你和安格瑞之间从来就没有未来。

paras.en: You knew that—and yet you chose to indulge in yet another lie.
paras.zh: 你心里明白——却还是纵容自己沉溺于又一个谎言。

paras.en: A lie that you knew would end in heartbreak.
paras.zh: 一个你明知会以心碎收场的谎言。

paras.en: This story was never going to have a happy ending for me.
paras.zh: 这个故事于我而言，注定不会有圆满结局。

paras.en: Agnarr would marry a princess.
paras.zh: 安格瑞会娶一位公主。

paras.en: Father children.
paras.zh: 生儿育女。

paras.en: Raise a family inside these walls while ruling the kingdom outside.
paras.zh: 在城墙内操持家庭，在城墙外治理王国。

paras.en: And I would be forced to watch it all from afar, my heart ripped from my chest.
paras.zh: 而我只能被迫在远处眼睁睁看着这一切，心像被硬生生从胸口掏走。

paras.en: Despite my best efforts, a strangled sob escaped my throat.
paras.zh: 尽管我拼命忍着，一声哽咽还是冲出了喉咙。

paras.en: Agnarr grabbed me, pulling me into his arms in a hold so tight I was half convinced he’d crush me.
paras.zh: 安格瑞一把抱住我，搂得那样紧，我几乎以为他会把我勒碎。

paras.en: But at the same time, I didn’t want him to let me go.
paras.zh: 但与此同时，我又不愿他放开我。

paras.en: I never wanted him to let me go. “Iduna, I love you,” he whispered, his mouth brushing against my ear, sending all-too-familiar tingles all the way to my toes. “I love you more than the stars in the sky.
paras.zh: 我永远都不想他放开我。「伊杜娜，我爱你，」他低语，嘴唇擦过我的耳朵，那种再熟悉不过的酥麻感一直窜到脚尖。「我爱你胜过天上的繁星。

paras.en: I love you more than the breath in my body.” “I love you, too,” I replied.
paras.zh: 我爱你胜过我体内的呼吸。」「我也爱你，」我回答。

paras.en: But my voice sounded older than my years.
paras.zh: 但我的声音听起来比实际年龄沧桑。

paras.en: Tired.
paras.zh: 疲惫。

paras.en: He pulled away, cupping my face in his hands.
paras.zh: 他退开些，双手捧住我的脸。

paras.en: His eyes were so green.
paras.zh: 他的眼睛那样碧绿。

paras.en: I could never get enough of them.
paras.zh: 我永远看不够。

paras.en: And yet soon—too soon—I might never see them up close again. “I will figure this out,” he declared. “I am to be king, right?
paras.zh: 然而很快——太快了——我也许再也无法这样近距离望进那双眼。「我会想出办法的，」他坚定地说。「我注定要成为国王，对吧？

paras.en: That has to mean something.
paras.zh: 那总该意味着什么。

paras.en: If I say I won’t marry her, then that should be the end of it.” I nodded slowly.
paras.zh: 如果我说我不娶她，那这事就该到此为止。」我缓缓点头。

paras.en: I knew he was just trying to make me feel better.
paras.zh: 我知道他只是想让我好受些。

paras.en: And besides, I had no strength left to argue. “If you say so.” “I do,” he declared in a fierce voice. “Now come on.
paras.zh: 况且我也再没力气争辩。「你这么说就算数吧。」「算数，」他语气激烈地宣称，「来吧。

paras.en: Let’s go I sighed, his enthusiasm causing an ache to well in my stomach.
paras.zh: 我们走——」我叹了口气，他的热忱让我胃里泛起一阵酸楚。

paras.en: Just an hour before, I’d been so excited to show him.
paras.zh: 仅仅一个小时前，我还那么兴奋地想带他来看。

paras.en: So proud of the little place I’d gotten all by myself.
paras.zh: 为自己独自张罗来的这方小天地那样骄傲。

paras.en: I’d imagined inviting Agnarr over for dinner, cooking on the little stove.
paras.zh: 我曾想象请安格瑞过来吃晚饭，在那小炉子上做饭。

paras.en: Probably burning the fårikål, but he wouldn’t mind.
paras.zh: 多半会把羊肉炖菜烧糊，但他不会介意。

paras.en: He would tell me it was delicious.
paras.zh: 他会说好吃极了。

paras.en: The best he’d ever tasted.
paras.zh: 是他吃过最棒的。

paras.en: But now… “It’s really not that interesting,” I protested weakly. “Just a silly cottage.” “ Your very And I wanted to.
paras.zh: 可现在……「其实真没什么好看的，」我有气无力地推辞，「就是间傻乎乎的小屋。」「可这是你……」而我确实想去。

paras.en: Oh, god, I wanted to. “All right,” I said at last. “We can stop at Blodget’s on the way.
paras.zh: 天哪，我太想去了。「好吧，」我终于开口，「路上我们可以去布洛杰特家停一下。

paras.en: Grab some chocolate.” Agnarr’s grin widened. “You know the way to my heart, Iduna.” If only that were enough….
paras.zh: 买点巧克力。」安格瑞的笑容绽开了。「你最懂怎么走进我心里，伊杜娜。」要是这样就足够就好了……

paras.en: AFTER THAT, WE HARDLY PARTED EACH other’s company.
paras.zh: 从那以后，我们几乎寸步不离。

paras.en: Even without saying the words, we both knew that these days together might be our last.
paras.zh: 虽没说破，我们心里都明白，这些相处的日子或许是我们的最后时光。

paras.en: We’d meet first thing in the morning in our favorite tree.
paras.zh: 每天一早我们就在最爱的那棵树下碰面。

paras.en: We’d say goodbye to one another late at night outside my cottage door.
paras.zh: 深夜才在我小屋门外互相道别。

paras.en: We’d spend hours in the library secret room—our only truly safe haven—wrapped in one another’s arms.
paras.zh: 我们会在图书密室里——那是我们唯一真正安全的避风港——相拥着度过数小时。

paras.en: It was as if we both felt the time slipping through our fingers.
paras.zh: 仿佛我们都感到时光正从指缝间溜走。

paras.en: As if our relationship was like a vacation, with an end date looming, and we were desperate to make the most of the time we had left.
paras.zh: 又仿佛我们的恋情像一场假期，终点日益逼近，而我们拼命想充分利用所剩的时光。

paras.en: We didn’t talk about it, of course.
paras.zh: 我们当然绝口不提。

paras.en: Our conversations stayed light and easy.
paras.zh: 我们的交谈始终保持轻松随意。

paras.en: Both of us danced around the subject of the upcoming royal visit from a certain foreign princess, which, it seemed, the rest of Arendelle was spending all their time preparing for.
paras.zh: 我们都对那位外国公主即将到访的事绕着弯子，而阿伦黛尔上下似乎正把所有时间都花在准备迎接上。

paras.en: Cakes were being made.
paras.zh: 蛋糕在赶制。

paras.en: Ice sculptures designed.
paras.zh: 冰雕在设计。

paras.en: Both great halls scrubbed down within an inch of their lives and colorfully decorated for a royal ball.
paras.zh: 两座大厅被擦洗得锃亮，还挂满彩饰，准备举办王室舞会。

paras.en: I was pretty sure Olina hadn’t left the kitchen in a week and certainly hadn’t gotten any sleep.
paras.zh: 我几乎可以肯定，奥丽娜这一周都没出过厨房，自然也没合过眼。

paras.en: She almost bit our heads off when Agnarr stole a krumkake from a towering pile.
paras.zh: 安格瑞从那摞得老高的库鲁姆蛋糕堆里偷拿一块时，她差点把我们骂个狗血淋头。

paras.en: It was wonderful.
paras.zh: 这一切美妙极了。

paras.en: It was also terrible.
paras.zh: 但也糟透了。

paras.en: And so, so wrong.
paras.zh: 而且，错得离谱。

paras.en: Every day, I told myself that this would be the last.
paras.zh: 每一天，我都对自己说这会是最后一次。

paras.en: That I would cut this all off while I was still able to be the one to do so.
paras.zh: 说我会趁自己还能做主时，把这一切斩断。

paras.en: Before the choice was no longer mine to make.
paras.zh: 在选择的主动权不再属于我之前。

paras.en: But then I’d see Agnarr’s hopeful smile.
paras.zh: 可随后我一看到安格瑞满怀希冀的笑容。

paras.en: Feel his fingers stroking my skin.
paras.zh: 感受到他指尖抚过我的肌肤。

paras.en: And I would once again be powerless to stop any of it.
paras.zh: 便又一次无力阻止任何事的发生。

paras.en: I was already too far gone.
paras.zh: 我早已深陷其中无法自拔。

paras.en: Drowning in love, with no desire to come up for air, even if it meant my doom.
paras.zh: 溺于爱中，不愿浮出水面换口气，哪怕这意味我的毁灭。

paras.en: And my doom it would be.
paras.zh: 而它注定会毁了我。

paras.en: The princess would be here in a week.
paras.zh: 公主一周后就要到了。

paras.en: We were running out of time. “Let’s go on an adventure!” I looked up from my book, across the table at Agnarr, who had been engrossed in a pile of maps he’d found on one of the shelves in the secret room.
paras.zh: 我们没时间了。「我们去冒险吧！」我从书里抬起头，隔着桌子望向安格瑞，他正埋头翻看在密室某个书架上找到的一堆地图。

paras.en: He looked back at me, a mischievous smile on his face. “It’s been way too long,” he added. “I mean, we didn’t even get a chance to travel to the mist this year.
paras.zh: 他回望我，脸上挂着狡黠的笑。「太久了，」他补了一句，「我是说，今年我们连去雾境的机会都没有。

paras.en: How unfair is that?” I nodded.
paras.zh: 多不公平啊。」我点点头。

paras.en: Peterssen had nixed any trips to the mist due to the unusual occurrences in Arendelle.
paras.zh: 因为阿伦黛尔接连发生怪事，彼得森取消了所有去雾境的行程。

paras.en: He said the village was in a state of too much unrest right now for Agnarr to wander far from town.
paras.zh: 他说镇上现在动荡不安，安格瑞不宜远离城镇乱跑。

paras.en: Which meant adventures, in general, were out. “You know Peterssen is never going to let you go,” I reminded him.
paras.zh: 也就是说冒险基本免谈。「你清楚彼得森绝不会放你走，」我提醒他。

paras.en: He scowled. “What he doesn’t know won’t hurt him.” His eyes sparkled. “We can sneak out of town through that secret passageway off of the kitchen.
paras.zh: 他皱起眉。「他不知道的事，就不会害他。」他眼睛一亮。「我们可以从厨房旁的秘密通道溜出城。

paras.en: No one will ever have to know.” “And when they notice we’re gone?” “We’ll be back before they do.
paras.zh: 没人会知道。」「那等他们发现我们不见了呢？」「我们会在他们发现前回来。

paras.en: We’ll just make it a day trip.
paras.zh: 就当是一日游。

paras.en: Not far.” He reached across the table, his eyes pleading. “Come on, Iduna.
paras.zh: 不远。」他隔着桌子伸出手，眼神恳切。「来嘛，伊杜娜。

paras.en: You know you want to.” His enthusiasm was catching.
paras.zh: 你心里明明想去。」他的热忱很有感染力。

paras.en: And I did want to.
paras.zh: 而我确实想去。

paras.en: I loved our adventures.
paras.zh: 我爱我们的冒险。

paras.en: And I knew this one might very well be our last. “Where are you thinking of going?” I asked.
paras.zh: 也知道这趟很可能就是我们的最后一场。「你想去哪儿？」我问。

paras.en: Agnarr grinned, knowing he’d gotten his way.
paras.zh: 安格瑞咧嘴一笑，知道自己得逞了。

paras.en: He swept his hand over the stack of maps. “Your choice!
paras.zh: 他用手一扫那叠地图。「你挑！

paras.en: Pick a map, Iduna.
paras.zh: 选一张地图，伊杜娜。

paras.en: Any map.
paras.zh: 随便哪张都行。

paras.en: We’ll follow it to the end.
paras.zh: 我们一路跟到尽头。

paras.en: See what we’ll find.” “All right,” I teased, making a big show of closing my eyes and waving my hands over the pile. “But if I randomly pick the map to the World’s Largest Ball of Yarn, we’re still going.” “I couldn’t think of a better destination,” Agnarr declared. “Now pick already!” “All right, all right.” I reached down to the table and grabbed a map at random, digging deep into the pile.
paras.zh: 看看能发现什么。」「行，」我打趣着，夸张地闭上眼，在地图堆上挥了挥手。「可要是我随手抽到『世界最大毛线球』地图，我们也得去哦。」「我想不出更好的目的地了，」安格瑞宣称，「快抽啊！」「好好好。」我伸手到桌上，从堆底胡乱抓了一张。

paras.en: Then I opened my eyes and looked at it.
paras.zh: 然后我睁开眼，看了看它。

paras.en: The map was of the mountains just outside of Arendelle.
paras.zh: 那是张阿伦黛尔城外群山的地图。

paras.en: And someone had drawn a pathway through, leading to a small valley nestled between two large mountains. “‘The Valley of the Living Rock,’” I read.
paras.zh: 有人画了条穿过群山的路，通向两座大山之间一处幽静的小山谷。「『活石山谷』，」我念道。

paras.en: Then I looked up at Agnarr. “Well, it beats the World’s Largest Ball of Yarn.
paras.zh: 接着我抬头看安格瑞。「嗯，总比世界最大毛线球强。

paras.en: Though I’m not sure by how much—” To my surprise, Agnarr suddenly grabbed the map, turning it over in his hands.
paras.zh: 虽然我也说不好强多少——」出乎我意料，安格瑞突然一把抓过地图，在手里翻看。

paras.en: His mouth dipped to a frown, his eyebrows furrowed. “What’s wrong?” I asked. “Were you holding out for the ball of yarn?
paras.zh: 他嘴角一沉，皱起眉头。「怎么了？」我问。「你其实是想要毛线球吗？

paras.en: ’Cause truthfully, I’m not exactly sure if that really—” Agnarr planted his finger on the map, pointing to some writing in the corner I hadn’t noticed before.
paras.zh: 说实话，我也不确定那地方到底——」安格瑞把手指按在地图上，指向角落里我先前没注意到的一行字。

paras.en: It was in a language I couldn’t read.
paras.zh: 那是一种我读不懂的文字。

paras.en: I cocked my head. “Can you read it?” I asked. “No.” He shook his head. “But I recognize the handwriting.” His voice had a tremble to it that made me suddenly uneasy. “You do?” “It’s my mother’s,” he said softly. “I’ve seen it on other papers in this room.
paras.zh: 我偏了偏头。「你能读懂吗？」我问。「不能。」他摇摇头。「但我认得这笔迹。」他的声音带着一丝颤抖，让我骤然不安。「你认得？」「是我母亲的，」他轻声说，「这屋里别的纸上我也见过。

paras.en: My father must have brought all her things here, after she disappeared.” I could hear the bitterness in his voice as he spoke.
paras.zh: 母亲失踪后，父亲一定把她的东西都搬来了这里。」我听得出他话里的苦涩。

paras.en: Especially on the word disappeared Suddenly I really wished I had found the ball of yarn map instead. “We can pick another one.
paras.zh: 尤其是念到「失踪」二字时。突然间，我真希望当初抽到的是毛线球地图。「我们可以换一张。

paras.en: It’s no big deal,” I tried. “No.” He shook his head fiercely. “This is the one.” He rose from his seat, rolling the map in his hands.
paras.zh: 这没什么大不了的，」我试着说。「不。」他用力摇头。「就这张。」他从座位上起身，把地图在手里卷起来。

paras.en: I could see the pain on his face, but also a sudden spark of what looked like hope.
paras.zh: 我看得见他脸上的痛楚，但也瞥见一抹乍现的、像是希望的光芒。

paras.en: And suddenly I knew what he was thinking.
paras.zh: 突然间，我明白他在想什么。

paras.en: What if we followed this map and found something at the end of it?
paras.zh: 如果我们循着这张地图，在尽头找到些什么呢？

paras.en: What if we found out about his mother and the reason she had vanished so many years ago…?
paras.zh: 如果我们查出他母亲的事，以及她多年前消失的原因……？

paras.en: BEFORE DAWN THE NEXT MORNING, WHILE everyone was still asleep, we slipped out of Arendelle miraculously unseen.
paras.zh: 次日天亮前，趁所有人都还在睡梦中，我们奇迹般神不知鬼不觉地溜出了阿伦黛尔。

paras.en: The air was crisp and cool as we crossed the bridge in a shroud of darkness, excitement prickling our skin.
paras.zh: 我们披着夜色过桥，空气清冽而凉爽，兴奋感在皮肤上刺痒。

paras.en: Even the horses seemed ready for an adventure, their steps light and prancing as we headed for the hills.
paras.zh: 连马儿都像准备好了去冒险，朝山丘进发时步子轻快蹦跳。

paras.en: Once we reached the hills, Agnarr and I were playful, almost giddy, as we put the real world aside and set off on our journey, buoyed by the sense of carelessness that accompanies doing something reckless.
paras.zh: 一到山丘，安格瑞和我便像孩子般打闹，几乎欣喜若狂，把现实世界抛到脑后踏上旅程，做傻事时那种不顾一切的轻快感托着我们前行。

paras.en: We knew what we were doing was wrong, dangerous, and completely irresponsible.
paras.zh: 我们知道自己在做错事，危险又极不负责任。

paras.en: Especially for a prince.
paras.zh: 对一位王子来说尤其如此。

paras.en: But Agnarr insisted he didn’t care.
paras.zh: 但安格瑞坚持说不在乎。

paras.en: He was sick of playing by other people’s rules.
paras.zh: 他受够了照别人的规矩行事。

paras.en: Living up to other people’s expectations.
paras.zh: 受够了满足别人的期待。

paras.en: He wanted this—he needed And, in a way, I did, too.
paras.zh: 他想要这个——他需要。而在某种意义上，我也是。

paras.en: We followed the map north, deep into the mountains—on a different path from the one that led to the Enchanted Forest and the mist.
paras.zh: 我们循着地图向北，深入群山——走的并非通往魔法森林和雾境的那条路。

paras.en: On the way there, we stopped for a late lunch at a picturesque trading post and sauna, where we warmed up and attempted to haggle over some way As we began to climb higher into the mountains, the journey became more treacherous, with icy roads winding around steep cliffs with sheer drops.
paras.zh: 途中，我们在一个风景如画的贸易站兼桑拿房停下吃迟来的午饭，在那儿暖了暖身，还试着讨价还价……当我们开始往更高处爬，路途变得愈发凶险，冰封的道路绕着悬崖蜿蜒，下方是陡直的深渊。

paras.en: The last stretch of the journey was up a footpath, too narrow for horses.
paras.zh: 旅程最后一段是徒步上山的小径，窄得马儿走不了。

paras.en: We tied them to the trees and headed for it.
paras.zh: 我们把马拴在树上，朝小径走去。

paras.en: When we came to the top, the the sun had disappeared over the horizon, bathing the landscape in dusk, but all we encountered was an empty valley of rocks. “Well, this is certainly less exciting than I had pictured it,” Agnarr joked as he looked around the valley.
paras.zh: 我们爬到顶时，太阳已沉到地平线下，暮色笼罩大地，可我们眼前只有一处空荡荡的碎石山谷。「嗯，这肯定没我想的那么刺激，」安格瑞环顾山谷，打趣道。

paras.en: He glanced down at the map, pursing his lips.
paras.zh: 他低头瞥了眼地图，抿起嘴唇。

paras.en: I could see the disappointment in his eyes as he looked up again.
paras.zh: 他再抬头时，我看得见他眼中的失望。

paras.en: I knew how badly he was hoping for some answer about his mother.
paras.zh: 我知道他多盼望能找到关于母亲的某种答案。

paras.en: But what had he expected?
paras.zh: 可他到底指望什么？

paras.en: For her to be at the end of the map?
paras.zh: 指望母亲就等在地图尽头？

paras.en: Like a treasure, just waiting to be found? “Maybe there was something here once,” I said gently. “Things don’t always stay as they are, you know.” I had been familiar with movement, fluctuation, from a young age.
paras.zh: 像件宝藏，只等被人发现？「也许这里曾经有过什么，」我温和地说，「世事未必一成不变，你懂的。」我从小便熟悉变动与流转。

paras.en: My family had always been wanderers.
paras.zh: 我的族人向来是漂泊者。

paras.en: Constantly on the move, following the paths of the reindeer.
paras.zh: 随驯鹿的踪迹不断迁徙。

paras.en: No map could lead you to the nomadic Northuldra.
paras.zh: 没有任何地图能指引你找到游牧的北地人。

paras.en: No map could lead Agnarr to his mother.
paras.zh: 也没有地图能把安格瑞引向他母亲。

paras.en: Suddenly my ears caught a noise.
paras.zh: 忽然，我耳朵捕捉到一阵声响。

paras.en: I grabbed Agnarr, yanking him back behind a nearby tree, shoving my hand over his mouth to muffle his sound of surprise.
paras.zh: 我一把抓住安格瑞，将他拽到近旁一棵树后，伸手捂住他的嘴，不让他惊呼出声。

paras.en: We watched as a young woman came over the horizon, walking slowly down into the valley from the other side.
paras.zh: 我们看着一名年轻女子从地平线那头走来，缓缓从另一侧走下山谷。

paras.en: Her hair was brown and unbraided.
paras.zh: 她棕色头发，没有编辫。

paras.en: And she was dressed like a Northuldra in a simple undyed robe, cinched at the waist with a colorful belt.
paras.zh: 穿着北地人的式样——一件素色未染的长袍，腰间束着彩带。

paras.en: My heart beat fast.
paras.zh: 我的心怦怦直跳。

paras.en: Could it really be one of my family, escaped from the mist?
paras.zh: 她真会是我的族人，从雾境里逃出来的吗？

paras.en: I didn’t recognize her, but the Agnarr moved my hand so he could speak. “I recognize her,” he whispered. “I think she’s one of the ice harvesters.” My heart sank a little.
paras.zh: 我认不出她，但安格瑞挪开我的手，好开口说话。「我认得她，」他低语，「我想她是采冰人之一。」我的心微微一沉。

paras.en: That made sense.
paras.zh: 这就说得通了。

paras.en: The ice harvesters were nomadic, like the Northuldra.
paras.zh: 采冰人和北地人一样，也是游牧的。

paras.en: They followed the ice throughout the winter season and came to Arendelle every summer with huge blocks that could be used to keep food fresh or could be carved into decorative sculptures for the town squares.
paras.zh: 他们整个冬天追着冰走，每年夏天带着巨大的冰块来到阿伦黛尔，那些冰块既能保鲜食物，也能雕成装饰雕像摆放在镇上广场。

paras.en: The woman stepped into the center of the valley.
paras.zh: 那女子走到山谷中央。

paras.en: She raised her chin and started to sing.
paras.zh: 她扬起下巴，唱起歌来。

paras.en: My heart leapt as my ears caught the clear song rising into the air.
paras.zh: 清亮的歌声升入空中，我的心跳骤然加速。

paras.en: I closed my eyes as the woman continued to sing.
paras.zh: 女子继续唱着，我闭上双眼。

paras.en: Memories flooded through me with each soulful note.
paras.zh: 每一个饱含深情的音符都让我回忆翻涌。

paras.en: While I’d never heard this particular song, I’d heard similar ones growing up with the Northuldra.
paras.zh: 虽从未听过这支特定的歌，但我随北地人长大时听过类似的调子。

paras.en: My mother used to tell me they were gifts to our people from the fairies and elves of the arctic lands.
paras.zh: 母亲曾告诉我，这些是北极之地的仙子与精灵赐予我们族人的礼物。

paras.en: She would sing them to me to help me sleep—her lilting voice, melodic and sweet, lulling me into dreamland, offering a soothing sound in my head.
paras.zh: 她会唱这些歌哄我入睡——她轻快婉转的嗓音，甜美如乐，把我送入梦乡，在脑海里留下安抚的声响。

paras.en: A deep longing rose inside of me. “It’s beautiful,” Agnarr said softly, also seeming caught up in the song. “I’ve never heard anything like—” His words were cut off by a sudden thundering sound.
paras.zh: 我心底升起一股深切的渴望。「真美，」安格瑞也轻声说，似乎同样沉醉在歌里。「我从没听过像——」突然一声雷鸣般的巨响打断了他。

paras.en: Like rocks rolling downhill.
paras.zh: 像是石头滚下山坡。

paras.en: The woman’s singing stopped.
paras.zh: 女子的歌声停了。

paras.en: Curious, I peeked out from behind the tree again.
paras.zh: 我好奇地又从树后探出头。

paras.en: And I realized the rocks were moving Like actually moving. “Whoa!” I whispered in awe as big and small boulders rolled down the hill, coming to rest at the woman’s feet. “Are you seeing this?” I asked Agnarr.
paras.zh: 我这才发现石头在动——真的在动。「哇！」大大小小的卵石滚下山，停在那女子脚边，我敬畏地低语。「你看到没？」我问安格瑞。

paras.en: He nodded. “Is it magic?” he whispered.
paras.zh: 他点点头。「这是魔法吗？」他低声问。

paras.en: I glanced over at him, wondering if it would be a problem if it was.
paras.zh: 我瞥了他一眼，想着如果是魔法会不会有麻烦。

paras.en: But I saw only fascination in his eyes, not fear.
paras.zh: 可他眼里只有着迷，没有恐惧。

paras.en: Before I could answer, the rocks suddenly popped open, revealing themselves not to be rocks at all, but rather trolls. “I read about these!” I whispered in excitement. “They were in the book that had the Huldréfolk in it.” “What are they?” Agnarr asked, his eyes not leaving the scene. “I think they’re called trolls,” I replied. “From what I understand they’re the oldest creatures alive.
paras.zh: 我还没来得及回答，石头突然裂开，露出的根本不是石头，而是地精。「我在书里读到过！」我兴奋地低语，「就是那本写胡尔德精灵的书里的。」「它们是什么？」安格瑞问，眼睛死死盯着那一幕。「我想它们叫地精，」我答，「据我所知，它们是世上最古老的生灵。

paras.en: They can live hundreds of years.
paras.zh: 它们能活好几百年。

paras.en: And…this may sound weird, but evidently they’re experts in love.” Agnarr raised an eyebrow. “Okay, that I would not have guessed.” “Shhh,” I said, hushing him. “Something’s happening.” My eyes locked on to the ice harvester, who was now standing in the center of what had become a troll circle and wringing her hands together. “Grand Pabbie,” she said in a trembling voice, “you helped my mother once before.
paras.zh: 而且……听着可能奇怪，但它们显然是爱的专家。」安格瑞挑了挑眉。「这个我可猜不到。」「嘘，」我让他安静，「有情况。」我的目光锁在那名采冰人身上——她此刻站在已围成一圈的地精中央，绞着双手。「皮比，」她用颤抖的声音说，「你以前帮过我母亲一次。

paras.en: Now I need your help as well.” “What is it, my child?” asked the oldest and largest of the trolls. “My Elias died in an ice accident last week,” she replied.
paras.zh: 如今我也需要你的帮助。」「怎么了，孩子？」最年长也最大的那只地精问。「我的埃利亚斯上周死于一场冰上意外，」她答道。

paras.en: A tear slipped down her cheek. “It was sudden.
paras.zh: 一滴泪滑下她的脸颊。「走得太突然。

paras.en: Tragic…” She dropped to her knees, her shoulders racked with sobs.
paras.zh: 太惨了……」她跪倒在地，双肩因啜泣而颤抖。

paras.en: A few of the female trolls rolled up to her to give her comforting hugs and rub her back. “He was my world.
paras.zh: 几只雌性地精滚到她身边，给她安慰的拥抱，轻拍她的背。「他就是我的整个世界。

paras.en: My sun and my stars,” she cried. “I cannot go on without him.” “I am truly sorry to hear this,” the older troll—Grand Pabbie—replied solemnly. “Elias was a good man.
paras.zh: 我的太阳，我的繁星，」她哭道，「没有他我活不下去。」「听到这个，我真的很难过，」年长的地精——皮比——肃然答道，「埃利亚斯是个好人。

paras.en: He did not deserve his fate.” The woman swallowed hard. “A good man.
paras.zh: 他不该落得这样的结局。」女子艰难地咽了口唾沫。「一个好人。

paras.en: And a good husband.” She brought a hand to her stomach. “He would have made a good father, too.
paras.zh: 也是个好丈夫。」她把手放到肚子上。「他也会是个好父亲。

paras.en: Alas, he died before he knew I carried his child inside me.” The female trolls now broke into excited chatter, reaching “It’s a boy!” the eldest female troll crowed. “A big, bouncing baby boy!” The woman’s eyes widened. “You can tell?” “Of course!” said the troll who had made the announcement.
paras.zh: 可惜，他死前还不知道我怀了他的孩子。」雌性地精们顿时兴奋地叽喳起来，凑上前去。「是个男孩！」最年长的雌地精欢呼，「一个结实活泼的小男娃！」女子瞪大了眼。「你们能看出？」「当然！」报信的那只地精说。

paras.en: She had what looked like dandelions growing out of her head. “Bulda knows all when it comes to babies!” “Ooh!
paras.zh: 她头上像是长着蒲公英。「论宝宝的事，布尔达全知道！」「噢！

paras.en: You should name the baby Bulda!” declared another female troll. “It’s such a pretty name.” “Or Pebble!
paras.zh: 你们该给宝宝取名叫布尔达！」另一只雌地精宣称，「这名字多好听。」「或者卵石！

paras.en: I’ve always The woman did not look like she “Don’t listen to them,” Bulda broke in. “Those are all troll names.
paras.zh: 我一向——那女子显然不——「别听她们的，」布尔达插话，「那些都是地精的名字。

paras.en: You need a people name.” She tapped her finger to her stony chin. “What about simply naming him after his father?
paras.zh: 你需要个『人』的名字。」她用手指敲了敲石下巴。「干脆用他父亲的名字命名怎么样？

paras.en: That would be a wonderful tribute and a way to remember him.” The woman struggled to her feet. “Don’t you understand?” Her voice took on a near-hysterical pitch. “That’s why I’m here!
paras.zh: 那会是美好的纪念，也能让人记得他。」女子挣扎着站起来。「你还不明白吗？」她的声音几乎歇斯底里，「这正是我来这儿的目的！

paras.en: I don’t want Grand Pabbie stepped forward with a solemn look on his stony face. “You want to forget,” he said.
paras.zh: 我不要——皮比带着肃穆的神情走上前，石脸上写满郑重。「你想忘记，」他说。

paras.en: It wasn’t a question.
paras.zh: 这不是疑问句。

paras.en: She nodded, tears coursing silently down her cheeks. “I can’t sleep at night.
paras.zh: 她点点头，泪无声地滑落脸颊。「我夜里睡不着。

paras.en: I can’t work during the day.
paras.zh: 白天干不了活。

paras.en: All I can see is him.
paras.zh: 满眼都是他。

paras.en: I can’t bear it anymore!
paras.zh: 我再也受不了了！

paras.en: Please, take the memories from me.
paras.zh: 求你，把那些记忆从我这里拿走。

paras.en: I beg you!” Grand Pabbie motioned for her to kneel before him. “I can do what you ask,” he said. “But it will come at a price.
paras.zh: 我求求你！」皮比示意她跪到自己面前。「我可以照你说的做，」他说，「但这要付出代价。

paras.en: I can make your mind forget.
paras.zh: 我能让你的头脑忘记。

paras.en: But the heart is not so easily changed.
paras.zh: 但心没那么容易改变。

paras.en: You may not remember Elias.
paras.zh: 你也许不记得埃利亚斯了。

paras.en: But you will always feel him in your heart.
paras.zh: 但你心里永远会感觉到他。

paras.en: Like a phantom pain that will never completely go away.
paras.zh: 像一种幻痛，永远无法彻底消散。

paras.en: And you will not know why.” “That’s what I want,” she choked out. “ Anything “Very well,” Grand Pabbie replied solemnly.
paras.zh: 而你不会知道原因。」「这正是我想要的，」她哽咽着说，「什么都——」「好吧，」皮比肃然答道。

paras.en: He lay a hand on her forehead and closed his eyes.
paras.zh: 他把手放在她额上，闭上眼睛。

paras.en: Agnarr and I watched, mesmerized, as the Northern Lights in the sky above her head seemed to change.
paras.zh: 安格瑞和我看得入了迷，她头顶上方的北极光仿佛也变了模样。

paras.en: For a split second I saw an image of a man, tall, strong, carrying an ax, hacking away at a block of ice.
paras.zh: 刹那间，我看见一个高大强壮、扛着斧头劈砍冰块男人的影像。

paras.en: Then, just as quickly as it had appeared, it burst away in a cloud of stardust.
paras.zh: 接着，它来得那样快去得也那样快，在一团星尘中炸散消失。

paras.en: As if it had never been there at all.
paras.zh: 仿佛从未出现过。

paras.en: A moment later, the woman rose unsteadily to her feet.
paras.zh: 片刻后，女子颤巍巍地站起身。

paras.en: She looked dazed.
paras.zh: 她一脸茫然。

paras.en: But the tears, I noticed, had stopped. “What am I doing here?” she asked, sounding perplexed. “You came for a blessing for your baby!” Bulda told her gently. “Remember?” “My…baby?” She stared at Bulda for a moment, then nodded, reaching for her stomach again.
paras.zh: 但我注意到，泪已经停了。「我在这儿干什么？」她困惑地问。「你是来为宝宝求祝福的！」布尔达温柔地告诉她，「记得吗？」「我的……宝宝？」她盯着布尔达看了片刻，点点头，又伸手摸向肚子。

paras.en: She remembered that. “Yes.
paras.zh: 这个她还记得。「是的。

paras.en: You told us his name was Pebble,” added the young troll, winking at her friend.
paras.zh: 你跟我们说叫『卵石』呢，」年轻的地精补了一句，朝同伴眨眨眼。

paras.en: Grand Pabbie steered her away from the women. “You must get back to the ice now,” he instructed. “Your family is waiting for you there.” “My family.” A small smile crossed her face. “Yes.
paras.zh: 皮比把她从女地精们身边引开。「你现在得回冰上去，」他叮嘱，「你的家人在那儿等你呢。」「我的家人。」她脸上掠过一丝微笑。「对。

paras.en: I must get back to my family.” She waved at the trolls. “Thank you for the blessing!” And with that, she disappeared into the night.
paras.zh: 我得回到家人身边。」她朝地精们挥挥手。「谢谢你们的祝福！」说完，她消失在夜色里。

paras.en: The trolls remained, however, hanging out and munching on some nearby mushrooms, chatting among themselves.
paras.zh: 地精们却留了下来，闲荡着嚼起旁边的蘑菇，自顾自聊着天。

paras.en: I turned back to Agnarr. “That was crazy,” I whispered. “I’ve never seen anything like it.” “Magic,” he said slowly. “True magic.” He shook his head. “Good thing the people of Arendelle don’t know about these guys.” I rolled my eyes. “Aksel would probably blame them for his purple sheep.” Agnarr snorted. “Hey, maybe if they meet the trolls, they can stop blaming the Northuldra for everything that goes wrong in town.” I tried not to flinch at his causal joke.
paras.zh: 我转回身面对安格瑞。「太离谱了，」我低语，「我从没见过这种事。」「魔法，」他慢慢说，「真正的魔法。」他摇摇头。「幸好阿伦黛尔人不知道这些家伙的存在。」我翻了个白眼。「阿克塞尔大概会把他的紫羊也赖到他们头上。」安格瑞嗤笑。「嘿，要是他们见见地精，或许就不会把镇上出的一切岔子都怪到北地人身上了。」我努力不对他这随口的玩笑露出怯意。

paras.en: At least he didn’t “I can’t believe the trolls just wiped her memory like that,” I said, mostly to change the subject. “Or that she wanted them to!
paras.zh: 至少他没——「我真不敢信地精就这么抹掉了她的记忆，」我说，多半是为了岔开话题，「更不敢信她自己竟要求他们这么做！

paras.en: Who would want their memories wiped?” Agnarr opened his mouth, then clamped it shut again, his face going stark white.
paras.zh: 谁会想让人抹掉自己的记忆？」安格瑞张开嘴，又猛地闭上，脸色变得煞白。

paras.en: I frowned. “What’s wrong?” “You don’t think…” His voice trailed off.
paras.zh: 我皱眉。「怎么了？」「你该不会以为……」他的声音低得没了下文。

paras.en: But I realized exactly what he was thinking.
paras.zh: 可我清楚地知道他在想什么。

paras.en: The map we’d followed had belonged to his mother.
paras.zh: 我们循着的地图曾属于他母亲。

paras.en: That meant she probably knew about the trolls.
paras.zh: 这意味着她大概知道地精的存在。

paras.en: Maybe she had come here, too, before she vanished.
paras.zh: 或许她消失前也曾来过这里。

paras.en: Maybe she’d had a similar request.
paras.zh: 或许她也曾提出类似的请求。

paras.en: To forget her life in Arendelle.
paras.zh: 要忘掉她在阿伦黛尔的生活。

paras.en: To forget her husband and son. “Come on!” I urged Agnarr, grabbing his hand. “Let’s go talk to them.” “What?
paras.zh: 要忘掉她的丈夫和儿子。「走！」我抓住安格瑞的手催促，「我们去跟他们谈谈。」「什么？

paras.en: No!” he cried, alarmed. “We can’t!” “Why not?” “They could be dangerous.” I glanced over at the trolls.
paras.zh: 不行！」他惊慌地叫，「我们不能去！」「为什么不行？」「他们可能很危险。」我朝地精那边瞥了一眼。

paras.en: Two of them were playing a game by rolling round stones.
paras.zh: 其中两只正滚着圆石头玩游戏。

paras.en: Another was rocking a little troll baby.
paras.zh: 另一只正摇晃着一只小地精宝宝。

paras.en: I looked back at Agnarr with one eyebrow raised.
paras.zh: 我挑起眉毛，回看安格瑞。

paras.en: Agnarr let out a frustrated breath. “Fine,” he said. “Let’s go meet some trolls.” We emerged from behind the tree and made our way down into the valley.
paras.zh: 安格瑞泄出一口闷气。「行吧，」他说，「我们去会会地精。」我们从树后出来，朝山谷下走去。

paras.en: It was starting to get darker, and the crystals around the trolls’ necks had begun to glow.
paras.zh: 天色渐暗，地精脖子上的水晶开始发光。

paras.en: Hearing us, they looked up.
paras.zh: 听见我们，它们抬起头。

paras.en: For a moment they just stared as we stared back, an uncomfortable silence growing between us.
paras.zh: 有那么一刻，我们就这么对望着，彼此间弥漫着一阵尴尬的沉默。

paras.en: But then Grand Pabbie stepped forward. “Your Majesties,” he said with a reverential bow. “I didn’t expect to see you here so soon.”
paras.zh: 但随后皮比走上前。「陛下，」他恭敬地鞠了一躬，「没想到这么快又见到二位。」

paras.en: I STARED AT THE ELDER TROLL, CONFUSION swirling through me.
paras.zh: 我盯着这只年长的地精，满心困惑。

paras.en: How could he possibly have been expecting us?
paras.zh: 他怎么会料到我们会来？

paras.en: Was this more magic? “I—I think there must be some mistake,” Agnarr stammered.
paras.zh: 又是魔法作祟？「我——我想一定是弄错了，」安格瑞结巴道。

paras.en: Grand Pabbie pressed his stone lips together. “Are you not King Agnarr?” “Well, I’m Agnarr.
paras.zh: 皮比抿紧石嘴唇。「你不是安格瑞国王吗？」「嗯，我是安格瑞。

paras.en: Technically I’m not king yet.
paras.zh: 严格说我还不是国王。

paras.en: Not till my twenty-first birthday.” “I see.” Grand Pabbie turned to me. “And you, my dear.
paras.zh: 要等到我二十一岁生日。」「我明白了。」皮比转向我。「还有你，亲爱的。

paras.en: Does that make you Princess Iduna?
paras.zh: 那你是伊杜娜公主了？

paras.en: I am not always clear how titles work in your land.” “Just plain Iduna,” I said, drumming my fingers on my thigh. “I’m not royalty at all.” Grand Pabbie nodded solemnly. “You two are not married yet?” I felt my cheeks heat up, and I was able only to shake my head in answer.
paras.zh: 我总搞不清你们那儿的称谓规矩。」「就是普普通通的伊杜娜，」我用手指敲着大腿说，「我根本不是王室的人。」皮比肃然点头。「你们俩还没成婚？」我觉得脸颊发烫，只能摇了摇头作答。

paras.en: This was getting embarrassing.
paras.zh: 这越来越让人难堪了。

paras.en: Grand Pabbie shook his head as though trying to rid himself of a pesky thought. “I am sorry,” he said. “The Northern Lights show me many things.
paras.zh: 皮比摇了摇头，像要甩掉一个挥之不去的念头。「抱歉，」他说，「北极光照给我许多景象。

paras.en: But sometimes they come out of order. “We don’t have a daughter,” I answered, feeling a little annoyed now.
paras.zh: 但有时它们会乱了顺序。「我们可没有女儿，」我答道，这会儿有点恼了。

paras.en: This troll was dangling everything I had ever wanted right in front of me as though it were fact.
paras.zh: 这只地精把我梦寐以求的一切当作既成事实，明晃晃地摆在我面前。

paras.en: Agnarr and I married.
paras.zh: 安格瑞与我结为夫妻。

paras.en: With a little girl.
paras.zh: 还有个小女孩。

paras.en: The vision was so powerful it hurt my stomach.
paras.zh: 这景象如此真切，刺得我胃部生疼。

paras.en: Because I knew it could never come true.
paras.zh: 因为我清楚它永不可能成真。

paras.en: I swallowed hard, but when I spoke, my voice was resolute. “We’re not married.
paras.zh: 我用力咽了口唾沫，开口时声音却很坚定。「我们没结婚。

paras.en: We’re just friends.” The trolls burst out laughing.
paras.zh: 我们只是朋友。」地精们哄堂大笑。

paras.en: I glanced at Agnarr. “What’s so funny?” he demanded, also sounding annoyed. “You two are not just friends,” Bulda proclaimed with a wide, toothy grin. “And if you’re not married yet, well, we can easily fix that, can’t we, ladies?” The female trolls cheered. “We should go,” Agnarr said, grabbing my hand and trying to pull me away.
paras.zh: 我看向安格瑞。「有什么好笑的？」他也恼火地问。「你们俩才不只是朋友，」布尔达咧开大嘴笑着宣称，「既然还没结婚，咱们轻易就能把这事办了，对吧，姐妹们？」雌地精们一阵欢呼。「我们该走了，」安格瑞抓住我的手，想把我拉走。

paras.en: This whole thing was clearly freaking him out. “Come on, Iduna.” But I stood firm, planting my feet.
paras.zh: 整件事显然把他吓坏了。「走吧，伊杜娜。」可我钉在原地，纹丝不动。

paras.en: We’d come this far.
paras.zh: 我们都走到这一步了。

paras.en: And the trolls were strange, maybe, but they didn’t seem evil or malicious.
paras.zh: 地精或许古怪，但看来既不邪恶也无恶意。

paras.en: And if they could help… I looked down at Grand Pabbie. “We’re here to find information about Agnarr’s mother,” I told him. “Do you know if she came here once?
paras.zh: 而且若他们能帮忙……我低头看着皮比。「我们是来打听安格瑞母亲的事的，」我告诉他，「你知道她是否来过这里？

paras.en: Maybe to seek help of some kind?” The trolls all started whispering furiously among themselves.
paras.zh: 也许是来寻某种帮助？」地精们顿时彼此急切地窃窃私语。

paras.en: Agnarr was beginning to look really nervous.
paras.zh: 安格瑞开始显得真的很紧张。

paras.en: I knew he wanted to know but at the same time was petrified of finding out. “This is ridiculous,” he whispered to me. “They clearly don’t know anything.
paras.zh: 我知道他想知道，却又怕知道答案。「这太荒唐了，」他低声对我说，「它们显然什么都不知道。

paras.en: We should—” “Yes,” Grand Pabbie interrupted.
paras.zh: 我们该——」「是的，」皮比打断了他。

paras.en: Agnarr’s face turned pale. “You knew her?” “She came to us many years ago,” he said. “I remember her well.
paras.zh: 安格瑞脸色发白。「你认识她？」「多年前她来过我们这儿，」他说，「我清楚地记得她。

paras.en: She was very sad, your mother.” I could see Agnarr’s hard swallow.
paras.zh: 你的母亲，那时非常悲伤。」我看得见安格瑞艰难地咽了口唾沫。

paras.en: The slight tremble in his legs.
paras.zh: 他的双腿微微发抖。

paras.en: I reached out and slipped my hand into his, trying to give “I do not wish to speak ill of any man,” Grand Pabbie continued. “But suffice to say your mother married out of duty to her kingdom, not for love.
paras.zh: 我伸出手，悄悄握住他的，想给他……「我无意说任何男人的坏话，」皮比继续道，「但简而言之，你母亲出嫁是出于对王国的责任，而非为爱。

paras.en: And the marriage was not a happy one.
paras.zh: 而这桩婚姻并不幸福。

paras.en: And though she loved her baby boy, she could not see the sun through the clouds.
paras.zh: 尽管她爱自己的小男孩，却拨不开云层见不到阳光。

paras.en: She told us she would lie in bed all day crying.
paras.zh: 她告诉我们，她整天躺在床上哭泣。

paras.en: Mourning the life and kingdom she left behind.
paras.zh: 哀悼她抛下的生活与王国。

paras.en: Your father grew impatient at her behavior.
paras.zh: 你父亲对她的模样渐失耐心。

paras.en: He couldn’t understand why she was so sad when he had given her everything she could possibly desire.
paras.zh: 他不明白，自己已给了她一切所欲，她为何还如此悲伤。

paras.en: But there was one thing he could never give her.” “Love,” Bulda whispered to me, cuddling up against my leg.
paras.zh: 但有一件东西他永远给不了她。」「爱，」布尔达贴着我的腿，对我低语。

paras.en: A tear slipped down her stony cheek. “Poor dear was starving for love.” “She struggled with her sadness for years,” Grand Pabbie continued. “But at last she could take it no more.
paras.zh: 一滴泪滑下她石质的脸颊。「可怜的孩子，是爱饿坏了她。」「她与悲伤挣扎了多年，」皮比继续，「但最终再也无法承受。

paras.en: She fled the castle with only the clothes on her back—” “And left her son behind,” Agnarr interrupted, his voice now layered with contempt. “How could a mother do that?
paras.zh: 她只穿着身上衣服逃出城堡——」「却把儿子留在了身后，」安格瑞打断他，声音里添了轻蔑，「一个母亲怎会这样？

paras.en: To her own child!” Grand Pabbie gave him a look. “You must understand.
paras.zh: 对自己的孩子！」皮比看了他一眼。「你必须明白。

paras.en: It was the hardest thing she ever had to do.
paras.zh: 那是她此生最难做的事。

paras.en: Also, the bravest.
paras.zh: 也是最勇敢的。

paras.en: She knew she could not make a life for you outside the castle.
paras.zh: 她清楚，在城堡之外她无法为你谋得安身立命之所。

paras.en: If she took you, they would come after you.
paras.zh: 若她带你走，他们会追捕你。

paras.en: It would likely start a war between her home country and Arendelle.
paras.zh: 很可能引发她故国与阿伦黛尔之间的战争。

paras.en: Many would die.
paras.zh: 许多人会丧命。

paras.en: And your life would hang in the balance.” His eyes met Agnarr’s. “Leaving you behind wasn’t selfish.
paras.zh: 而你的性命也将悬于一线。」他的目光与安格瑞相遇。「把你留下并非自私。

paras.en: In fact, it was the most selfless act she could have chosen.” I felt a lump in my throat, imagining what Agnarr’s mother must have gone through.
paras.zh: 事实上，那是她能做到的最无私之举。」想到安格瑞母亲所经历的，我喉头一紧。

paras.en: How much she must have been hurting to take such drastic measures, and how anguished she must have been at having to leave her only child behind to keep him safe.
paras.zh: 她该有多痛，才会采取如此极端的手段；又该多煎熬，才不得不抛下唯一的孩子以保他平安。

paras.en: I risked a glance at Agnarr.
paras.zh: 我鼓起勇气瞥了安格瑞一眼。

paras.en: His face was still pale.
paras.zh: 他的脸依旧苍白。

paras.en: He’d wanted answers.
paras.zh: 他想要答案。

paras.en: But perhaps not these answers. “So she came here?” I prompted.
paras.zh: 但或许不是这样的答案。「所以她来了这里？」我追问。

paras.en: Grand Pabbie nodded. “She did.
paras.zh: 皮比点点头。「她来了。

paras.en: She knew we had the ability to help her forget.
paras.zh: 她知道我们有能力帮她遗忘。

paras.en: And forgetting was the only way she could He paused, then added, “But before we performed the spell, she had one other request.
paras.zh: 而遗忘是她唯一能……他顿了顿，又道，「但在我们施法前，她还有另一个请求。

paras.en: To see her son, not as he was then, but as he would be.” Grand Pabbie’s eyes zeroed in on Agnarr. “So we searched the Northern Lights for visions of your future.
paras.zh: 想看看她的儿子，不是当时的模样，而是将来的模样。」皮比的目光锁定安格瑞。「于是我们在北极光中搜寻你未来的景象。

paras.en: It is how I knew you would come to us someday.” “But you thought we’d be married,” I reminded him. “With a daughter.” “Two daughters, actually,” Bulda piped up. “Two beautiful little girls.” She closed her eyes and sighed happily.
paras.zh: 正因如此，我才知道你终有一日会来找我们。」「可你以为我们已经结婚了，」我提醒他，「还有个女儿。」「其实是两个女儿，」布尔达插嘴，「两个漂亮的小姑娘。」她闭上眼，幸福地叹了口气。

paras.en: Two “Are you all right?” I whispered. “I know that’s a lot to hear.” “It’s just so awful,” he said, his voice cracking on the words. “To think she was so unhappy.
paras.zh: 两个——「你还好吗？」我低声问，「我知道这信息量很大。」「只是太让人难受了，」他说，声音说到一半就哑了，「想到她曾那么不快乐。

paras.en: And I couldn’t do anything to help her.” Tears welled in my eyes at the pain in his voice. “No.
paras.zh: 而我却什么也帮不了她。」他声音里的痛楚让我眼眶泛泪。「不。

paras.en: You couldn’t.
paras.zh: 你帮不了。

paras.en: You were only a child, Agnarr.
paras.zh: 你那时只是个孩子啊，安格瑞。

paras.en: And also, you can’t make people happy.
